sections.content_zh:
引言

在这本书里，我们呈献给读者们的，是我们对一群最美的村落的研究成果，它们在楠溪江中游。

楠溪江在浙江省东南部的永嘉县，是瓯江最大的、也是最后的一条支流。它的流域夹在括苍山脉和雁荡山脉之间，是一个独立的地理区。由于环境封闭，它也是一个独立的经济区和文化区。

1989年12月初，乍寒天气，胡理琛先生把我们带到了楠溪江，他主管着那儿的规划和建设，对那儿的乡土建筑做过多次调查，写过介绍它们的最初几篇文章。

一到楠溪江，我们又惊又喜。古老的村落使我们感到非常新鲜。村子里既没有深宅大院，也没有飞楼杰阁；既没有琐窗网户，也没有雕梁画栋。然而用蛮石原木建成的房屋是那样朴素真实，自然明朗。村子规划得那样严谨和谐，完整统一。大多数房子是外向的，开敞的，四面开门开窗的。它们需要间隔，因此每幢房子保持了它独立的形体，独立的品格。村子的大部分也因此比较疏朗，房前屋后，竹树浓绿。整个村子的水系、街巷，有条有理。多层级的各种公共建筑物和活动中心分布在各处。渠边塘沿的大石条上，妇女们在洗涤，身边缠着孩子；村头路口的小凉亭里，老人们悠闲地聊天唱戏。生活的画卷展开在公众眼前，走在街上还能隔矮墙见到谁家用石臼打年糕，用木架晾面条。村落的建筑环境连我们这些陌生人都觉得亲切祥和。最出乎我们意外的，是许多村落里居然有公共园林，常常以大片的人工湖为核心，湖面上飘着近树远山的倒影。

等我们了解了楠溪江的文化史，我们再一次感到又惊又喜。原来从东晋以还，历代都有代表当时最高文化水平的学者文人们到这里来任地方长官，来隐居，来游览山水，探访当地的名贤高士，诗文累累，遗迹历历。其中最著名的当然是先后任永嘉太守的王羲之和谢灵运。谢灵运的后裔落籍楠溪江，至今谢氏村落已经将近二十座。我们踏着矴步，渡过清溪，来到幽谷深处的鹤洋村，祠堂里康乐公的神位赫然尚在。村村溪边浣衣女的"鹅兜"，参差成群，人人都说是右军饲养的白鹅变成。穿梭在楠溪江上的紫燕，背上驮着的夕阳还曾照亮过响应文天祥义军的刀枪。这真是一次奇异的感情经历，千余年的文化史，忽然浓缩到眼前，似乎可以触摸。

于是，我们兴致勃勃，初步调查了楠溪江中游的乡土建筑。我们大体认识到：

第一，楠溪江有一些很古老的村落，有记载可查的，如初建于晚唐的茗岙村、下园村和五代的枫林、花坛、苍坡、西巷、周宅等村。建于两宋的就更多了，如芙蓉、廊下、鹤洋、渠口等村建于北宋，豫章、溪口、岩头、蓬溪、塘湾等村建于南宋。

第二，许多村落经过统一的、综合的规划。村子有围墙寨门，墙里有整齐的街巷网和水系，有礼制中心、文化中心、休闲中心和园林绿化等开放空间，有公共的生活设施。有些村落的规划是宋代制定的，至今还局部甚至大部保存着当年的遗迹，如苍坡、塘湾、芙蓉等村。这些村子的规划把建筑环境形成一个完整的生活服务系统。

第三，不少村落里有许多明、清两代的建筑，甚至还可能有宋代的住宅。在一些明、清时代的建筑上，还有在官式建筑中早就没有了的构件和古老的做法，如生起、侧脚、卷杀以及月梁、圆栌斗、层叠的丁头拱和杠杆式地起结构作用的下昂等等，还流行各种减柱造的构架。许多村子里还有不少房子用木柱础，木抱鼓也可以在一些宗祠里见到。

第四，建筑类型很丰富，几乎包括了商品经济发展之前农村里可能有的全部建筑类型，尤其是文化建筑，如书院、读书楼、文昌阁、文峰塔、文庙和一些起教化作用的牌坊、亭阁等等。园林和它的小品建筑也可以算是一种文化建筑。少数水陆交通要道的村落，如枫林、岩头、桐州、廊下、鹤盛等，晚近也出现了一些商业建筑，甚至形成商业街道。

第五，不论是村落的规划还是个别的房屋设计，都表现出楠溪江人发达的环境意识，表现出他们对山川自然的亲切感和审美能力。村落的选址、布局和入口处理，开放空间的配置，一些公共建筑和祭祀建筑典雅清淡的形式，自然景物如山、水的利用，大型园林的开辟，住宅和文化建筑的形制和风格，粗野的天然蛮石和原木的巧妙运用，建筑物身上精致敏感的曲线曲面，等等，都是这种亲切感和审美能力的明证。

第六，楠溪江建筑的风格非常平淡天然，就像它们的原木、蛮石一样平淡天然。庄子说："朴素而天下莫能与之争美"（《天道》），"淡然无极而众美从之"（《刻意》）。楠溪江建筑，美得就像那些纯朴的农民。楠溪江曾经孕育过谢灵运的诗。钟嵘《诗品》说："汤惠休曰：谢诗如芙蓉出水，颜如错彩镂金，颜终身病之。"楠溪江建筑的美，也是"芙蓉出水"的美，比之于有些地区，如皖南的"错彩镂金"的建筑，它是一种境界更高的美。两者风格的差别，就是乡民性格与商贾性格的差别。不但个体建筑如此，村落的整体面貌也如此。

第七，楠溪江大多数村落的布局以及它们的建筑物的形制和风格，社会性的分化还不大。最纯朴自然的民间建筑风格占着绝对的主导地位。大多数建筑物是独立的，保持着自己的形象和个性。除了少数宗祠和"进士第"之类的建筑物外，房屋大多外向开敞，不设防、不拒人，因此造成了整个村落的宽畅爽快，亲切安逸，教人感到乡亲们坦诚的胸怀。它大不同于江南有些地方由内向封闭的院落形成的村落，那里小巷夹在高高的封护墙之间，阴暗而狭窄，个体房屋被连续的高墙吞没，失去了自己的品格。生活场景大多被封闭在院落里，那些小巷里森严的防范性，叫外来人感到压抑不安。

大体得到这些认识之后，我们可以说，楠溪江流域是一个独立的、特点鲜明的建筑文化圈，一个有很高人文意义的建筑文化圈。楠溪江乡土建筑，在我国乡土文化宝库中闪烁着特殊的光辉。

然而，"无可奈何花落去"，近年来农村经济蓬勃繁荣，村民们纷纷营造新屋，于是，大量乡土建筑被拆除。千余年来形成的和谐的建筑环境被破坏，多少高度发达的乡土文化的见证飞快地消失了。我们为新的建设高兴，也为文化遗产的毁灭伤心。

于是我们决心放下从事了几十年的工作，趁楠溪江乡土建筑还没有完全失去之前，对它做一番研究，留下一份资料，聊尽我们对民族文化的赤子之忧。

研究乡土建筑，必须有宽阔的人文视野。虽然搜集一批实例，罗列介绍，也不失为一种方法，但我们希望把工作做得更进一步。一方面，我们打算把乡土建筑本身阐释得更深入；一方面，我们打算把乡土建筑与整个自然和文化环境紧密联系起来阐释。

我们对工作的设想是：

第一，以乡土建筑研究代替一向流行的民居研究。我们不赞成把民居从乡土建筑中割裂出来，单独地研究，更不赞成把民居之外各种类型的乡土建筑类型弃置不顾。乡土建筑的基本单元是一个个完整的聚落，它所包含的各种类型的建筑形成了它的内部结构。我们不可能不分别地研究各种类型的建筑，但力求把它们放在聚落结构的关联中来研究。我们更要研究聚落系统的整体以及它和外部环境的关系，包括环境中的地理、历史、文化、社会等因素。只有以生活圈为单元，全面研究乡土建筑的各种类型，才能阐明人们生活的建筑环境和文化环境的联系。

第二，为了整体地研究乡土建筑，应该以一个个基本的"生活圈"为单元，而不是孤立地研究单栋的房屋。生活圈有相对的独立性，它有比较牢固的、稳定的内部联系和结构，或者是血缘的，或者是地缘的，或者是宗教的、行业的。它有一个或隐或显的凝聚核心，一个或隐或显的边界。在这个生活圈里，乡土建筑大致能自成一个系统。楠溪江的村落在自给自足的自然经济下形成，一个血缘村落就是一个生活圈，所以，我们在楠溪江可以拿有主姓的血缘村落作为研究单元。

第三，我们打算把乡土建筑当做乡土文化的一部分来研究，乡土建筑研究应该是乡土文化研究的一个篇章。这要求突破就建筑论建筑这个流行的狭隘框框，扩大我们的视野，开放我们的思路，发散我们的探索方向。文化的核心是生活模式和相应的价值观。村落和房舍，是生活的环境，生活的舞台，它们与人们的生活发生着千丝万缕的关系，交换着影响。乡土建筑必然反映出乡村生活的模式和相应的价值观。阐释乡土建筑，不能不阐释它和生活的关系，从而阐释它和乡土文化的全面关系。

第四，应该对乡土建筑系统作动态的研究。一是社会、经济、文化发展所引起的村落和房屋的变化，一是材料、技术的发展所引起的。只有在动态中才能清晰地看出生活与作为生活舞台的大建筑环境的相互影响和相互塑型的作用，就是要研究聚落本身的发育过程。这也就是说，要研究乡土建筑运动着的历史。

第五，要采用比较的方法。一切事物的特色存在于它与其他可比事物的比较之中。只有通过比较才能认识事物的特色。我们确定楠溪江是一个建筑文化圈，就是把当地建筑的类型、形制、构造方法、形式、风格和聚落形态等与其他地区的作比较，认识了特点，才得到的结论。在村子内部，把礼制建筑与居住建筑或者某些文化建筑比较，可以看到上层雅言文化与下层民俗文化在建筑风格上的不同表现和相互影响，看出乡土建筑中的社会性分化与对立。用不同发育程度的村落作对比，也能看出它们发育的过程来，例如从只许在家里偏屋做买卖到商业街道的形成过程。把在各种不同地理条件下的村落拿来比较，也会加深我们的认识。

总而言之，我们希望在楠溪江乡土建筑的研究中，采用整体的、联系的、动态的和比较的方法。

但是，条件很困难。几十年来。农村经历了一次又一次激烈的斗争和变化，竟至于使农村里已经没有人全面而系统地知道本乡本土的历史，传统的礼仪、习俗，连宗祠的作用和活动，也不大说得清楚。我们也找不到真正懂得乡土建筑的老木匠。文字资料已经大多散失，幸存下来的宗谱残缺不全，而且本来编纂的水平就不高，体例不严谨，项目不完备。绝大多数村落的规划年代和现存房屋的建造年代已经无法考证。这种情况大大限制了我们的方法的适用性。

对任何一个对象进行的任何一次研究都不可能是完善的，总要留下一些空白和遗憾，那么，请也允许我们留下空白和遗憾罢。

我们这次的楠溪江乡土建筑研究为时一年多。从1990年10月到1991年12月。

楠溪江上游的村子比较贫穷，村落的发育程度低，建筑类型少，规划也不大严谨。下游的村子距温州太近，早就经过改造，失去了乡土特色。所以我们选择了楠溪江中游的村落作为研究对象。研究的重点是岩头、苍坡、芙蓉三个村子，其他还有黄南、岩坦、溪口、鹤洋、蓬溪、东皋、周宅、霞美、溪南、枫林、西岸、下园、上烘头、下烘头、岭下、坦下、渠口、塘湾、豫章、珠岸、桐州、埭头、水云、花坛、廊下等，一共28座村子。

一次研究28座村子，我们的工作面太大了一些，所以不够深入细致，而且生活圈的整体性研究削弱了许多。但是，形势逼人，要做的工作太多，而做工作的人太少，乡土建筑又在一天一天快速地破坏、减少。我们不能精雕细琢，慢慢地干，所以，我们就这样冒失地干了。

1992年春完稿
sections.content_en:
Introduction

In this book, we present to readers the research results of a group of the most beautiful villages — they are in the middle reaches of Nanxi River.

Nanxi River is in Yongjia County, southeastern Zhejiang Province, the largest and last tributary of the Ou River. Its basin, sandwiched between the Kuocang Mountains and Yandang Mountains, is an independent geographical region. Due to its enclosed environment, it is also an independent economic and cultural region.

In early December 1989, in the early cold, Mr. Hu Lichen took us to Nanxi River. He is in charge of planning and construction there, has conducted multiple surveys of local vernacular architecture, and wrote the first few articles introducing them.

Upon arriving at Nanxi River, we were both surprised and delighted. The ancient villages felt very fresh to us. There were no deep mansions, no soaring towers; no lattice windows, no carved beams and painted pillars. Yet houses built of rough stone and raw timber are so simple, authentic, natural and bright. Village planning is so rigorous, harmonious, complete and unified. Most houses are outward-facing, open, with doors and windows on all four sides. They need separation, so each house maintains its independent form and independent character. Most of the village is therefore relatively open, with dense green bamboo and trees around houses. The entire village's water system and streets are orderly. Multi-level public buildings and activity centers are distributed throughout. On large stone slabs by canals and ponds, women wash clothes with children at their sides; in small pavilions at village entrances, elderly people chat and sing opera leisurely. The scroll of life unfolds before the public; walking down the street, one can see over low walls who is pounding New Year cakes in a stone mortar, drying noodles on wooden frames. The village's architectural environment feels warm and peaceful even to us strangers. Most unexpectedly, many villages actually have public gardens, often centered on large artificial lakes, with reflections of nearby trees and distant mountains floating on the surface.

When we learned Nanxi River's cultural history, we were again surprised and delighted. It turns out that since the Eastern Jin dynasty, generations of scholars and literati representing the highest cultural level of their times came here as local officials, as hermits, to tour mountains and waters, visit local worthies, leaving abundant poetry and many relics. The most famous are of course Wang Xizhi and Xie Lingyun, who successively served as Yongjia Prefects. Xie Lingyun's descendants settled in Nanxi River; today there are nearly twenty Xie clan villages. We stepped on stone stepping-stones, crossed clear streams, came to Heyang Village deep in a secluded valley — in the ancestral hall, the spirit tablet of Duke Kangle (Xie Lingyun) is still prominently there. The "goose baskets" of village women washing clothes by streams, clustered in groups, everyone says are transformed from white geese raised by Wang Xizhi (Youjun). Swallows skimming over Nanxi River, the sunset on their backs once illuminated the spears of troops responding to Wen Tianxiang's righteous army. This was truly a strange emotional experience — over a thousand years of cultural history suddenly condensed before our eyes, seemingly touchable.

Thus, enthusiastically, we conducted a preliminary survey of vernacular architecture in middle Nanxi River. We generally recognized:

First, Nanxi River has some very ancient villages. Recorded ones include Ming'ao and Xiayuan villages built in late Tang, and Fenglin, Huatan, Cangpo, Xixiang, Zhouzhai etc. built in Five Dynasties. Many more built in Song dynasty: Furong, Langxia, Heyang, Qukou etc. built in Northern Song; Yuzhang, Xikou, Yantou, Pengxi, Tangwan etc. built in Southern Song.

Second, many villages underwent unified, comprehensive planning. Villages have walls and gates, inside with orderly street networks and water systems, ritual centers, cultural centers, leisure centers and garden greening open spaces, public living facilities. Some village plans were made in Song dynasty, and still partially or largely preserve original remains, such as Cangpo, Tangwan, Furong villages. These villages' planning forms the architectural environment into a complete life-service system.

Third, many villages have many Ming and Qing buildings, possibly even Song residences. On some Ming-Qing buildings, there are components and ancient practices long gone from official-style architecture, such as shengqi (height increase at corners), cejiao (inward tilt), juansha (curved tapering), as well as yueliang (crescent beams), round capitals, layered dingtou brackets, lever-type lower ang that structurally function, etc.; various column-reducing frames are also popular. Many villages have houses using wooden column bases; wooden drum-shaped stone bases can also be seen in some ancestral halls.

Fourth, building types are very rich, almost including all types possible in rural areas before commodity economy developed, especially cultural buildings: academies, study towers, Wenchang pavilions, Wenfeng pagodas, Confucian temples, and some archways and pavilions for moral education. Gardens and their accessory buildings can also be considered a type of cultural architecture. A few villages at land-water transportation hubs, such as Fenglin, Yantou, Tongzhou, Langxia, Hesheng, recently developed some commercial buildings, even forming commercial streets.

Fifth, whether village planning or individual house design, both show Nanxi River people's developed environmental awareness, their intimacy with and aesthetic appreciation of mountains and rivers. Village site selection, layout and entrance treatment, allocation of open spaces, the elegant and austere form of some public and ritual buildings, utilization of natural scenery like mountains and water, creation of large gardens, form and style of residences and cultural buildings, ingenious use of rough natural stone and raw timber, delicate and sensitive curved surfaces on buildings, etc., are all evidence of this intimacy and aesthetic ability.

Sixth, Nanxi River architecture's style is very plain and natural, just like their raw timber and rough stone. Zhuangzi said: "With simplicity, nothing under heaven can compete in beauty" (Way of Heaven), "Infinite tranquility, and all beauties follow" (Deliberate Intent). Nanxi River architecture is as beautiful as those simple farmers. Nanxi River once nurtured Xie Lingyun's poetry. Zhong Rong's "Critique of Poetry" says: "Tang Huixiu said: Xie's poetry is like lotus emerging from water; Yan's is like carved and gilded color; Yan was troubled by this all his life." Nanxi River architecture's beauty is also "lotus emerging from water" beauty — compared to some regions, like southern Anhui's "carved and gilded" architecture, it is a beauty of higher realm. The difference between the two styles is the difference between farmer character and merchant character. Not only individual buildings, but also the overall village appearance.

Seventh, in most Nanxi River villages, the layout and their buildings' form and style show little social differentiation. The simplest, most natural folk architectural style dominates absolutely. Most buildings are independent, maintaining their own image and personality. Except for a few ancestral halls and "Jinshi Mansion" type buildings, houses are mostly outward and open, non-defensive, non-exclusive, thus creating the whole village's spaciousness, warmth and ease, making one feel villagers' frank hearts. This is very different from some Jiangnan villages formed by inward-closed courtyards, where alleys are sandwiched between high enclosing walls, dark and narrow; individual houses are swallowed by continuous high walls, losing their own character. Life scenes are mostly enclosed in courtyards; the stern defensiveness in those alleys makes outsiders feel oppressed and uneasy.

Having generally reached these understandings, we can say: Nanxi River basin is an independent, distinctly characterized architectural cultural circle, an architectural cultural circle of high humanistic significance. Nanxi River vernacular architecture shines with special brilliance in our nation's vernacular cultural treasure house.

However, "helplessly, flowers fall." In recent years, rural economy has boomed, villagers纷纷 build new houses, thus大量 vernacular architecture is demolished. The harmonious architectural environment formed over a thousand years is destroyed; how many highly developed vernacular cultural witnesses are rapidly disappearing. We rejoice at new construction, yet grieve at the destruction of cultural heritage.

Thus we resolved to set aside work we had done for decades, and before Nanxi River vernacular architecture is completely lost, conduct a study of it, leave a record, doing our humble part for our national culture.

Studying vernacular architecture requires a broad humanistic vision. Although collecting examples and listing them is also a valid method, we hope to go further. On one hand, we intend to interpret vernacular architecture itself more deeply; on the other hand, we intend to interpret vernacular architecture in close connection with the entire natural and cultural environment.

Our work设想:

First, replace the popular "dwelling research" with "vernacular architecture research." We do not approve of separating dwellings from vernacular architecture for isolated study, much less ignoring various types of vernacular architecture beyond dwellings. The basic unit of vernacular architecture is a complete settlement; the various building types it contains form its internal structure. We cannot but study each building type separately, but strive to study them in relation to settlement structure. We must further study the settlement system as a whole and its relation to external environment, including geographical, historical, cultural, social factors. Only by taking the "life circle" as unit, comprehensively studying all types of vernacular architecture, can we clarify the connection between people's living architectural environment and cultural environment.

Second, to study vernacular architecture holistically, should take basic "life circles" as units, not isolated individual houses. A life circle has relative independence, relatively firm and stable internal connections and structure — whether kinship, territorial, religious, or occupational. It has one or more implicit or explicit cores, one or more implicit or explicit boundaries. Within this life circle, vernacular architecture roughly forms its own system. Nanxi River villages formed under self-sufficient natural economy; a kinship village is a life circle, so in Nanxi River we can take kinship villages with a dominant surname as research units.

Third, we intend to study vernacular architecture as part of vernacular culture; vernacular architecture research should be a chapter of vernacular culture research. This requires breaking through the popular narrow framework of "architecture for architecture's sake," expanding our vision, opening our thinking,发散 our exploration direction. The core of culture is life patterns and corresponding values. Villages and houses are living environments, stages of life; they have countless connections with people's lives, exchanging influences. Vernacular architecture inevitably reflects rural life patterns and corresponding values. Interpreting vernacular architecture cannot but interpret its relation to life, thereby its comprehensive relation to vernacular culture.

Fourth, should conduct dynamic study of vernacular architecture system. One is changes in villages and houses caused by social, economic, cultural development; another is changes caused by material and technological development. Only in dynamics can one clearly see the mutual influence and mutual shaping between life and the large architectural environment as life's stage — that is, study the settlement's own development process. That is, study the moving history of vernacular architecture.

Fifth, adopt comparative method. The character of all things exists in comparison with other comparable things. Only through comparison can one recognize a thing's character. We determined Nanxi River is an architectural cultural circle by comparing local building types, forms, construction methods, styles and settlement patterns with other regions, recognizing its distinctive features. Within a village, comparing ritual buildings with residences or certain cultural buildings reveals the different expressions and mutual influence of upper-class literate culture and lower-class folk culture in architectural style, showing social differentiation and opposition in vernacular architecture. Comparing villages at different development stages also reveals their development process, e.g., from doing business only in side rooms to formation of commercial streets. Comparing villages under different geographical conditions also deepens our understanding.

In summary, we hope in Nanxi River vernacular architecture research to adopt holistic, connected, dynamic and comparative methods.

However, conditions are very difficult. Over decades, rural areas experienced repeated intense struggles and changes, to the point that no one in the countryside comprehensively and systematically knows local history anymore; traditional rituals and customs, even the function and activities of ancestral halls, are hard to explain clearly. We cannot find old carpenters who truly understand vernacular architecture. Written materials are mostly lost; surviving genealogy are incomplete, and originally compiled at low level, with lax structure and incomplete entries. The planning dates of most villages and construction dates of existing houses can no longer be verified. This situation greatly limits the applicability of our methods.

Any study of any object can never be perfect, always leaving some blanks and regrets — so please allow us to leave blanks and regrets too.

Our Nanxi River vernacular architecture research lasted over one year, from October 1990 to December 1991.

Villages in upper Nanxi River are poorer, with lower development degree, fewer building types, and less rigorous planning. Downstream villages are too close to Wenzhou, long ago transformed, losing vernacular character. So we chose middle Nanxi River villages as research对象. Research focused on Yantou, Cangpo, Furong three villages; others include Huangnan, Yantan, Xikou, Heyang, Pengxi, Donggao, Zhouzhai, Xiamei, Xinan, Fenglin, Xi'an, Xiayuan, Shanghongtou, Xiahongtou, Lingxia, Tanxia, Qukou, Tangwan, Yuzhang, Zhu'an, Tongzhou, Daitou, Shuiyun, Huatan, Langxia, etc. — total 28 villages.

Studying 28 villages at once, our scope was too large, so not thorough and detailed enough, and the holistic study of life circles was weakened. But the situation is pressing — too much work to do, too few people doing it, and vernacular architecture is being destroyed and reduced day by day. We cannot carve carefully and work slowly; so we worked this way, recklessly.

Completed spring 1992

sections.name: 地理环境
sections.content_zh:
1. 地理环境

楠溪江在浙江省东南部，是瓯江下游北侧的最后一条支流。它的干流，由北而南，曲曲折折流经145公里，在今温州市北岸注入瓯江。楠溪江东西两侧支流发达，干流和支流一起，像一棵平躺着的大树，流域面积2472平方公里。这是一个封闭的流域，独立的经济区，范围大致就是现在整个的永嘉县。虽然县治屡经搬迁，辖境也多次调整，但楠溪江流域从唐代以来，一千多年，始终是一个政区，所以它又形成了一个文化区，一个方言区。

永嘉县现在隶属温州市，县治上塘距浙江省会杭州市大约240公里。

楠溪江流域是火山岩丘陵区，上游山峰多有700米以上的，中游往下，山峰多不到500米。整个流域里，有1000米高峰8座。到了下游，两岸是大片平展展的冲积平原。楠溪江汇入瓯江的地方，海拔只有4米。

楠溪江的东面是雁荡山脉，西面是括苍山脉，两山风景绮丽如画。楠溪江流域也是山川灵秀。江水在上游奔腾跌扑，形成瀑布和急湍，把丘陵切割成深谷，雕刻出耸立的危峰险崖。到了中游，它任性地左右摆动，轻轻推开两岸的山峦，河谷宽阔了一点，还串连着大大小小的盆地。沉积滩、牛轭湖、浪花闪耀的浅濑和浓绿透明的深潭，使河流变化出一幅又一幅的图画。峰峦嶂壁的奇险依然，层层叠叠，却谦逊地让澄澈的江水占尽风流，悄悄地侍立在两岸，只把黛色的影子投向水面。清初邑人陈遇春有《楠溪道中》诗：

澄碧浓蓝夹路回，崎岖迢递入岩隈；
人家隔树参差见，野径当山次第开。
乱鸟林间饶舌过，好峰天外掉头来；
莫嫌此地成萧瑟，一纲茅蹊去复回。

楠溪江风景之美，古代就已闻名。东汉末年和三国时代，就有一些求仙问道的人来隐居，其中有梅福。到了刘宋时期，它成了孕育中国第一代山水诗人谢灵运的摇篮之一。稍晚一点，萧梁时期的陶弘景，曾经在楠溪江的大若岩等地修炼。他在《答谢中书书》里描写这里的风光：

山川之美，古来共谈。高峰入云，清流见底，两岸石壁，五色交辉。青林翠竹，四时俱备。晓雾将歇，猿鸟乱鸣，夕日欲颓，沉鳞竞跃。实是欲界之仙都，自康乐以来未复有能与其奇者。

楠溪江流域的地形呈袋状封闭，三面环山，只有南端向瓯江敞开一个口子。介于北纬28度至28.5度之间。北面有山脉挡住冬季的寒风，1月份平均气温8.5℃，极低时-4.2℃，并不很冷。到了夏季，海风循山谷北上，带来好雨，驱走炎热，7月份平均气温29.1℃，极高时40.5℃，也并不很热。年平均气温为18.2℃。年降雨量1698毫米，四季分布不匀。夏秋之交，台风频频袭来，豪雨如注，江水猛涨。决堤的江水和倾盆的大雨常常吞没田畴庐舍，造成灾害。清初康熙年间，豫章村的外宅就被洪水冲走，片瓦不留。但台风带来的暴雨正好能解除常有的伏旱。热季恰逢雨季，温暖加上湿润，楠溪江流域宜于生长亚热带常绿阔叶林。由于地形复杂，土壤种类多，所以植被富有变化。除了山上原生林之外，河滩上长满了人工培植的树木和竹子，郁郁勃勃，成为楠溪江特有的滩林景色。盆地四周的浅山坡上，油桐、油茶、杨梅、板栗、柑橘和柿子，年年结实累累。一到秋季，散落在田野间的乌桕和枫杨，鲜红如火。流域里无霜期长达283天，宜于农业。肥壮的稻麦，从江边一直覆盖到山麓梯田，绿了又黄，黄了又绿，一年可以三熟。

《谷谱》说："温州稻岁两熟"，又引《吴都赋》"国税再熟之稻"，指称就是温州所产。其他如玉米、甘蔗和薏米，也生长得很旺盛。

农业集中在河谷的平川上，那里灌溉便利，土壤肥沃。两侧浅山宜于经济林木。县际的和乡间的道路也多缘江而走，江上又有舟楫之利。因此，富裕的村落大多聚集在楠溪江两岸的谷地里，尤其是比较宽阔的盆地里。楠溪江中游，以岩头村为中心的盆地，是全流域最大的、最富庶的盆地。这里人口稠密，村落星布，比较重要的有港头村、芙蓉村、苍坡村、枫林镇等等。稍小一点的盆地里有溪口村（古名菰田村）、桐州村、五鹈镇、碧莲镇、东皋村、花坛村（花坛）等等。在大小楠溪江的交汇处，有豫章村、坦下（坛下）村、塘湾村（棠湾、棠川）、渠口村（瞿口）等等。田头林梢，时时见到炊烟袅袅，笼罩着参参差差鳞片似的屋顶。几百座散落在楠溪江两岸的村庄，大多是古老的宗族血缘聚落，有杂姓的村子很少，倒往往是一姓数村，联宗合谱，奉祀共同的先祖。这些村子，古貌苍颜，给楠溪江渲染出一层遗世而隐的色彩，像"秦人旧舍"，"不知有汉，无论魏晋"。

这些宁静得近乎停滞的村落，却洋溢着浓郁的人文气息。原来楠溪江的外侧是会稽、婺州和台州。东晋和南宋，中原衣冠两次南渡，文化中心都离楠溪江不远。除了谢灵运、陶弘景曾在楠溪江上徘徊吟诵，王子猷雪夜访戴的剡溪，李清照轻舟填词的双溪，都只和楠溪江隔一道分水岭。那种当时载不动许多国恨家愁的舴艋舟，到现在还在楠溪江上，张着白帆，来来往往。
sections.content_en:
1. Geographical Environment

Nanxi River is in southeastern Zhejiang Province, the last tributary on the north side of the lower Ou River. Its main stream, from north to south, winds 145 kilometers, emptying into the Ou River at the north bank of present-day Wenzhou. Nanxi River's east and west tributaries are well-developed; main stream and tributaries together, like a tree lying flat, drain a basin of 2,472 square kilometers. This is an enclosed basin, an independent economic region, roughly corresponding to present-day entire Yongjia County. Although the county seat has been relocated repeatedly and jurisdiction adjusted many times, the Nanxi River basin has, since Tang dynasty, for over a thousand years, consistently been one administrative district — so it also formed a cultural region, a dialect region.

Yongjia County now belongs to Wenzhou; the county seat Shangtang is about 240 kilometers from Hangzhou, capital of Zhejiang Province.

Nanxi River basin is a volcanic-rock hilly region. Upstream peaks are mostly over 700 meters; downstream, peaks mostly under 500 meters. In the entire basin, there are 8 peaks over 1,000 meters. At the lower reaches, both banks are broad flat alluvial plains. Where Nanxi River joins Ou River, elevation is only 4 meters.

East of Nanxi River is the Yandang mountain range, west is the Kuocang mountain range — both ranges have scenery as beautiful as a painting. Nanxi River basin is also endowed with magnificent mountains and waters. Upstream, the river rushes and plunges, forming waterfalls and rapids, cutting hills into deep valleys, carving out soaring perilous peaks and cliffs. At middle reaches, it swings willfully left and right, gently pushing aside the mountains on both banks; the valley widens somewhat, and is strung with basins large and small. Depositional beaches, oxbow lakes, sparkling shallow rapids and deep green transparent pools make the river change into painting after painting. The precipitous peaks and cliffs remain, layer upon layer, yet humbly let the clear river take the spotlight, standing quietly on both banks, casting only their dark silhouettes onto the water. Early Qing local Chen Yuchun wrote "On the Road in Nanxi":

Clear blue and deep green line the winding road, rugged and distant into rocky recesses;
Houses glimpsed unevenly through trees, wild paths open one by one against the mountain.
Chattering birds pass through the woods, fine peaks turn toward us from beyond the sky;
Do not dislike this place for being desolate — a thatched path winds away and returns.

Nanxi River's scenic beauty was known since ancient times. In late Eastern Han and Three Kingdoms era, some seekers of immortality came to live in seclusion, including Mei Fu. In Liu-Song period, it became one of the cradles nurturing China's first generation of landscape poet Xie Lingyun. A bit later, in Xiao-Liang period, Tao Hongjing once practiced Daoist cultivation at Daluo Rock and other places in Nanxi River. In his "Letter in Reply to Secretary Xie," he described the scenery here:

The beauty of mountains and waters has been discussed since ancient times. High peaks pierce clouds, clear streams reveal the bottom, cliffs on both banks shine with five colors. Green forests and bamboo, present in all four seasons. Morning mist about to lift, monkeys and birds call in confusion; evening sun about to sink, leaping fish compete. Truly a fairyland of the mortal world; since Duke Kangle (Xie Lingyun), no one has again been able to match its wonder.

Nanxi River basin's terrain is pouch-shaped and enclosed, surrounded by mountains on three sides, only the southern end opens toward Ou River. Located between 28° and 28.5° north latitude. Mountains to the north block winter cold winds; January average temperature 8.5°C, extreme low -4.2°C, not very cold. In summer, sea winds blow up valleys, bringing good rain, driving away heat; July average 29.1°C, extreme high 40.5°C, not very hot. Annual average temperature 18.2°C. Annual rainfall 1,698 mm, unevenly distributed across seasons. At summer-autumn transition, typhoons strike frequently, torrential rain, river surges. Breached riverbanks and pouring rain often engulf fields and houses, causing disasters. In early Qing Kangxi era, Yuzhang Village's outer estate was washed away by flood, not a tile left. But typhoon rains正好 relieve the usual summer drought. Hot season coincides with rainy season; warmth plus moisture make Nanxi River basin suitable for subtropical evergreen broadleaf forest. Due to complex terrain and diverse soil types, vegetation varies richly. Besides native forests on mountains, riverbanks are covered with artificially planted trees and bamboo, lush and vigorous, forming Nanxi River's distinctive beach-forest scenery. On low hills around basins, tung oil trees, tea-oil trees, bayberries, chestnuts, tangerines and persimmons bear abundant fruit yearly. Come autumn, tallow trees and Chinese ash scattered in fields turn bright red like fire. The basin has a frost-free period of 283 days, suitable for agriculture. Luxuriant rice and wheat cover from riverbank to mountain terraces, green then yellow, yellow then green — three harvests a year possible.

"Grain Manual" says: "Wenzhou rice ripens twice a year," and cites "Wu Capital Rhapsody": "state tax of double-ripening rice" — referring to Wenzhou produce. Others like corn, sugarcane and coix seed also grow vigorously.

Agriculture concentrates on river valley plains, where irrigation is convenient and soil fertile. Low hills on both sides suit economic forest trees. Inter-county and inter-village roads mostly follow the river; the river also offers boat transport. Therefore, prosperous villages mostly gather in valleys along Nanxi River, especially in wider basins. In middle Nanxi River, the basin centered on Yantou Village is the largest and wealthiest in the entire basin. Here population dense, villages scattered like stars; important ones include Gangtou Village, Furong Village, Cangpo Village, Fenglin Town, etc. In slightly smaller basins are Xikou Village (ancient name Gutian Village), Tongzhou Village, Wuti Town, Bilian Town, Donggao Village, Huatan Village, etc. At the confluence of major and minor Nanxi rivers are Yuzhang Village, Tanxia Village, Tangwan Village, Qukou Village, etc. At field edges and treetops, cooking smoke curls up constantly, shrouding uneven scale-like roofs. Hundreds of villages scattered along Nanxi River are mostly ancient clan kinship settlements; villages with mixed surnames are few, rather often one surname in several villages, united in genealogy, worshipping common ancestors. These villages, with ancient weathered faces, lend Nanxi River a reclusive aura, like "Qin people's old homes," "not knowing of Han, let alone Wei and Jin."

These villages, tranquil to the point of stagnation, yet brim with rich humanistic atmosphere. It turns out outside Nanxi River are Kuaiji, Wuzhou and Taizhou. In Eastern Jin and Southern Song, the Central Plains elite migrated south twice, cultural centers both not far from Nanxi River. Besides Xie Lingyun and Tao Hongjing lingering and chanting by Nanxi River, the Shanxi Creek where Wang Ziyou visited Dai on a snowy night, and Shuangxi where Li Qingzhao wrote ci on a light boat — both are separated from Nanxi River only by a watershed. Those tiny boats that then could not bear so much national grief and family sorrow, still sail on Nanxi River today, white sails, coming and going.

sections.name: 从上古到六朝
sections.content_zh:
2. 从上古到六朝

楠溪江下游的文化史开始得很早，有几处新石器时代的文化遗址，但后来的发展很缓慢。《逸周书·五会解》："正东有沤深，越沤剪发文身。"（王应麟补注：沤深即瓯也，沤亦瓯也）《史记·赵世家》记载："夫剪发文身，错臂左衽，瓯（按：即瓯）越之民也。"可见直到春秋战国，如今的温州、台州一带的"瓯越文化"还很原始，而且与中原文化不属于同一个体系。楠溪江下游的文化，当时就是瓯越文化的一部分。西汉初年，有东瓯国（前192-前138年），在楠溪江口西侧建造了"东瓯王城"。后来在东瓯王领地设回浦县，属会稽郡，一度又改为东瓯乡，隶章安县。章安县县治远在现在的黄岩县章安乡，当时人口之稀少可以想见。东汉时在瓯江北岸建永宁县（138年），仍属会稽郡，三国吴时改属临海郡。虽然传说西汉甘露年间傅隐遥和三国时期王玄贞两位道士曾经在小楠溪的大若岩修炼，道教传入楠溪江中、上游很早（见乾隆《大若岩记》），但直到西晋末年，中、上游的人口大约仍旧很少。

西晋末年，中原大乱，却给东南沿海地区的发展带来了转机。南渡的中原士族，用先进的文化改造了瓯越文化，使它统一于中原的正统文化。楠溪江也开始了新的历史。

东晋明帝太宁元年（323年），设立了永嘉郡，辖地包括今温州和丽水部分地区。从此楠溪江隶属于永嘉。同年，大学问家郭璞为郡城在瓯江南岸选定了地址，规划并且筑城（今温州市鹿城区），显然那时候人口增加，经济有了长足的进步。

中原衣冠渡江偏安，一时人文荟萃江右。初建的永嘉郡，在六朝时竟得了中国文化史上几颗灿烂夺目的星辰来任郡守：先后有东晋大文学家、大书法家王羲之，注《三国志》的刘宋史学家裴松之，刘宋玄言诗人、赋家孙绰，诗人、骈文家、文论家颜延之，中国第一位山水诗人谢灵运和萧梁文学家、骈文高手丘迟。这些当时中国文化的最高代表，"助人伦、成教化"，对永嘉的历史发生了深远的影响。

按照儒家理想，"善政不如善教之得民也。善政，民畏之；善教，民爱之。善政，得民财；善教，得民心"（《孟子·尽心上》）。所以，从东汉以来，地方长官为"师"重于为"吏"，已经成为一个传统。那几位先后守永嘉郡的文人名士，未必服膺儒家，但不能逸出这个传统。乾隆《永嘉县志》转引《旧志》说："晋立郡城，生齿日繁，王右军导之以文教，谢康乐继之，乃知向方。自是家为学，至宋遂称小邹鲁。"又说："王羲之治尚慈惠，谢灵运招士讲学，由是人知向学，民风一变。"

政教之余，谢灵运徜徉流连于山水之间，写下了中国第一批真正的山水诗。其中至少有六首写的是楠溪江风景，而且多在中上游。楠溪江对山水之进入中国文化史起过重要的作用。杜甫《送裴虬尉永嘉》有句"隐吏逢梅福，看山忆谢公"。北宋林逋《送僧机素还东嘉》则说："康乐遗踪地，言归已有期"。永嘉与谢康乐永远连在一起了。

王谢风流，氤氲起楠溪江浓厚的人文气息。明末清初，邑人梅调元有《王谢祠》诗：

前守推王谢，荒祠倚郡城。千秋传墨妙，六代擅诗名。
沼古鹅还浴，塘春草自生。风流今古事，俯仰一含情。

丘迟在《永嘉郡教》里说，永嘉"控山带海，利兼水陆，东南之沃壤，一都之巨会"，则萧梁时永嘉已经比较繁荣。不过，楠溪江流域，从东汉到六朝的古窑址仍然集中在下游，推断起来，中、上游的开发程度大约还很低。
sections.content_en:
2. From Antiquity to the Six Dynasties

The cultural history of lower Nanxi River began very early, with several Neolithic cultural sites, but later development was slow. "Yizhoushu · Wuhui Jie": "Due east there is Oushen, Yue Ou people cut hair and tattoo bodies." (Wang Yinglin supplementary note: Oushen is Ou, Ou is also Ou) "Records of the Grand Historian · Zhao Family" records: "Those who cut hair and tattoo bodies, decorate arms and wear left-lapel garments, are the Ou (i.e., Ou) Yue people." This shows that until Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, the "Ou-Yue culture" in present-day Wenzhou and Taizhou area was still very primitive, and did not belong to the same system as Central Plains culture. Lower Nanxi River culture at that time was part of Ou-Yue culture. In early Western Han, there was the Eastern Ou Kingdom (192-138 BCE), which built the "Eastern Ou King City" on the west side of Nanxi River mouth. Later, Huipu County was established in Eastern Ou King's territory, belonging to Kuaiji Commandery, once changed to Eastern Ou Township, under Zhang'an County. Zhang'an County seat was far in present-day Huangyan County's Zhang'an Township — the sparseness of population at that time can be imagined. In Eastern Han, Yongning County was established on the north bank of Ou River (138 CE), still under Kuaiji Commandery; in Three Kingdoms Wu period, changed to Linhai Commandery. Although legend says Daoists Fu Yinyao in Western Han Ganlu era and Wang Xuanzhen in Three Kingdoms period once practiced Daoist cultivation at Daluo Rock on Minor Nanxi River, and Daoism entered middle-upper Nanxi River very early (see Qianlong "Daluo Rock Record"), until late Western Jin, the population of middle and upper reaches was probably still very small.

In late Western Jin, chaos in the Central Plains brought a turning point for development of the southeast coast. The Central Plains aristocracy who migrated south transformed Ou-Yue culture with advanced culture, unifying it into the Central Plains orthodox culture. Nanxi River also began a new history.

In Eastern Jin Emperor Ming's Taining first year (323 CE), Yongjia Commandery was established, jurisdiction including present-day Wenzhou and parts of Lishui. From then on Nanxi River belonged to Yongjia. In the same year, great scholar Guo Pu selected the site for the commandery city on the south bank of Ou River, planned and built the city (present-day Wenzhou Lucheng District) — obviously population had increased and economy made considerable progress by then.

The Central Plains elite crossed the river and settled in the south, at once talents gathered on the right bank of the Yangtze. The newly established Yongjia Commandery, in the Six Dynasties period, actually got several of the most brilliant stars in Chinese cultural history to serve as commandery governors: successively Eastern Jin great writer and calligrapher Wang Xizhi, Liu-Song historian Pei Songzhi who annotated "Records of the Three Kingdoms," Liu-Song metaphysical poet and rhapsodist Sun Chuo, poet, parallel-prose writer and literary theorist Yan Yanzhi, China's first landscape poet Xie Lingyun, and Xiao-Liang writer and parallel-prose master Qiu Chi. These highest representatives of Chinese culture at that time, "assisting human relations, completing moral education," had profound influence on Yongjia's history.

According to Confucian ideal, "Good government is not as good as good education in winning the people. Good government, the people fear it; good education, the people love it. Good government gains people's wealth; good education gains people's hearts" ("Mencius · Jinxin Shang"). Therefore, since Eastern Han, local officials serving as "teachers" more than "bureaucrats" had become a tradition. those literati who successively governed Yongjia Commandery, may not have embraced Confucianism, but could not escape this tradition. Qianlong "Yongjia County Annals" quoting "Old Annals": "When Jin established commandery city, population grew daily; Wang Youjun (Wang Xizhi) guided with culture and education, Xie Kangle (Xie Lingyun) continued, then people knew the right direction. From then every family studied; by Song dynasty it was called 'Little Zou-Lu'." Also says: "Wang Xizhi governed with kindness and benevolence; Xie Lingyun recruited scholars to lecture; hence people knew to study, local customs changed."

Beyond government and education, Xie Lingyun wandered and lingered among mountains and waters, writing China's first batch of true landscape poetry. At least six of them describe Nanxi River scenery, mostly in middle and upper reaches. Nanxi River played an important role in landscape entering Chinese cultural history. Du Fu's "Sending Pei Qiu to Yongjia as Defender" has lines: "Hermit official meets Mei Fu, watching mountains recalls Lord Xie." Northern Song Lin Bu's "Sending Monk Jisu Back to Dongjia" says: "The land of Duke Kangle's traces, returning already has a date." Yongjia and Xie Kangle are forever linked.

The elegance of Wang and Xie families permeated Nanxi River with rich humanistic atmosphere. Late Ming-early Qing local Mei Diaoyuan wrote "Wang-Xie Shrine":

Former governors praised Wang and Xie, desolate shrine leans by commandery city.
Through ages calligraphy transmitted marvel, six dynasties excelled in poetic fame.
Ancient pond geese still bathe, spring pond grass grows by itself.
Elegance is an ancient and modern matter, looking up and down one embraces emotion.

Qiu Chi in "Yongjia Commandery Proclamation" said Yongjia "controls mountains and borders the sea, benefits from both land and water, fertile land of the southeast, great metropolis of a region" — then in Xiao-Liang period Yongjia was already relatively prosperous. However, in Nanxi River basin, ancient kiln sites from Eastern Han to Six Dynasties still concentrated in lower reaches; inferring, the development degree of middle and upper reaches was probably still very low.

key_terms.en: Assist human relations and complete moral education

sections.name: 从隋唐到宋
sections.content_zh:
3. 从隋唐到宋

隋唐时期，人口继续向楠溪江中上游推进，所以在这地区造了几座佛教寺院，例如岩头村北五鹈溪畔长蛇坑的普安寺，初建于唐玄宗先天壬子(712年)。

隋文帝开皇九年（589年）废永嘉郡，更永宁县为永嘉县。隋炀帝大业元年(605年)又复永嘉郡。以后几经变动，唐太宗贞观元年（627年）再建永嘉县，唐高宗上元元年（674年）设温州，治永嘉。从此经五代、宋、元、明至清一千多年没有大变动，直到如今。

向中、上游开发的人，大多来自外地，为避世乱而寻到这片三面环山的桃源。乾隆《永嘉县志·疆域》引旧《浙江通志》说："楠溪太平险要，扼绝江，绕郡城，东与海会，斗山错立，寇不能入。"环境比较安全，对外地人有吸引力。例如中游芙蓉峰下的下园村，据《下园瞿氏宗谱》记载："晚唐时，黄巢乱，宁波刺史瞿靖避乱来此，鉴于天险奇峰，旷洞清幽，乃定居。"五代末季，各地战乱频繁，独有钱氏吴越境内比较安定。永嘉之南，相去不远的闽国，国君王延钧、王延政于933年和943年先后称帝，父子兄弟交相攻杀，有大批闽人为避乱北迁属于吴越的永嘉，在楠溪江中游建立了许多村落。苍坡、芙蓉、溪口、枫林、花坛、廊下、岩头等中游最重要的几个村子，就是闽人建立的，而且都来自长溪（即福宁州）。这些移民，大多出自仕宦人家，有过功名，凭借他们的文化优势，后人都成了楠溪江的望族，楠溪江人文之盛，主要以这几个村子为代表。

经过这样长期的发展，到了北宋，温州的经济已经相当发达。北宋时候的温州太守杨蟠有诗咏温州："一片繁华海上头，从来唤作小杭州。"（见乾隆《永嘉县志·风俗》）而杭州这时早已是江南繁华胜地，柳永在《望海潮》词中说："东南形胜，江吴都会，钱塘自古繁华。烟柳画桥，风帘翠幕，参差十万人家。"被称为小杭州的温州，当然也颇有可观。到了南宋，温州的农业、手工业和商业飞快进步，一度成为海上商港。

宋代是中国封建文化最辉煌的时期。造成这个文化高潮的原因大致是：士族地主完全消失，庶族地主代之而兴，科举取仕的重要性也大大增加；文官队伍扩大，科举取仕的数量也大大增加。在这样的情况下改革了科举制度，基本杜绝了夤缘奔竞，使平民子弟攀升的机会多了。同时，印刷术发展，书籍普及，也促进了普通人读书博取功名的可能性。因此，温饱的小康之家，大多奔上了科举的道路，从而普遍提高了社会的文化水平。宋朝政府并不采取文化专制政策，学术思想比较自由，学术风气也比较活泼，因而繁荣了上层雅言文化，它的代表就是理学。

楠溪江最灿烂的文化高峰在南宋。宋室偏安江左，又一次大规模的衣冠南渡，把先进的中原文化带到东南沿海。像东晋一样，偏安之地人文荟萃，南宋时来守温州的，如张九成（1042-1159年）、王十朋（1112-1171年）、楼钥（1137-1213年）和杨简（1141-1225年）等人，都是一时的俊彦。他们，以及北宋的温州郡守胡则都很尊重永嘉的人文传统，风流犹存。张九成在他写的《咨目》里说："永嘉道德之乡，贤哲相踵，前辈虽往，风流犹存。"他们作为儒家正统雅言文化的代表，在任地方官吏的时候，也以礼乐教化为第一要务。对于提高永嘉的文化水平起了很大作用。

乾隆《永嘉县志·学校》说："永嘉于宋，名贤辈出，登洛闽之堂者，后先相望，郁郁彬彬，至称为小邹鲁，何其盛哉！"从唐至清，永嘉一共有过604位进士，其中宋代513位，又其中南宋464位。可以确实考订为楠溪江人的，至少有50多位。南宋咸淳元年乙丑（1265年）榜进士中，永嘉籍的有36位之多，占全数的11.4%。其中有芙蓉村的抗元英雄陈虞之和蓬溪村的李时靖，至少这二位是楠溪江人。溪口村戴氏、豫章村胡氏、塘湾村郑氏、花坛村朱氏、苍坡村李氏、芙蓉村陈氏等等，都是"簪缨鹊起，甲第蝉联"的名门望族。苍山碧水之间，田父野老最引为乡土光荣的，是宋朝豫章村胡氏的一门三代五进士、溪口村戴氏的一门四代六进士、花坛村朱氏和塘湾村郑氏的兄弟进士。

科甲盛，当官的就多。据光绪《永嘉县志·人物》统计："自宋以
sections.content_en:
3. From Sui-Tang to Song

In Sui-Tang period, population continued to advance into middle-upper Nanxi River, so several Buddhist temples were built in this area, for example Pu'an Temple at Changshekeng by Wuti Stream north of Yantou Village, first built in Tang Xuanzong Xiantian Renzi year (712 CE).

Sui Wendi Kaihuang ninth year (589 CE) abolished Yongjia Commandery, changed Yongning County to Yongjia County. Sui Yangdi Daye first year (605 CE) restored Yongjia Commandery. After several changes, Tang Taizong Zhenguan first year (627 CE) reestablished Yongjia County; Tang Gaozong Shangyuan first year (674 CE) established Wenzhou, governing Yongjia. From then through Five Dynasties, Song, Yuan, Ming to Qing — over a thousand years no major changes, until today.

People who developed middle and upper reaches mostly came from elsewhere, seeking this mountain-surrounded paradise to escape chaos. Qianlong "Yongjia County Annals · Territory" quoting old "Zhejiang General Annals": "Nanxi is strategically secure, blocks the river, surrounds the commandery city, east meets the sea, mountains interlock, bandits cannot enter." The environment was relatively safe, attractive to outsiders. For example, Xiayuan Village below Furong Peak in middle reaches, according to "Xiayuan Qu Clan Genealogy": "In late Tang, Huang Chao rebellion; Ningbo Prefect Qu Jing fled here, seeing natural peril and strange peaks, spacious caves and quiet clarity, settled here." In late Five Dynasties, wars frequent everywhere, only Qian氏 Wuyue territory relatively stable. South of Yongjia, not far away, the Min Kingdom — kings Wang Yanjun and Wang Yanzheng declared emperors in 933 and 943 respectively, fathers, sons, brothers attacked each other — large numbers of Min people migrated north to Yongjia (belonging to Wuyue) to escape chaos, establishing many villages in middle Nanxi River. Cangpo, Furong, Xikou, Fenglin, Huatan, Langxia, Yantou — the most important middle-reach villages — were established by Min people, all from Changxi (i.e., Funing Prefecture). These immigrants, mostly from official families with scholarly degrees,凭借 their cultural advantage, descendants became prominent clans of Nanxi River; Nanxi River's cultural flourishing is mainly represented by these villages.

After such long development, by Northern Song, Wenzhou's economy was quite developed. Northern Song Wenzhou Governor Yang Pan wrote poetry about Wenzhou: "A stretch of prosperity on the sea, always called Little Hangzhou." (See Qianlong "Yongjia County Annals · Customs") Hangzhou by then was already a prosperous Jiangnan resort; Liu Yong in "Wanghaichao" ci said: "Southeastern strategic spot, Jiang-Wu metropolis, Qiantang prosperous since ancient times. Misty willows and painted bridges, wind curtains and emerald curtains, uneven hundred thousand households." Wenzhou called Little Hangzhou was of course quite impressive. By Southern Song, Wenzhou's agriculture, handicrafts and commerce advanced rapidly, once becoming a maritime trade port.

Song dynasty was the most brilliant period of Chinese feudal culture. Reasons for this cultural高潮 roughly: aristocratic landlords completely disappeared, commoner landlords rose in their place, importance of imperial examination for official selection greatly increased; civil service expanded, number of examination graduates greatly increased. Under these circumstances, examination system was reformed, basically eliminating favoritism and cronyism, giving commoner youths more upward mobility. Meanwhile, printing developed, books普及, also promoting ordinary people's possibility of studying for official degrees. Therefore, well-off middle-class families mostly pursued the examination path, thereby普遍 raising society's cultural level. Song government did not adopt cultural autocracy, academic thought relatively free, academic atmosphere relatively lively, thus flourishing upper-class literate culture, represented by Neo-Confucianism (lixue).

Nanxi River's most brilliant cultural peak was in Southern Song. Song court settled south of the Yangtze, another large-scale migration of elite southward, bringing advanced Central Plains culture to southeast coast. Like Eastern Jin, the settled territory gathered talents; those who governed Wenzhou in Southern Song, such as Zhang Jiucheng (1042-1159), Wang Shipeng (1112-1171), Lou Yue (1137-1213) and Yang Jian (1141-1225), were all outstanding figures of their time. They, and Northern Song Wenzhou Governor Hu Ze, all respected Yongjia's humanistic tradition, its elegance enduring. Zhang Jiucheng wrote in his "Zimu": "Yongjia is a land of morality, sages follow one another, though predecessors gone, elegance endures." As representatives of Confucian orthodox literate culture, when serving as local officials, they also made rites and moral education their first priority. This greatly raised Yongjia's cultural level.

Qianlong "Yongjia County Annals · Schools" says: "Yongjia in Song, famous worthies emerged one after another, those entering Luo-Min (Neo-Confucian) halls followed one another, lush and refined, even called Little Zou-Lu — how prosperous!" From Tang to Qing, Yongjia had altogether 604 jinshi (palace examination graduates), of which 513 in Song, and of those 464 in Southern Song. Those verifiably Nanxi River people number at least 50-plus. In Southern Song Xianchun first year Yichou (1265) jinshi list, Yongjia natives numbered 36, 11.4% of total. Among them were Furong Village's anti-Yuan hero Chen Yuzhi and Pengxi Village's Li Shijing — at least these two were Nanxi River people. Xikou Village Dai clan, Yuzhang Village Hu clan, Tangwan Village Zheng clan, Huatan Village Zhu clan, Cangpo Village Li clan, Furong Village Chen clan, etc., were all "official hats rising like magpies, top degrees repeating" prominent families. Among green mountains and blue waters, what farmers and elders took most local pride in were Song dynasty Yuzhang Village Hu clan's three generations five jinshi, Xikou Village Dai clan's four generations six jinshi, Huatan Village Zhu clan and Tangwan Village Zheng clan's brother jinshi.

With examination success, many became officials. According to Guangxu "Yongjia County Annals · Figures" statistics: "Since Song

sections.name: 元、明、清三朝
sections.content_zh:
4. 元、明、清三朝

楠溪江在南宋这种繁花似锦的盛况，经宋末元兵的大烧杀后不再出现。不过，如《县志》所说："遗风余韵，元明间犹时有闻"，豫章村胡氏、鹤垟村谢氏、岩头村金氏、花坛村朱氏、溪口村戴氏等，在明代还有一些科举功名的成就，出了中书舍人胡宗韫，锦衣卫指挥佥事谢廷循这样比较重要的人物。溪口村戴氏大宗祠有一副楹联是：

宋室尚书第；明廷御史家。

花坛村朱氏大宗祠则有一副楹联：

宋室衣冠龟盖朱幡擢秀；明廷阀阅黄门乌府联芳。

明代前半叶，温州还曾有过两位很有影响的郡守，一位是何文渊，一位是文林。二位都是有著作传世的文士，以"化民成俗"为己任。文林制定《族范》，在温属各县推广，力求强化家族伦理。

嘉靖之后，倭寇侵扰海疆，温州的经济文化大受打击。嘉靖《永嘉县志·城池·都里》中说楠溪江"宋时人物颇盛，今故家遗族，间有存者，视往昔殊矣！"甚至说小楠溪流域"地旷民贫"，为逋逃之薮。

明清易代之际，楠溪江又一次遭到严重破坏。《茗川胡氏大宗祠谱》中写于康熙二年（1663年）的《重建致爱堂记》说，清代初年，由于官兵剿乱，"室庐资产，烧荡一空，而祠宇株连，阖门萧条……垂二十年，鸿雁犹悲鸣于旷野。"《豫章胡氏宗谱》康熙三十四年（1695年）《旧序》说："至清鼎革，变起沧桑，兵燹之余，世家右族不无徙迁，集泽哀鸣，未能常聚。"民力凋惫，赋役不供，文化也就衰败了。南宋时期，一榜进士中不下数十人的永嘉，在整个清代将近三百年间，只有十一名进士，其中还有一名是恩榜。好在康乐公的后裔，鹤垟村谢氏，出了两名进士。《重修鹤垟谢氏宗谱序》（道光三十年，1850年）夸耀这件事说："至今犹想见谢家之门第，即为溪山之生色者，历久弗衰矣！"

楠溪江的历史尽管有荣衰兴替，唐宋以还，村落里的深层生活，毕竟是稳定的日子居多。乡民们在宗法制度之下，有耕有读，几百年间，恒常不变。这种社会生活，和它所伴生的心态，在《岩头金氏宗谱·重修族谱叙》(康熙)》里描绘得很清楚：

安福公墓三岩之胜，家于岩头。贤哲代生，规模宏远。如英六、升四四诸公，开渠筑堤以备旱潦，创谱牒、建宗祠、置祀田以资塋荐，置义田以裕读书。嗣是人文丕振，簪缨继起。……彼汉武玉堂非不贵也，石崇金谷非不富也，吴宫花草、晋代衣冠非不芬芳而赫奕也，然人往风微，徒深感悼，孰若兹之聚族而居，老尔宅，田尔田，涧溪如故，塘堑依然，庙社常新，松楸无恙，士习民风，数百载如一日也乎。

楠溪江的村落，就是这样的社会生活的舞台，显现出宗族关系的强固，生产劳动的艰辛，耕读生活的宁静，以及由此而生的乡愿式自满自足的保守心态。
sections.content_en:
4. Yuan, Ming and Qing Dynasties

Nanxi River's flourishing prosperity in Southern Song, after the great slaughter by Yuan troops at end of Song, never reappeared. However, as "County Annals" says: "Remaining elegance, still occasionally heard in Yuan-Ming period" — Yuzhang Village Hu clan, Heyang Village Xie clan, Yantou Village Jin clan, Huatan Village Zhu clan, Xikou Village Dai clan, etc., still had some examination success in Ming, producing relatively important figures like Zhongshu Sheren Hu Zongyun and Embroidered-Uniform Guard Assistant Commander Xie Tingxun. Xikou Village Dai clan's main ancestral hall has a couplet:

Song dynasty Secretary residence; Ming court Censor family.

Huatan Village Zhu clan's main ancestral hall has a couplet:

Song dynasty official hats and red banners flourish; Ming court prominent families and censor offices share glory.

In first half of Ming, Wenzhou had two influential governors: He Wenyuan and Wen Lin. Both were literati with works传世, taking "transforming people and forming customs" as their mission. Wen Lin formulated "Clan Norms," promoted in all Wenzhou counties, striving to strengthen family ethics.

After Jiajing era, Japanese pirates (wokou) harassed the coast, Wenzhou's economy and culture suffered greatly. Jiajing "Yongjia County Annals · City Walls · Districts" says Nanxi River "Song times had many notable people; now old families and surviving clans, some remain, but far from the past!" Even says Minor Nanxi River basin "land sparse, people poor," a haven for fugitives.

At Ming-Qing transition, Nanxi River again suffered severe destruction. "Mingchuan Hu Clan Main Ancestral Hall Genealogy" contains "Record of Rebuilding Zhi'ai Hall" written in Kangxi second year (1663), saying early Qing, due to government troops suppressing rebellion, "houses and assets burned to nothing, ancestral halls牵连, whole families depressed... for nearly twenty years, wild geese still cry mournfully in the wilderness." "Yuzhang Hu Clan Genealogy" Kangxi thirty-fourth year (1695) "Old Preface" says: "At Qing dynastic change, upheaval like seas and mulberry fields, after war flames, prominent families无不 migrated, gathering in grief, unable to stay together." People's strength exhausted, taxes and corvée unpaid, culture declined. Yongjia, which in Southern Song had no fewer than several dozen jinshi in one examination list, in nearly three hundred years of entire Qing had only eleven jinshi, one of which was even an honorary degree. Fortunately, Duke Kangle's descendants, Heyang Village Xie clan, produced two jinshi. "Preface to Rebuilding Heyang Xie Clan Genealogy" (Daoguang thirtieth year, 1850) boasts: "To this day one can still imagine the Xie family's eminence, which adds luster to streams and mountains, enduring without decline!"

Despite Nanxi River's history of rise and fall, since Tang-Song, the deep life in villages was after all mostly stable days. Villagers under patriarchal clan system, both farming and studying, for hundreds of years, constant and unchanging. This social life, and the accompanying mindset, is clearly depicted in "Yantou Jin Clan Genealogy · Preface to Rebuilding Genealogy" (Kangxi):

Anfu Gong buried at scenic Three Rocks, family settled at Yantou. Sages born generation after generation, scale grand and far-reaching. Like Yingliu, Shengsisi etc., opened canals and built dikes against drought and flood, created genealogy, built ancestral hall, established sacrificial fields for worship, established charity fields for education. Then culture flourished, official hats followed one another. ... Han Wudi's Jade Hall was not unnoble, Shi Chong's Golden Valley was not unwealthy, Wu palace flowers and Jin dynasty official hats were not unfragrant and glorious, yet people gone and wind faded, only causing deep grief — how compare to this clan living together, old your house, farm your fields, streams as before, ponds as ever, temples and altars ever new, pines and cypresses unharmed, scholar habits and folk customs, hundreds of years as one day!

Nanxi River villages are thus stages of social life, manifesting the strength of clan relations, the hardship of productive labor, the tranquility of farming-reading life, and the resulting complacent, self-sufficient conservative mindset.

sections.name: 生产经济
sections.content_zh:
5. 生产经济

关于楠溪江的经济史，几乎没有资料。不过，从仅有的零星资料可见，长期以来，都以自给自足的农业经济为主，工商业受到轻视。《蓬溪谢氏宗谱·赠耕隐公序》里说正德年间的谢朗：

读书尚义士也，怀经济策，寓意于农，遂以耕隐自号。……古之贤士，多出为农，以其业安畎亩，恬静朴茂，非若工与商贾，突骛喧嚣，俯仰尘市，逐十一、较锱铢而不得以宁居也。……故勋业弗成，不如归耕。

这位耕隐公其实是"筑室创业，富望一乡"的人，《序》里写的其实是一种传统的价值观。

农作物首先是稻米、玉米、甘薯、芋艿，然后是络麻、蚕桑。茶叶和柑橘早在唐代就是贡品，柑橘尤其闻名。商品作物也早已有了，如甘蔗、薏米、花生等等。商品中的一大宗是山货，主要的有木材、竹、桐油、笋和板栗等等，还有一些果品和木炭，大多运销温州，这时永嘉县治就在郡城。

大约到了清代中叶，商品经济有了相当规模。光绪《永嘉县志·建置》说，楠溪江"旧用茅竹编筏以通往来，同治三年（1864年），陈令宝善，准民改用梭船，至今称便"，这显然是货运量增大的关系。不过，宋人潘希白《入楠溪》诗里已经写到篷舟，可能同治三年（1864年）前后的变化在于数量的增加。以后航运日益发达，"船过瓯江楠溪开，江上千帆相牵连"，这是《楠溪船歌》里唱的词句。

运输繁忙，有了专业的船老大。《楠溪地名谣》里提到古庙口村和下岸村是船户村，"一篙一桨拼老命，一年到头不停休"。也有了以造船为专业的渔口村。

初级的商品经济，刺激楠溪江沿岸发展了手工业，而且也产生了相应的专业村。例如西岸村出粉干，黄岗村出缸钵，等等。与建筑有关的工匠也有了专业村，如蓬溪村。

商品经济的发展，促进了贫富的分化。明代晚期，高利贷已在楠溪江的村落里出现。《棠川郑氏宗谱》载塘湾村郑世益："精于理财，祖、父无多遗业，翁乃勤俭自持，权其子母，量出入，铢积寸累，握算持筹，不数年而粟陈贯朽，富甲一邑。"

村落的面貌也分化了。在岩头、鹤盛、枫林、东皋、廊下等村落，先是出现了商店，然后在县际大路经过的地方逐渐形成了不长的商业街，最后，终于产生了枫林镇和岩头镇的比较长的、店铺连户的商业街。也有了茶馆和酒楼。

商品经济的发展，引起生活的全面变化。道光、咸丰间永嘉县令汤成烈纂《县志》稿，很生动地描述了这个变化：

永嘉在宋有邹鲁之风，维时士大夫先达者多从二程、朱子游，居乡恒以讲学为业，故能诱掖后进，式化乡间，薰为善良，浸成风俗。户有弦诵，邑无巫觋，人怀忠信，女行贞洁。冠昏丧祭，厚薄适中，奢俭当礼。疾病不祷祈，婚配不听星命，岁时娱乐，弛张合宜，其于养生送死之制，盖秩如也。自元而明，去古渐远，风尚亦漓。轨物废而邪说行，儒术衰而异端起，奁资盛而女溺，宴食腆而讼繁；疾病薄骨肉之亲，报赛侈鬼神之会。昏丧之仪，非复曩制。至于上元灯火，端午竞渡，争奇炫新，靡财奢费，略不顾惜。士女游观，靓妆华服，阘城溢郭，有司莫之能禁。（见光绪《永嘉县志·风土》转引《汤志》稿）

永嘉县，包括楠溪江流域，在明代发生的重大历史性变化，对楠溪江的村落和房屋的影响十分显著。由于宗族力量被削弱，明代晚期以后，村落的大型整体规划没有了，原有的规划格局逐渐被破坏；大家族趋向减少，住宅的规模缩小，兵燹中遭到损害的大宅第不再恢复，残存的也大多被肢解；然而建筑装饰有所增加，出现了华丽的砖墙门；商业建筑萌芽并在交通线旁发展起来；庙宇、宗祠普遍附设戏台，削弱了严肃性，等等。
sections.content_en:
5. Productive Economy

There is almost no资料 on Nanxi River's economic history. However, from the few scattered资料 available, for a long time it was dominated by self-sufficient agricultural economy, with commerce and industry looked down upon. "Pengxi Xie Clan Genealogy · Preface in Honor of Gengyin Gong" says of Xie Lang in Zhengde era:

A scholar who valued righteousness, possessing economic strategies, found meaning in agriculture, thus called himself Gengyin (Farming Hermit). ... Ancient worthies mostly became farmers, because their occupation settled in fields, tranquil and simple, unlike craftsmen and merchants who rush in noise, bow in dusty markets, chase one-tenth profit, haggle over pennies, and cannot live in peace. ... Therefore if merit and achievement cannot be made, better return to farming.

This Gengyin Gong was actually someone who "built houses and established enterprise, wealthy and renowned in the township" — what the Preface writes is actually a traditional value system.

Crops were first rice, corn, sweet potatoes, taro, then jute, silkworm mulberry. Tea and tangerines were tribute goods as early as Tang dynasty, tangerines especially famous. Cash crops also existed early, such as sugarcane, coix seed, peanuts, etc. A major category of goods was mountain products, mainly timber, bamboo, tung oil, bamboo shoots and chestnuts, plus some fruits and charcoal, mostly shipped to Wenzhou — by then Yongjia county seat was in the commandery city.

Around mid-Qing, commodity economy reached considerable scale. Guangxu "Yongjia County Annals · Establishments" says Nanxi River "formerly used bamboo rafts for transport; in Tongzhi third year (1864), Magistrate Chen Baoshan permitted people to switch to shuttle boats, convenient to this day" — obviously due to increased freight volume. However, Song person Pan Xibai's poem "Entering Nanxi" already mentions covered boats; perhaps the change around Tongzhi third year (1864) was in quantity increase. Later shipping increasingly developed: "Boats pass Ou River, Nanxi opens; thousand sails on the river connect one another" — this is from "Nanxi Boat Song."

With busy transport, professional boat captains emerged. "Nanxi Place-name Ballad" mentions Gumiaokou Village and Xia'an Village as boat-owner villages: "One pole one oar, risking old life, year-round without rest." There was also Yukou Village specializing in boat-building.

Primary commodity economy stimulated handicraft development along Nanxi River, and produced corresponding specialized villages. For example, Xi'an Village produced rice noodles, Huanggang Village produced pottery bowls, etc. Craftsmen related to architecture also had specialized villages, such as Pengxi Village.

Development of commodity economy promoted polarization of rich and poor. In late Ming, usury already appeared in Nanxi River villages. "Tangchuan Zheng Clan Genealogy" records Tangwan Village Zheng Shiyi: "Skilled in finance; grandfather and father left little property; he maintained diligence and frugality, calculated interest, measured income and expenditure, accumulated penny by penny, held abacus and counters — within a few years grain stored and coins rotted, wealthiest in the county."

Village appearance also polarized. In Yantou, Hesheng, Fenglin, Donggao, Langxia and other villages, first shops appeared, then along inter-county main roads gradually formed short commercial streets, finally producing the longer, shop-lined commercial streets of Fenglin Town and Yantou Town. Teahouses and wine shops also appeared.

Development of commodity economy caused comprehensive changes in life. During Daoguang-Xianfeng, Yongjia Magistrate Tang Chenglie compiled "County Annals" draft, vividly describing this change:

Yongjia in Song had Zou-Lu (Confucian) ethos; at that time scholar-officials and pioneers mostly associated with the two Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi, living in hometowns constantly engaged in lecturing, thus able to guide later generations, transform countryside, nurture goodness, permeate into customs. Every household had string music and recitation, county had no shamans, people cherished loyalty and trust, women practiced chastity. Capping, marriage, funeral and sacrifice rites — moderate in thickness, appropriate in luxury and frugality. Illness not prayed for, marriage not guided by astrology; seasonal entertainment balanced relaxation and seriousness; systems for nurturing the living and sending off the dead were orderly. From Yuan to Ming, farther from antiquity, customs also deteriorated. Norms abandoned and heresies spread, Confucianism declined and heterodoxies arose; dowries lavish and female infanticide, banquets rich and lawsuits numerous; illness neglects flesh-and-blood kin, sacrificial gatherings extravagantly honor gods. Marriage and funeral rites no longer follow old systems. As for Lantern Festival lights, Dragon Boat boat races — competing in novelty, squandering wealth, without restraint. Men and women sightseeing, in fine makeup and gorgeous clothes, filling cities and suburbs — officials cannot prohibit. (See Guangxu "Yongjia County Annals · Local Customs" quoting "Tang Annals" draft)

Yongjia County, including Nanxi River basin, underwent major historical changes in Ming, with very significant impact on Nanxi River villages and houses. Due to weakened clan power, after late Ming, villages no longer had large-scale overall planning; original planning patterns gradually destroyed; large families tended to decrease, residence scale shrank, large mansions damaged in war no longer restored, surviving ones mostly dismantled; however architectural decoration increased, ornate brick-wall gates appeared; commercial architecture germinated and developed along transportation lines; temples and ancestral halls普遍 attached stages, weakening solemnity, etc.

sections.name: 耕读生活
sections.content_zh:
1. 耕读生活

耕读生活，早期作为士人的一种理想，起源于隐逸，起源于他们儒家的"退则独善其身"和道家的返回自然相结合的人格结构。但到了宋朝，它被科举制度改造并且大大加强了。

科举制度本为遴选官吏而设，它的推行提高了社会普遍的文化水平。宋代扩大了科举录取名额，改善了考试方法，再加上雕版印刷盛行，从而激发了普通人家对科举的兴趣，造成了文化的普及。连农家子弟也看到了眼前可能的机会，于是牛角挂书，参加到举业的竞逐中去，这就形成了农村中新的耕读生活。

（1）科举与文化普及

宋仁宗有几条政策进一步促进了耕读生活的理想。一是规定士子必须在本乡读书应试，因而地方普设各级学校；一是各科进士榜名，给南方诸省规定了优惠的最低配额。更重要的是，工商业者和他们的子弟不得参与科举考试，而只许士、农参加。农家子弟科名机会大大增加，"朝为田舍郎，暮登天子堂"，由春梦成了希望，茅檐下响起了琅琅的书声。

楠溪江流域，耕读理想深入到山陬水涯的每个村落。各个宗族，在《家训》、《族规》里明定，子弟务必要读书。《鹤垟谢氏宗谱·家训》里说，子孙应该"以耕读为业"；《坦下陈氏宗谱·家训》（康熙本）教导："耕以务本，读以明教。"《云岭潘氏宗谱·家训》说得更周全明白："祖宗家法，以忠孝节义为纪纲，以耕读勤俭为本务。"

为子弟读书，各村纷纷兴学。一方面请老师主持义学或义塾，一方面资助贫寒人家子弟入学。例如《岩头金氏宗谱·家规》写道："每岁延敦厚博学之士以教子弟，须重以学俸，隆以礼文，无失故家轨度。子弟有质士堪上进而无力从学者众，当资以祠租曲成之。"各族的祠下大多规定，凡进县学、府学读书和赴府、省应试，费用由祠下公出。中试以后祭祖和各方打点、花销也由宗祠支付，族中有公有的学田，收入全用来兴学。

子弟取得科举功名，是整个宗族的光荣，一律载入宗谱。有功名的人在家族的各种仪典里都享受特殊的光荣。祠堂里的匾额和楹联，除了颂扬先人辉煌的功业之外，就是炫耀族人的举业和仕途。豫章村胡氏大宗祠有一副楹联写的是：

翰墨流芳百世衣冠开砚沼；
诗书继美千秋禋撰焕文章。

《珍川朱氏合族副谱》里有一篇《如在堂记》，把对子弟科名的期望写得很殷切：

使我拥书万卷，何减积粟千锺，然则后之子若孙，苟不忘此意，必将奋志诗书，骧首云逵，上以绳其祖武，下以贻厥孙谋，无忝先世科甲之荣，不振前朝理学之绪，则不惟有光于近祖，亦且善述乎大宗祠矣！

这种耕读理想成了楠溪江人的传统。偏僻闭塞的楠溪江，小小的村落里，文风之盛，科甲成就之辉煌，在全国的乡村里极为少见。道光三十年（1850年）《重修鹤垟谢氏宗谱序》里说"诗书继美，比户可封；游庠之士，指不胜屈"，并不是浮夸的虚言。

文风之兴，由于科举，但文风兴起之后，必定超越科举。《珍川朱氏宗谱·族范盟辞》里说得明白：

不学则夷乎物，学则可以立，故学不亦大乎。学者尽人事所以助乎天也。天设其伦，非学莫能敦；人有恒纪，非学莫能叙。贤者由学以明，不贤者废学以昏。大匠成室，材木盈前，程度去取而不乱者，由绳墨之素定。君子临事而不骇，制度而不扰者，非学安能定其心哉。是故学者君子之绳墨也。

对文化的这种深刻的理解和热烈的追求，给楠溪江深山幽谷里的村庄笼罩上一层浓浓的书卷气。

（2）理学家

文化水平的普遍提高，扩大了知识分子阶层，也就扩大了宋、明以还理学的社会基础，增强了它的影响。

王十朋《送叶秀才序》里说：永嘉"谊礼之学甲于东南，笔横渠、口伊洛者纷如也。取科第、登仕籍，多自此途出。"永嘉人直接求学于程、朱门下的也不少。在国学里，先后有永嘉籍的元丰九先生和淳熙六君子，"俱以道德性命传程朱之学"（见乾隆《永嘉县志·风俗》）。在南宋，还形成了理学的"永嘉学派"，以薛季宣、郑伯熊、陈傅良和叶适为代表。郑伯熊是楠溪江中游塘湾村人。又据《岩头金氏宗谱》记载，叶适童年由岩头村金姓抚养，在岩头村读书，他和楠溪江有亲密的关系。

除郑伯熊和叶适外，楠溪江文士中还有不少理学名家。溪口村戴氏家族，北宋时有戴述（元符三年进士，即1100年）、戴迅二兄弟，从二程学，世称二戴。到南宋，有戴述子栩（嘉定进士），是叶适的学生，著作《五经说》、《诸子辩论》、《东都要略》等；戴迅之子溪（淳熙五年进士，即1178年），"由礼部郎中凡六转为太子詹事，兼秘书监。景献太子命类《易》、《诗》、《书》、《春秋》、《语》、《孟》、《资治通鉴》各为说以进。权工部尚书，除文华阁学士，卒赠端明殿学士，谥文端。太子亲书'明经'扁其堂，有《岷隐集》。"（见嘉靖《温州府志·人物》）溪弟龟年之子蒙（绍熙庚戌进士，即1190年），曾从朱晦庵于武夷，著作有《易、书、四书家说》、《六书故》等；蒙长子仔，不乐仕进，著有《诸经补义》、《通鉴外纪》、《说林文集》等；蒙之次子侗（淳祐辛丑进士，即1241年），著作有《六书设》及其他杂著文集。戴氏大宗祠里有一副楹联写道：

入程朱门迭奏埙篪理学渊源双接绪；
历南北宋并称邹鲁春官第甲六登墀。

夸耀的就是戴氏家族的这份荣誉。

塘湾村郑伯熊三兄弟都是南宋进士。伯熊"德行夙成，尤邃经学。登绍兴第，历官国子司业、宗正少卿。乞外，以龙图阁知宁国府。卒谥文肃。绍兴末，伊洛之学稍息，复于伯熊倡之。弟伯英、伯海皆知名，由是永嘉之学宗郑氏。有《郑景望集》"（嘉靖《温州府志·人物》）。伯英是隆兴癸未（1163年）进士，有《归愚集》。伯海是绍兴辛未（1151年）进士，设帐授徒，生徒常达五百人。

此外，岙底上湾村有陈揆，绍兴癸丑（1133年）与陈亮同榜进士，与叶适相善，有诗集二十馀卷及文集五卷问世。芙蓉村陈宝之，绍兴进士，从吕祖谦学，与陈亮为诗友。宗谱有《送陈同父》和《挽吕东莱》诗各一首。

乾隆《永嘉县志》记载，朱熹在任两浙东路常平盐茶公事的时候，曾经到楠溪江来访问当地的理学家。先到岩头村访问门人"以理学鸣于世"的刘愈，说："过楠溪不识刘进之，如过洞庭不识橘。"不巧没有见到。又到谢岙访问门人谢复经，再访戴蒙、戴侗及蓬溪村李时靖，在蓬溪村留有墨迹。（摩崖石刻及门头石匾，真伪待证）

楠溪江地处荒僻，却与当时的主流文化保持着这样密切的关系，达到这样高的水平，这在全国乡村中也是少见的。

虽说宋亡之后楠溪江文运大衰，但元明之间鹤垟村还出了个谢德瑀，"博通经史，为时名儒"，所著有《狂斐集》、《家礼会通》等。又如同时期花坛村朱谧，著有《四书述义》、《四书辅注》、《太极图说》、《西铭集》等等，从祀郡庠。

理学盛行，加强了楠溪江的宗族制度和封建的伦理道德观念，也提高了乡人的素质。

（3）乡贤士绅

耕读生活培养出来的乡村知识分子，科场得意的是少数，成为理学家的更是寥寥。他们中的大多数，留在村子里，作为上层雅言文化的代表，与郡县官吏一起，在乡村推行教化。这些人里，有的隐居读书，过着比较丰富的精神文化生活，甚至富有著作，有的掌握宗族大权。在楠溪江，这些人为数不少；对涵养楠溪江村落的文化气息作用很大。

《鹤垟谢氏宗谱·义学条规》里说：

义学之设，原为国家树人至计，非以为后生习浮艳，取青紫已也。凡系生徒，务须以白鹿洞规身体力行，……凡肄业弟子，必须一举足疾徐，一语言进止，事事雍容审详，安雅冲和。

学校对子弟的操守品行提出很严格的要求，读书人成了农村敦品励行的榜样。他们的文化生活和精神追求往往被理想化而记载在宗谱里，世代传诵。例如，《棠川郑氏宗谱》里记载着乡绅郑公谔，"旷达多才，好稽古，善词赋。筑美室，置图书，列古画玩物以供清赏。读诵之暇，惟以弹琴栽花为乐，遇风日晴和，则汲泉煮茗，拂席开樽，与二三知己，啸傲于烟霞泉石间，不复知有人世荣辱事。且课子有程，义方之外，更以诗书陶镕其气质"。花坛村朱谧，"读书好古，淳朴自持，利欲不能移其心，荣禄不足夺其志。孝以事亲，友以处弟"（见《明义堂处士墓志铭》）。宗谱和墓志有夸饰，但从中可见价值观的取向。

有些乡绅直接担任教育工作。宋末元初鹤垟村的谢梦符，"博学经史，推重当时，宋咸淳中为郡庠学宾，继升经谕。丰仪整肃，衣冠严雅，
sections.content_en:
1. Farming-Reading Life

Farming-reading life, early as an ideal of scholars, originated in reclusion, in the personality structure combining Confucian "in retreat, cultivate oneself" and Daoist return to nature. But by Song dynasty, it was transformed and greatly strengthened by the imperial examination system.

The imperial examination system was originally designed to select officials; its implementation raised society's general cultural level. Song dynasty expanded examination quotas, improved examination methods, plus woodblock printing flourished, thereby stimulating ordinary families' interest in examinations, causing cultural普及. Even farmer's sons saw possible opportunities before their eyes, so books hung on ox horns, they joined the competition for examination degrees — this formed the new farming-reading life in rural areas.

(1) Examinations and Cultural Popularization

Emperor Renzong of Song had several policies further promoting the farming-reading ideal. One required scholars to study and take examinations in their home districts, thus localities established schools at all levels; another set favorable minimum quotas for southern provinces in various jinshi lists. More importantly, merchants, craftsmen and their sons were prohibited from taking examinations, only scholars and farmers allowed. Farmer sons' examination opportunities greatly increased; "morning a farm boy, evening enters the emperor's hall" — from spring dream became hope, and the sound of loud reading echoed under thatched eaves.

In Nanxi River basin, the farming-reading ideal penetrated every village in remote mountains and waters. Each clan, in "Family Instructions" and "Clan Rules," explicitly required children to study. "Heyang Xie Clan Genealogy · Family Instructions" says descendants should "make farming and reading their occupation"; "Tanxia Chen Clan Genealogy · Family Instructions" (Kangxi edition) teaches: "Farming serves the fundamental, reading illuminates moral teaching." "Yunling Pan Clan Genealogy · Family Instructions" says more comprehensively: "Ancestral family law takes loyalty, filial piety, chastity and righteousness as framework, takes farming, reading, diligence and frugality as fundamental tasks."

For children's education, villages eagerly established schools. On one hand inviting teachers to run charity schools or charity academies; on the other hand subsidizing poor families' children to attend. For example, "Yantou Jin Clan Genealogy · Clan Rules" writes: "Each year invite honest and learned scholars to teach children, must pay generous salaries, honor with ritual and courtesy, not lose old family standards. Children with talent for advancement but lacking means to study, should be assisted with clan rents to complete their education." Most clans' ancestral halls stipulated: those entering county or prefecture schools, and those going to prefecture or provincial examinations, expenses paid by clan. After passing, ancestral worship and various expenses also paid by ancestral hall; clans had public study fields, all income used for education.

Children obtaining examination degrees was the entire clan's glory, all recorded in genealogy. Those with degrees enjoyed special honor in all clan ceremonies. Plaques and couplets in ancestral halls, besides praising ancestors' glorious achievements, boasted clan members' examination success and official careers. Yuzhang Village Hu clan's main ancestral hall has a couplet:

Calligraphy flows fragrance through ages, official hats open ink ponds;
Poetry and books continue beauty through millennia, sacrificial writings illuminate literature.

"Zhenchuan Zhu Clan Combined Genealogy" contains "Record of Ruzai Hall," expressing earnest expectation for children's examination success:

If I possess ten thousand books, no less than storing a thousand bushels of grain; then later sons and grandsons, if not forgetting this intention, will surely strive in poetry and books, soar to official careers, above continuing ancestral achievements, below leaving plans for descendants, not disgracing prior generations' examination glory, reviving former dynasty's Neo-Confucian lineage — then not only glorifying recent ancestors, but also well continuing the main ancestral hall!

This farming-reading ideal became Nanxi River people's tradition. Remote and enclosed Nanxi River, in tiny villages, the flourishing of literary culture and brilliance of examination achievements is extremely rare in rural China. In Daoguang thirtieth year (1850) "Preface to Rebuilding Heyang Xie Clan Genealogy" says "poetry and books continue beauty, every household worthy of enfeoffment; students in county schools, too many to count" — not empty boasting.

Literary culture flourished due to examinations, but once flourished,必定 transcended examinations. "Zhenchuan Zhu Clan Genealogy · Clan Norm Oath" says clearly:

Without learning, one becomes like a thing; with learning, one can stand — so is learning not great? The learner fulfills human duty to assist heaven. Heaven sets human relations, without learning none can uphold; people have constant order, without learning none can arrange. The wise become clear through learning, the unwise become dull through abandoning learning. A great builder completing a house, timber abundant before him, selecting and arranging without confusion, because guidelines were set beforehand. The gentleman facing affairs without alarm, instituting systems without disturbance — without learning how can his heart be settled? Therefore learning is the gentleman's guideline.

Such deep understanding and passionate pursuit of culture shrouded Nanxi River's remote mountain villages in a thick scholarly atmosphere.

(2) Neo-Confucian Philosophers

General rise in cultural level expanded the intellectual class, thereby expanding the social base of Neo-Confucianism (lixue) since Song-Ming, strengthening its influence.

Wang Shipeng's "Preface to Sending Scholar Ye" says: Yongjia "learning of propriety and ritual ranks first in southeast; those writing like Hengqu (Zhang Zai) and speaking like Yiluo (Cheng brothers) are numerous. Obtaining degrees, entering official service, mostly from this path." Yongjia people directly studying under Cheng and Zhu were also many. In the National Academy, successively Yongjia-native "Yuanfeng Nine Gentlemen" and "Chunxi Six Gentlemen," "all transmitted Cheng-Zhu learning through moral nature and destiny" (see Qianlong "Yongjia County Annals · Customs"). In Southern Song, the "Yongjia School" of Neo-Confucianism formed, represented by Xue Jixuan, Zheng Boxiong, Chen Fuliang and Ye Shi. Zheng Boxiong was from Tangwan Village in middle Nanxi River. According to "Yantou Jin Clan Genealogy," Ye Shi in childhood was raised by Jin family in Yantou Village, studied there — he had intimate relation with Nanxi River.

Besides Zheng Boxiong and Ye Shi, Nanxi River literati included many Neo-Confucian masters. Xikou Village Dai clan: Northern Song had Dai Shu (Yuanfu third year jinshi, 1100) and Dai Xun, two brothers studying under two Cheng brothers, known as "Two Dai." In Southern Song, Dai Shu's son Dai Xu (Jiading jinshi), Ye Shi's student, authored "Five Classics Discussions," "Philosophers' Debates," "Eastern Capital Essentials" etc.; Dai Xun's son Dai Xi (Chunxi fifth year jinshi, 1178), "from Ministry of Rites secretary through six promotions to Crown Prince Supervisor, concurrently Secretary of Imperial Library. Crown Prince Jingxian ordered him to compile commentaries on Changes, Poetry, History, Spring and Autumn, Analects, Mencius, Comprehensive Mirror for Government, each presented as discussion. Acting Minister of Works, appointed Wenhua Pavilion Scholar, posthumously granted Duanming Pavilion Scholar, posthumous name Wenduan. Crown Prince personally wrote 'Understanding Classics' plaque for his hall; has 'Minyin Collection'." (See Jiajing "Wenzhou Prefecture Annals · Figures") Dai Xi's younger brother Guinian's son Dai Meng (Shaoxi Gengxu jinshi, 1190), once studied under Zhu Xi at Wuyi, authored "Changes, History, Four Books Family Discussions," "Six Books Explanations" etc.; Meng's eldest son Dai Zai, disliking official service, authored "Classic Supplements," "Comprehensive Mirror External Records," "Shuolin Collected Writings" etc.; Meng's second son Dai Tong (Chunyou Xinchou jinshi, 1241), authored "Six Books" and other miscellaneous writings. Dai clan's main ancestral hall has a couplet:

Entering Cheng-Zhu gates, playing harmony together, Neo-Confucian origins doubly connected;
Through Northern and Southern Song, called Zou-Lu alike, Ministry of Rites degrees six times attained.

Boasting of the Dai clan's this honor.

Tangwan Village Zheng Boxiong three brothers were all Southern Song jinshi. Boxiong "virtue formed early, especially deep in classical learning. Obtained Shaoxing degree, served as Imperial Academy Director, Imperial Clan Court Vice Minister. Requested external post, served as Longtu Pavilion Scholar governing Ningguo Prefecture. Posthumous name Wensu. Late Shaoxing, Yiluo (Cheng) learning slightly declined, revived by Boxiong. Younger brothers Boying and Bohai both renowned; hence Yongjia learning followed Zheng clan. Has 'Zheng Jingwang Collection'" (Jiajing "Wenzhou Prefecture Annals · Figures"). Boying was Longxing Guiwei (1163) jinshi, has "Guiyu Collection." Bohai was Shaoxing Xinwei (1151) jinshi, established teaching tent, students often reached five hundred.

Additionally, Aodi Shangwan Village had Chen Kui, Shaoxing Guichou (1133) jinshi same list as Chen Liang, friendly with Ye Shi, published over twenty volumes of poetry and five volumes of prose. Furong Village Chen Baozhi, Shaoxing jinshi, studied under Lü Zuqian, poetry friend of Chen Liang. Genealogy has poems "Sending Chen Tongfu" and "Mourning Lü Donglai" each one.

Qianlong "Yongjia County Annals" records: Zhu Xi, while serving as Salt and Tea Commissioner of Liangzhe East Circuit, once visited Nanxi River to meet local Neo-Confucians. First went to Yantou Village to visit his disciple Liu Yu, "renowned for Neo-Confucian learning," saying: "Passing Nanxi without knowing Liu Jinzhi is like passing Dongting without knowing oranges." Unfortunately did not meet. Then went to Xie'ao to visit disciple Xie Fujing, then visited Dai Meng, Dai Tong and Pengxi Village Li Shijing, leaving calligraphy in Pengxi Village. (Cliff carvings and gate stone plaques, authenticity pending verification)

Nanxi River, though remote, maintained such close relations with mainstream culture of the time, reaching such high level — rare in rural China nationwide.

Though after Song's fall Nanxi River's literary fortune greatly declined, between Yuan and Ming Heyang Village produced Xie Deyu, "broadly learned in classics and history, renowned scholar of the time," authored "Kuangfei Collection," "Family Rituals Comprehensive" etc. Similarly contemporary Huatan Village Zhu Mi, authored "Four Books Expositions," "Four Books Supplementary Annotations," "Taiji Diagram Explanation," "Ximing Collection" etc., enshrined in prefecture school.

Neo-Confucianism's prevalence strengthened Nanxi River's clan system and feudal ethical-moral concepts, also raised villagers' quality.

(3) Local Worthies and Gentry

Rural intellectuals nurtured by farming-reading life: few succeeded in examinations, even fewer became Neo-Confucian philosophers. The majority stayed in villages, as representatives of upper-class literate culture, together with county and prefecture officials, promoting moral education in countryside. Among them, some lived in reclusion reading, enjoying relatively rich spiritual-cultural life, even authoring works; some held clan power. In Nanxi River, such people were numerous; they greatly contributed to cultivating Nanxi River villages' cultural atmosphere.

"Heyang Xie Clan Genealogy · Charity School Regulations" says:

Charity schools established originally as the state's supreme plan for nurturing people, not for youth to learn flowery rhetoric and obtain official degrees. All students must personally practice the White Deer Grotto regulations... All studying disciples must, in every step's speed, every word's advance and retreat, be composed and careful, elegant and harmonious.

Schools imposed strict requirements on children's conduct and character; scholars became models of moral cultivation in rural areas. Their cultural life and spiritual pursuits were often idealized and recorded in genealogies, transmitted through generations. For example, "Tangchuan Zheng Clan Genealogy" records local gentry Zheng Gong'e: "Broad-minded and talented, fond of antiquity, skilled in poetry and rhapsody. Built fine house, placed books, displayed ancient paintings and curios for refined appreciation. Between reading, only took joy in playing qin and planting flowers; when weather fair, drew spring water to brew tea, spread mats and opened wine cups, with two or three close friends, roaming freely among mist, clouds, springs and rocks, no longer knowing worldly glory or shame. And taught children with schedule, beyond proper upbringing, further cultivated their temperament through poetry and books." Huatan Village Zhu Mi, "studied and loved antiquity, simple and self-contained, profit and desire could not move his heart, glory and salary could not seize his will. Filial to parents, fraternal to brothers" (see "Mingyi Hall Hermit Epitaph"). Genealogies and epitaphs have exaggeration, but从中可见 value orientation.

Some local gentry directly served in education. Late Song-early Yuan Heyang Village's Xie Mengfu, "broadly learned in classics and history, esteemed in his time; in Song Xianchun era served as prefecture school guest lecturer, then promoted to classics instructor. Dignified bearing, elegant dress,

sections.name: 山水情怀
sections.content_zh:
2. 山水情怀

楠溪江风光秀丽。楠溪江又是小邹鲁。秀丽的风光，与文化中热爱自然之美的传统一起，哺育了楠溪江人的山水情怀。每当丝雨迷濛、烟云舒卷的春季，遍青山开满了杜鹃。山红初谢，又是洁白的桐花烂漫。到了秋深，乌桕树浓艳如血。澄澈的江水，随着时序，映照各种鲜明的颜色。深深受到传统文化熏染的楠溪江文士们，对自然之美很敏感，一种清醒的环境审美意识，在楠溪江人的心中氤氲，并且转化为村落的魅力。它们与美的自然融为一体，还引用自然来装饰点缀，房舍的风格又最朴实。自然是楠溪江乡土建筑的魅力所在。

（1）江山有幸

江山多娇，江山也有幸。公元422年，刘宋永初三年，谢灵运来到永嘉郡任太守。他陶醉于永嘉的山水，"肆意游遨"，写出了中国第一批山水诗。谢灵运守永嘉不到一年，却在楠溪江留下了不少足迹。斤竹涧、白岸、石室涧、绿嶂山，他都题过诗。

乾隆《永嘉县志·舆地》说："往者谢康乐为郡，好游名山，由是此郡山水闻于天下。天下之士行过是邦者亦莫不俯仰留连，吟咏不辍，以诧其胜。"在这些俯仰流连的人里，据乾隆《永嘉县志·名胜志》载，有萧梁的陶弘景。他的名诗《答齐高帝诏》就写于绿嶂山。诗道：

山中何所有？岭上多白云；
只可自怡悦，不堪持寄君。

所以后来就有地名白云岭。乾隆《大若岩记》又说他在小楠溪的大若岩修炼，写了重要的道教典籍《真诰》和《本草集注》、《补阙肘后百一方》两部医书。他修炼的地方叫陶公洞，附近也有一座白云岭。不远的水云村里还造了一座白云亭。传说千古名篇《答谢中书书》描写的就是楠溪江风光。

唐代诗人孟浩然、罗隐和崔道融到过永嘉。白居易到过楠溪江，在大若岩捐钱开水道，筑了两处堤防（见《大若岩记》）。宋代到过永嘉的有陆游，明代则有李东阳。清初学者朱彝尊抗清失败后来到楠溪江，曾住在廊下村。《曝书亭集》里的《永嘉杂咏》，有几首是在廊下村写的。如《华坛望雁荡山歌赠方十三朱生、朱十八振嘉》：

登华坛之绝顶，眺雁岩之回峦。云容容兮欲雨，水嘈嘈兮下山。遥岭出没不可胜数，但见哀禽离兽日暝而俱还。

自康乐公启端，历代诗人们对楠溪江山水"吟咏不辍"。苏轼又钦佩又自信地写诗道："自言长官如灵运，能使江山似永嘉。"永嘉的江山真是幸运。

生活在锦绣河山之中，心田里受着千余年文化的滋润，楠溪江的乡村文人们，对山川草木的美非常敏感也非常热爱。以耕读自娱的读书人，"寄志林泉"，"或临流而歌啸，或倚石而垂钓"，以他们的整个生活和诗文表现对大自然的感情。花坛村的朱伯清，明代人，"丰神秀逸，嗜学有文，不乐仕进，志存林壑。……家事付之诸子，惟以文墨自娱。凡石、树、虫、鱼、水泉、花药之会心寓目者，咸属吟咏其间。遇风和日暖，角巾鹿裘，从以弟子，徘徊乎水光山色。拂云坐石，手挥丝桐，目送飞鸿，逍遥自乐"（《珍川朱氏宗谱·伯清公珍川十咏序》）。所以乾隆《永嘉县志》说，楠溪江"山峰挺秀，涧水呈奇，人生其地者，皆惠中而秀外，温文而尔雅"。

奇秀的山水涵养出楠溪江乡民独有的气质和人文的特色。

这种气质，化而为楠溪江建筑的风格。他们的村落、房舍和园林都朴实无华，然而都舒展开朗。他们善于利用天然材料的本形、本性、本色，使建筑与天地和谐。家家使用不加錾凿的蛮石墙，弧形放足，粗犷有力，矗立在大块卵石铺就的地面上，整个村落仿佛从荒古时代与山岩同时生成。他们也爱用天然原木，不加斤斧，随弯就曲，巧妙地把它们安装在恰当的位置上，它们就好像应该有那样的弯曲和粗糙。带着生命原有的形状，它们与庭前的树木和一切有生命的相呼应。

从上到下，建筑绝少雕琢，木石最大限度地保存着天然本色；少量的加工，出自人类双手天然的能力。这就孕成了楠溪江建筑给人的亲切感。

建筑物的形式也是很自然的。宜廊则廊，宜堂则堂，轻巧的披檐，自在地遮挡着一切应该遮挡的地方。翘曲飘洒的屋顶，像搏击长空的鹰翼那样灵动。

楠溪江人的环境审美意识，也表现在村落的选址、规划、绿化、园林、构图等等上面，使人为居住环境与美丽的山川构成统一的景观。

（2）意在山水之间

开发楠溪江的先人们，没有例外，都把村落建在风景优美的地方。谢灵运的后裔本来定居在郡城，有一次："冼五五公游楠溪，见鹤垟之胜，又自郡城迁居鹤垟。"（《重修鹤垟谢氏宗谱序》）其他各村的宗谱里，也都记载着类似的选址故事。如塘湾村，始迁祖"爱楠溪山水之胜"，而来落户；渠口村始迁祖也是"爱其山水之胜，遂家焉"，等等。

豫章村在小楠溪南岸，进村之前，先要穿密林，过荒江野渡，再穿密林。村后如刻如削的峰峦，层层叠叠，向两侧涌伸伸展。山脚下平畴如带，竹树掩映中，参差百十户人家。江水在村左村右萦回成宽阔的碧潭，隔江正对一座青翠的狮子山。《豫章胡氏宗谱·旧序》（康熙三十四年，1695年）说：

永嘉山水，秀丽无如楠源大小二岩，巉岩耸挺，空兀崆峒，历有仙灵凭居托迹。下此而称名胜，莫如豫章。文峰现沼锺其奇，玉笏横头著其异。其间降岳发祥，代多伟烈，居其下者，则有胡氏。……宗族殷蕃，子孙秀蔚……宗支派衍，霞蒸林郁。

珍溪上游的廊下村，在一条山沟里，四周山形奇突。溪水从东北来，掠过村北、村西，由西南流向花坛村。《珍川朱氏合族副谱·廊下即景诗序》里说：

山连雁荡，入径已觉清幽；地肖龙头，过岭方知奥旷。水环如带，可数游鳞；峰列为屏，时度飞鸟。桑麻蔽其野阡，枫授藏乎盈山。仿佛乎桃源之幽隐，盘谷之窈深焉。

楠溪江两岸古村落的风光大多如此，傍山就水，充分展现环境的美。

（3）保护、点缀、增益

楠溪江人，以他们的文化素养感受环境的美，细腻鲜明。《坦下陈氏宗谱》载康熙时人玠侯先生五言律，描绘坦下村的风景：

团团一派石，绿竹间青松。沙外溶溶水，门前叠叠峰。
山花开屿岸，野鸟唤春风。锄犁能读史，□□振飞鹏。

经过文人们揣摩品评，楠溪江许多村落都有"十景"、"八景"之类，宗谱里也多有《名胜》专篇。谢道宁《鹤垟八景诗》之一《锦嶂春晖》：

万仞屏环仰照临，阳和随见破群阴。岩花呈秀分高下，野树浮光间浅深。
适兴岂无人蹑屐，寻幽还有客抚琴。西郊只隔疏林外，多少红尘乱扑襟。

诗把风光的美和一种自然的生活态度融合在一起。通过追慕先祖康乐公，又把这种生活态度和千年的文化传统联系在一起。

经这些在乡文士倡导，楠溪江人很重视保护自然环境，包括树木。村村有风水林，不许砍伐。村头村尾，古树浓荫蔽天。《棠川郑氏宗谱·新宫坳樟树记》载，新宫坳里有太阴宫，"宫右侧有樟木一株，其大可丈围，其高难尺计。……葱茏在望，经雨露而弥新；新秀可餐，阅风霜而不改。斯固刍荛之所栖息，抑亦竖牧之婆娑也。然蔽烈日，御罡风，位置得宜，其又有关于风水乎？"但是，竟有一些见利忘义之徒，企图砍伐这棵树。"于是村中知事者不敢袖手以旁观，斟酌再三，集款买归宗祠之业，立有字据，永后并不许砍断。"

流连，吟咏，保护，都不足以充分表达楠溪江人的山水情怀，他们进而要为山川生色。大小村落，往往都有台榭亭阁之类的风景小品建筑物。记载最早的是北宋进士、宝章阁侍制陈除师在蓬下村，"筑一笑、拨云二亭于富岩以观瀑"（见《两源陈氏大宗祠谱》）。比较著名的则有谢公后裔的鹤垟村里几座小品建筑。宗谱载，元代至正年间，谢毅孙"襟怀潇洒，雅爱宾客。……善音乐，喜与人吟咏，……与西席陈宪宾主义洽，相与筑台于东山之上，植兰种竹，取康乐公遗言镌其岩曰兰玉台。师生经暇，憩息其间，以消长夜。朋友倡和，成《兰玉台集》"。到了明代中叶，任职锦衣卫的谢廷循"创楼于鹤溪之西，因楼傍清流，故名曰'临清'，以为宴宾吟咏之所"，同时在"村北水溪"造了一座"临流亭"。廷循绘临流亭图呈明宣宗，宣宗竟题了一首诗：

临流亭馆净无尘，落涧泉声处处闻。半湿半干花上露，飞来飞去岭头云。
翠迷洞口竹千个，白占林梢鹤一群。此地清幽人不到，惟留风月与平分。

这座亭子因此也叫"宝翰亭"。

对山水点缀增益，仍然不能满足文士们的一往情深，他们动手创建。楠溪江的"隐士"大多喜欢"锄园种花，凿池开圃"，布置私家小园。《乐安珍川朱氏宗谱》载廊下村朱映峰作《隐居歌》道：

非士亦非农，半耕还半读。傍山数顷田，临水几间屋。筑园又凿池，栽花复种竹。……花自吐清香，竹亦言芳郁，池水漾芰荷，园蔬借蓓苜。

明代中叶，花坛村的朱谧，"家颇饶，经营堂构，馀址凿池开圃，植花养鱼，以为宗戚朋旧壶觞吟咏笑傲处"。约略同时，同村朱闿轩有《石假山》诗一首，首联是"谁欤挺秀若天然，叠翠层峦景万千"（均见《珍川朱氏宗谱》），可见当时山村造园已经有叠假山技艺。岩头村的上花园，苍坡村的水月堂，芙蓉村芙蓉书院山长住宅和"大宅"都有小园，至今古木参天，花墙和假山残迹依稀可见。

山水情怀，造就了楠溪江村落最大的特色之一，大型的公共园林。岩头、苍坡、溪口、渠口、埭头、珠岸、西岸、鹤盛等村的公共园林大体还保存着。埭头村、鹤盛村和鹤垟村的公园在山坡上，西岸村的在江边，古木森森，远远就能望见。岩头村的公园，纯藉人力，内容最丰富、布局最多变化，是明代嘉靖年间兴造的。它包含一座小小的汤山，一片镇南湖、一片进宦湖，和它们间的琴屿半岛，还有一条300米长的丽水湖。两个湖都由人工堤坝拦蓄溪水形成，堤上古木数株，绿荫下一座精巧玲珑的小亭，汤山顶上有塔，山麓有楼阁和庙。湖中荷花盛开，岛上芙蓉灿烂如霞。

公园是村民们公共活动场所，尤其是乡村文人们的。岩头村的《十景诗》描绘了他们在公园里的活动。《长堤春晓》诗句有："结伴连朝频载酒，行吟不惜绕长堤"；《丽桥观荷》诗有句："坐对嫣然如解语，乘风散步纳凉时"；《清沼观鱼》诗有句："绍堤花柳可行歌，笑看游鳞跳锦波"；《曲流环碧》诗有句："不知把钓垂竿子，坐对渔矶乐若何？"这些诗里，乡村文士们的生活和意趣宛然可见，也可见他们如痴如醉的山水情怀。

这些乡村文士在公园里过着高品位的文化生活，必然会把他们深湛的文化修养带到公园的一草一木中去。所以这些园林和它们的建筑的风格都很轻逸淡雅。诗情画意，不脱乡土本色。

贯穿在楠溪江中游村落建设中的山水情怀和生活文化，是楠溪江中游乡土建筑不朽的魅力所在。
sections.content_en:
2. Landscape Sentiment

Nanxi River scenery is beautiful. Nanxi River is also "Little Zou-Lu" (Confucian cultural heartland). Beautiful scenery, together with the cultural tradition of loving natural beauty, nurtured Nanxi River people's landscape sentiment. Every spring, when misty rain and rolling clouds fill the air, azaleas bloom across green mountains. As mountain red fades, white paulownia flowers burst forth. In deep autumn, tallow trees turn vivid as blood. Clear river water, following seasons, reflects various bright colors. Nanxi River literati, deeply influenced by traditional culture, are very sensitive to natural beauty; a sober environmental aesthetic consciousness permeates Nanxi River people's hearts, and transforms into village charm. They integrate with beautiful nature, also引用 nature for decoration, while house style is simplest. Nature is the charm of Nanxi River vernacular architecture.

(1) Blessed Mountains and Rivers

Mountains and rivers are beautiful, and also blessed. In 422 CE, Liu-Song Yongchu third year, Xie Lingyun came to Yongjia Commandery as governor.
