He was intoxicated by Yongjia's mountains and waters, "recklessly roaming," writing China's first batch of landscape poetry. Xie Lingyun governed Yongjia less than a year, yet left many traces in Nanxi River. Jinzhu Stream, Bai'an, Shishi Stream, Lüzhang Mountain — he all wrote poems about.

Qianlong "Yongjia County Annals · Geography" says: "Formerly Duke Kangle (Xie Lingyun) as governor, loved touring famous mountains, hence this commandery's mountains and waters became known worldwide. Scholars passing through this region all linger, chanting endlessly, praising its beauty." Among those who lingered, according to Qianlong "Yongjia County Annals · Scenic Spots," was Xiao-Liang's Tao Hongjing. His famous poem "Reply to Emperor Gao of Qi's Edict" was written at Lüzhang Mountain:

What is in the mountains? Many white clouds on the ridges;
Only for self-enjoyment, cannot be sent to you, my lord.

Hence later place name Baiyun (White Cloud) Ridge. Qianlong "Daluo Rock Record" also says he practiced Daoist cultivation at Daluo Rock on Minor Nanxi River, writing important Daoist text "Zhengao" and two medical books "Collected Commentaries on Materia Medica" and "Supplementary Elbow-side Remedies." His cultivation place is called Tao Gong Cave; nearby is also a Baiyun Ridge. Not far away in Shuiyun Village, a Baiyun Pavilion was built. Legend says the eternal masterpiece "Letter in Reply to Secretary Xie" describes Nanxi River scenery.

Tang poets Meng Haoran, Luo Yin and Cui Daorong visited Yongjia. Bai Juyi visited Nanxi River, donating money to open water channels and build two dikes at Daluo Rock (see "Daluo Rock Record"). Song dynasty Lu You visited Yongjia; Ming dynasty Li Dongyang. Early Qing scholar Zhu Yizun, after failing in anti-Qing resistance, came to Nanxi River and lived in Langxia Village. In "Baishuting Collection," "Yongjia Miscellaneous Poems" has several pieces written in Langxia Village. Such as "Huatan Viewing Yandang Mountain Song, Presented to Fang Shisan, Zhu Sheng, Zhu Shibazhenjia":

Climb Huatan's highest peak, gaze at Yandang's winding ridges. Clouds swelling, about to rain; water rushing, descending mountains. Distant ridges appear and disappear beyond count, only mournful birds and separated beasts return at dusk.

Since Duke Kangle began it, generations of poets "chanted endlessly" about Nanxi River mountains and waters. Su Shi, both admiring and confident, wrote: "Saying the governor is like Lingyun, can make mountains and rivers like Yongjia." Yongjia's mountains and rivers are truly blessed.

Living amid splendid mountains and rivers, hearts nourished by over a thousand years of culture, Nanxi River rural literati are very sensitive to and deeply love the beauty of mountains, rivers, plants and trees. Scholars who amused themselves with farming and reading, "lodged aspirations in forests and springs," "sometimes sang by flowing water, sometimes angled leaning on rocks," expressing their feelings for nature through their entire life and poetry. Huatan Village's Zhu Boqing, Ming dynasty person, "elegant bearing, fond of learning and literary, disliking official service, aspirations in forests and valleys. ... Family affairs entrusted to sons, only amused himself with writing and ink. Whatever rocks, trees, insects, fish, springs, flowers and herbs caught his heart and eye, all became subjects of chanting. When weather warm and sunny, wearing scholar's cap and deerskin robe, followed by disciples, wandering among water and mountain light. Brushing clouds, sitting on rocks, playing qin, watching flying geese, carefree and joyful" ("Zhenchuan Zhu Clan Genealogy · Preface to Boqing Gong's Zhenchuan Ten Poems"). Therefore Qianlong "Yongjia County Annals" says Nanxi River "peaks graceful, streams wondrous; people born there are wise within and elegant without, gentle and refined."

Wondrous mountains and waters nurtured Nanxi River villagers' unique temperament and humanistic character.

This temperament transformed into Nanxi River architectural style. Their villages, houses and gardens are all plain and unadorned, yet open and bright. They are skilled at using natural materials' original form, nature and color, making architecture harmonious with heaven and earth. Every household uses uncarved rough stone walls, curved and broad, rugged and powerful, standing on ground paved with large cobblestones — the whole village seems to have been born with the rocks from primeval times. They also love using natural raw timber, without axe or chisel, following curves, cleverly installing them in appropriate positions — they seem meant to have that curvature and roughness. Bearing life's original shape, they echo with courtyard trees and all living things.

From top to bottom, architecture rarely carved; timber and stone maximally preserve natural color; minimal processing, from human hands' natural ability. This nurtures the亲切感 of Nanxi River architecture.

Building forms are also very natural. Where corridor suits, corridor; where hall suits, hall. Light lean-to eaves freely shelter whatever should be sheltered. Curved and flowing roofs, as nimble as eagle wings striking the sky.

Nanxi River people's environmental aesthetic consciousness also manifests in village site selection, planning, greening, gardens, composition, etc., making man-made living environment and beautiful mountains and rivers form a unified landscape.

(2) Intent Amid Mountains and Waters

Pioneers who developed Nanxi River, without exception, built villages in scenic places. Xie Lingyun's descendants originally settled in commandery city; once: "Xian Wuwu Gong toured Nanxi, saw Heyang's beauty, then moved from commandery city to Heyang" ("Preface to Rebuilding Heyang Xie Clan Genealogy"). Other villages' genealogies also record similar site-selection stories. Tangwan Village, founding ancestor "loved Nanxi mountains and waters' beauty," came to settle; Qukou Village founding ancestor also "loved its mountains and waters' beauty, then made home there," etc.

Yuzhang Village is on south bank of Minor Nanxi River; before entering village, must first pass dense forest, cross desolate river crossing, then pass dense forest again. Behind village, carved and chiseled peaks, layer upon layer, stretch outward on both sides. At mountain foot, flat fields like ribbons; amid bamboo and trees, uneven hundred-some households. River winds around village left and right into broad green pools; across river faces a verdant Lion Mountain. "Yuzhang Hu Clan Genealogy · Old Preface" (Kangxi 34th year, 1695) says:

Yongjia mountains and waters, none as beautiful as Nan Source's two large and small rocks; craggy and towering, hollow and deep, through ages immortals dwelt and left traces. Below these as scenic spots, none like Yuzhang. Literary Peak reflected in pool captures its wonder; Jade Tablet across head marks its uniqueness. Here auspiciousness descended, generations of great achievements; those dwelling below are the Hu clan. ... Clan prosperous, descendants elegant... clan branches spread, like rosy clouds and lush forests.

Langxia Village, upper reaches of Zhenxi Stream, lies in a mountain valley with strangely shaped surrounding mountains. Stream comes from northeast, passes village north and west, flows southwest toward Huatan Village. "Zhenchuan Zhu Clan Combined Genealogy · Preface to Langxia Scenic Poems" says:

Mountains connect to Yandang; entering path already feels secluded; land resembles dragon head, crossing ridge only then knows depth and openness. Water rings like a belt, one can count swimming fish; peaks array as screen, birds pass from time to time. Mulberry and hemp cover field paths, maples hide full mountains. Like the seclusion of Peach Blossom Spring, the depth of Pan Valley.

Nanxi River两岸 ancient villages' scenery is mostly like this — leaning on mountains and following waters, fully displaying environmental beauty.

(3) Protection, Embellishment, Enhancement

Nanxi River people, with their cultural cultivation, feel environmental beauty delicately and vividly. "Tanxia Chen Clan Genealogy" records Kangxi-era Mr. Jiehou's five-character regulated verse describing Tanxia Village scenery:

Round stretch of rocks, green bamboo interspersed with pine. Beyond sand, flowing water; before door, layered peaks.
Mountain flowers bloom on isle shores, wild birds call in spring breeze. Plow and hoe can read history, □□ soar like rocs.

After literati's appreciation and evaluation, many Nanxi River villages have "Ten Scenes," "Eight Scenes" and the like; genealogies also often have "Scenic Spots" special chapters. Xie Daoning's "Heyang Eight Scenes Poems" one "Brocade Cliff Spring Glory":

Ten-thousand-ren screen surrounds, welcoming light; warmth follows, breaking group shadows. Cliff flowers show beauty high and low; wild trees float light between shallow and deep.
For enjoyment, aren't there people in clogs? Seeking seclusion, still guests play qin. West suburb only separated by sparse forest, how much red dust rushes to collars.

Poetry integrates scenic beauty with a natural life attitude. Through admiring ancestor Duke Kangle, this life attitude connects with thousand-year cultural tradition.

Advocated by these local literati, Nanxi River people value protecting natural environment, including trees. Every village has fengshui forest, forbidden to cut. Village heads and tails, ancient trees cast dense shade. "Tangchuan Zheng Clan Genealogy · Record of Camphor Tree at Xingong'ao" records: at Xingong'ao there is Taiyin Palace, "right of palace stands a camphor tree, circumference over a zhang, height beyond measure. ... Lush in view, fresher after rain and dew; new beauty to savor, unchanged through wind and frost. It is where woodcutters rest, where shepherds linger. Yet it shields fierce sun, withstands strong winds, well-positioned, and also relates to fengshui?" However, some profit-forgetting people attempted to cut this tree. "Thus village leaders dared not stand by; after careful consideration, collected funds to buy it as ancestral hall property, established documents, forever forbidding cutting."

Wandering, chanting, protecting — none sufficient to fully express Nanxi River people's landscape sentiment; they further sought to enhance mountains and rivers. Large and small villages often have scenic accessory buildings like terraces, pavilions and towers. Earliest recorded: Northern Song jinshi and Baozhang Pavilion Attendant Chen Chushi at Pengxia Village, "built Yixiao and Boyun two pavilions at Fuyan to view waterfalls" (see "Liangyuan Chen Clan Main Ancestral Hall Genealogy"). More famous are several accessory buildings in Heyang Village of Xie Gong descendants. Genealogy records: Yuan Zhizheng era, Xie Yisun "broad-minded, loved guests. ... skilled in music, fond of chanting with others, ... with tutor Chen Xianbin in harmony, together built terrace on East Mountain, planted orchids and bamboo, taking Duke Kangle's last words to carve on rock: Lanyu Terrace. Teacher and student, in leisure, rested there, to pass long nights. Friends exchanged poems, forming 'Lanyu Terrace Collection'." By mid-Ming, Xie Tingxun of Embroidered-Uniform Guard "built tower west of Hexi Stream, because tower beside clear stream, named 'Linqing' (Facing Clarity), as place for banqueting guests and chanting"; simultaneously built "Linliu Pavilion" (Facing Stream Pavilion) at "village north stream." Tingxun painted Linliu Pavilion and presented to Ming Xuanzong; Xuanzong actually inscribed a poem:

Facing-stream pavilion pure without dust, falling stream spring sounds heard everywhere. Half-wet half-dry dew on flowers, flying back and forth clouds on ridge heads.
Green迷 cave mouth thousand bamboos, white占 forest tips a flock of cranes. This place secluded, people don't come, only wind and moon share equally.

This pavilion hence also called "Baohan Pavilion" (Precious Calligraphy Pavilion).

Embellishing and enhancing mountains and waters still couldn't satisfy literati's deep affection; they took to creating. Nanxi River "hermits" mostly liked "hoeing gardens and planting flowers, digging pools and opening plots," arranging private small gardens. "Le'an Zhenchuan Zhu Clan Genealogy" records Langxia Village Zhu Yingfeng's "Hermit Song":

Not scholar nor farmer, half farming half reading. By mountains several qing of fields, by water several rooms. Build garden and dig pool, plant flowers and bamboo. ... Flowers emit fragrance, bamboo also speaks of fragrance; pool water ripples with lotus, garden vegetables借 tender shoots.

Mid-Ming, Huatan Village's Zhu Mi, "family fairly wealthy, built halls, on remaining site dug pool and opened garden, planted flowers and raised fish, as place for relatives and friends to drink, chant and laugh." Around same time, fellow villager Zhu Kaixuan had "Rock Artificial Mountain" poem, first couplet: "Who stands graceful as if natural, layered green peaks scenery myriad" (both in "Zhenchuan Zhu Clan Genealogy") — showing mountain village gardening already had artificial mountain stacking technique by then. Yantou Village's Upper Garden, Cangpo Village's Shuiyue Hall, Furong Village's Furong Academy mountain-chief residence and "Great Mansion" all had small gardens; to this day ancient trees tower, flower walls and artificial mountain remnants faintly visible.

Landscape sentiment created one of Nanxi River villages' greatest features: large public gardens. Public gardens of Yantou, Cangpo, Xikou, Qukou, Daitou, Zhu'an, Xi'an, Hesheng villages etc. are largely preserved. Daitou, Hesheng and Heyang villages' parks are on hillsides; Xi'an Village's by the river, ancient trees dense, visible from afar. Yantou Village's park, purely by human effort, richest in content and most varied in layout, was built in Ming Jiajing era. It includes a small Tang Mountain, a Zhennan Lake, a Jinhuan Lake, the Qinyu Peninsula between them, and a 300-meter Lishui Lake. Both lakes formed by人工 dikes blocking stream water; on dikes several ancient trees, under green shade an exquisite small pavilion; Tang Mountain top has pagoda, mountain foot has pavilion and temple. In lake, lotus blooms abundantly; on peninsula, hibiscus brilliant as rosy clouds.

Parks are villagers' public activity places, especially for rural literati. Yantou Village's "Ten Scenes Poems" depict their activities in the park. "Long Dike Spring Dawn" has lines: "Companions together repeatedly carry wine, walking and chanting not begrudging circling long dike"; "Li Bridge Viewing Lotus" has: "Sitting facing her as if understanding speech, riding wind walking to enjoy cool"; "Clear Pool Viewing Fish" has: "Shao dike flowers and willows can sing along, laughing at swimming scales leaping in brocade waves"; "Winding Stream Encircling Green" has: "Don't know the angler with rod, sitting by fishing rock how joyful?" In these poems, rural literati's life and taste are vividly visible, as is their intoxicated landscape sentiment.

These rural literati living high-grade cultural life in parks inevitably bring their profound cultural cultivation to every plant and tree of the park. Therefore these gardens and their buildings' style are all light and elegant. Poetic and picturesque, yet not departing from vernacular character.

The landscape sentiment and life culture running through middle Nanxi River village construction is the immortal charm of middle Nanxi River vernacular architecture.

sections.name: 宗族组织的作用
sections.content_zh:
1. 宗族组织的作用

楠溪江的村落几乎都是血缘村落，一村一姓，一个宗族。虽然有政府的行政系统，但是在小农经济的农业社会，宗族组织实际上是血缘村落的政权机构。所以，尽管在村子里有大大小小的宗祠，有些村子甚至有宗祠十几座，却没有一个村子有地方行政机构的公廨。

两汉、南北朝和隋唐沿袭了将近一千年的门阀制度，到了宋代彻底消失。代之而起的社会组织力量就是宗族。范仲淹、欧阳询和苏轼都曾经顺应历史潮流，为加强宗族地位和作用有所创建。欧阳询和苏轼倡导宗谱学，各自设计了谱式，沿用了一千来年。范仲淹则提倡宗族设义田，抚老恤贫，保证族人"日有食、岁有衣、嫁娶婚葬皆有赡"，从而加强了宗族的社会功能，加强了它的凝聚力。宋代的理学家重修身，吕大钧首先提倡《乡约》，在家乡陕西蓝田推行之后，"关中风俗为之一变"。乡约是理学家用他们所阐释的儒家礼乐来教化乡民的生活公约，它规范乡民们的思维方式、行为方式和价值观念。宗族是推行乡约的组织力量。

宋室南渡之后，朱熹在南方推行吕氏乡约。楠溪江的主要宗族大都在这时期形成，产生了自己的理学家，并与朱熹有来往。

到了明代，先任永嘉县令，后来又任温州知府的文林，在知府任上于弘治十一年（1498年）制定了一套《族范》，基本内容与吕氏《乡约》一脉相承，在温属五邑推行，楠溪江"各族应之"，纷纷写入宗谱，成为"家训"、"族规"或者"宗范"。

《族范》是宗族的"基本法"，它的《掌教名数》则是宗族的组织法，主要内容是：

一、族宾（按：无说明）。
二、族献（按：无说明）。
三、族长：族长乃一族之统领，必先正己而后正人，务秉至公以御群子弟。……必使上和下睦，同敦雍厚之风。
四、族正：设学行兼优四人为族正，以匡族长之不逮也。凡族内有事，先当咨于族正，然后白于族长之前，为之分辨曲直，析正是非，庶有统属而无紊乱，抑亦正风俗而免事端矣！
五、主籍：择公直子弟二人为主籍，掌管善恶文簿……如此则劝惩之法立。
六、司学：择取性行端庄、学识明达者一人主之，专一训诲弟子，讲习诗书礼义等事。……
七、司讼：推族内洞明事理二人为司讼。凡族之有讼者凭其禀白族长、族正，劝谕不止乃率于官治之，毋得轻造公庭。
八、司恤：司恤二人。凡族人及乡里亲戚贫穷患难，丧葬嫁娶力不赡者，司恤为之白于族长前，劝谕族中之有力者周恤之。……
九、司直：推性刚直，遇事敢言者二人为司直，凡族长有过，从容指陈于族正前，以凭劝勉。族正有过，陈于族长前，以凭规戒。族众有过，轻则直接以屈之，重则白于族长斥之，使之改过自新而后已。
十、司纠：推举铁面无私、不避嫌怨者七人司之。凡族人为恶不听劝谕者，司纠率至家庙，由族长重责。再不听，从官惩之。
十一、值月：举老幼各一人为值月，凡一月之内，一应大小族人所为善恶及词讼等事不报于主籍者，值月必询访而报于各执事，各执事书于簿籍，以白于族长。

这个《掌教名数》把宗族组织规定成很完备的政权机构。《枫林徐氏宗谱·族范八条》里，甚至规定可以动用"祖宗家法"，把"孽深害大，素性又终不肯改移"的盗窃犯处死，"令其全身自毙"。宗族也可以在必要时组织"乡勇"、"义兵"这样的武装力量，进行战争。

宗族组织要负责非一家一户所能办的农田水利的建设和管理。《珍川朱氏宗谱·宗法》里规定，由族中派人"包灌稻田水，节省人工、水料，避免争端，此乃联宗睦族之道"，并且详细写明了各种气候情况下各类地块的灌溉顺序和方法。

宗族有公有经济，包括公田、祭田、学田、义田之类的收入。宗谱里严格规定，公有田产不得变卖。

宗族又是培植和维护社会意识的强大力量。文林的《族范》规定：

凡遇春秋祭祀之时，朔望参谒之日，族长、族正以下，依次而坐，令弟子三人北面而立，读太祖高皇帝《旧制》。其词曰："孝顺父母，尊敬长上，和睦乡里，教训子孙，各安生理，毋作非为。"族属皆跪听。又读古灵陈先生《劝谕文》，曰："为吾民者，父义、母慈、兄友、弟恭、子孝；夫妇有恩、男女有别、子弟有学、乡闾有礼；贫穷患难、亲戚相救，婚姻死丧、邻保相助；毋惰农业，毋作盗贼，毋学赌博，毋好争讼；毋以恶凌善，毋以富骄贫；行者逊路，耕者让畔，斑白者不负戴于道路，则为礼义之俗矣。"族属立听。

有些宗谱里规定得更隆重，朗诵每篇之前要击鼓三声。朗诵时"各要悚然而听，如有在班诒笑闲谈者，族正举于族前，量行责罚，以警将来"。

物质力量加上精神力量，使得宗族组织的力量非常强大，吞没了政府机构。这样强大的宗族力量，足可以管理关系到整个宗族利益的村落规划和建设了。这是楠溪江村落大多有完整的规划，有管理得很好的公共生活中心的主要原因。但是，除了族长的任命按惯例"以齿不以爵，以齿不以尊"之外，其他从族正以下各种职司其实都只能由读书有文化的人担当。其结果就是，农村的各项权力基本都掌握在士绅乡贤手里。可以说，他们的素质决定村落的命运，决定它的面貌。从各村的宗谱里可以见到，村落里比较重要的建设成就，都是由几位热心公益的乡绅文人的创议和主持，并且得到宗族的组织保证。《棠川郑氏宗谱》里有三篇重要的文章：《长堤记》、《池塘记》和《新城记》，它们很详明地记述了事关全村安危的重要工程的建设和管理规矩。
sections.content_en:
1. Role of Clan Organization

Nanxi River villages are almost all kinship villages — one village, one surname, one clan. Although there is government administrative system, in an agricultural society of small-scale peasant economy, clan organization was actually the political institution of kinship villages. Therefore, although villages have ancestral halls large and small, some even over a dozen, no village had a local administrative office.

The clan system (menfa) that persisted for nearly a thousand years through Han, Northern and Southern Dynasties, Sui and Tang completely disappeared by Song dynasty. The social organizational force that replaced it was the clan. Fan Zhongyan, Ouyang Xun and Su Shi all followed historical trends, creating institutions to strengthen clan status and role. Ouyang Xun and Su Shi advocated genealogy studies, each designing genealogical formats used for over a thousand years. Fan Zhongyan advocated clans establishing charity fields (yitian), caring for the elderly and poor, ensuring clan members "have food daily, clothing yearly, weddings and funerals all supported" — thereby strengthening clan's social function and cohesion. Song Neo-Confucians valued self-cultivation; Lü Dajun first advocated "Village Covenant" (Xiangyue), which after implementation in his hometown Lantian, Shaanxi, "changed Guanzhong customs." Village Covenant was a life convention by which Neo-Confucians used their interpreted Confucian rites and music to educate villagers; it regulated villagers' thinking, behavior and values. The clan was the organizational force for implementing village covenants.

After Song court moved south, Zhu Xi promoted Lü's Village Covenant in the south. Nanxi River's main clans mostly formed in this period, producing their own Neo-Confucian philosophers who associated with Zhu Xi.

In Ming dynasty, Wen Lin — first Yongjia County magistrate, later Wenzhou Prefect — in his prefect tenure in Hongzhi eleventh year (1498) formulated a set of "Clan Norms" (Zufan), basic content in same lineage as Lü's "Village Covenant," implemented in five Wenzhou counties; Nanxi River "all clans responded," writing them into genealogies as "family instructions," "clan rules" or "clan norms."

"Clan Norms" was the clan's "basic law"; its "Names and Numbers of Teaching Officers" was the clan's organizational law, main content:

1. Clan Guest (note: no explanation).
2. Clan Worthy (note: no explanation).
3. Clan Head: Clan head is leader of the clan, must first rectify self then rectify others, must uphold perfect fairness to govern all juniors. ... Must make upper harmonious and lower friendly, together cultivating generous ethos.
4. Clan Rectifiers: Appoint four of both learning and conduct as clan rectifiers, to assist clan head's shortcomings. Whenever clan matters arise, first consult clan rectifiers, then report to clan head, to distinguish right and wrong, analyze truth — thus there is order without chaos, also rectifying customs and avoiding disputes!
5. Chief Registrar: Select two fair and upright juniors as chief registrars, in charge of good and evil record books... thus reward and punishment methods established.
6. Education Officer: Select one of upright character and clear learning to lead, solely instructing juniors, studying poetry, books, rites and righteousness. ...
7. Litigation Officer: Select two of clear reasoning in clan as litigation officers. Whenever clan members have disputes, they report to clan head and rectifiers; if persuasion fails, then lead to official treatment, not lightly bringing to court.
8. Relief Officer: Two relief officers. Whenever clan members and relatives suffer poverty and hardship, unable to afford funerals, weddings and marriages, relief officers report to clan head, persuading capable clan members to assist. ...
9. Candid Officer: Select two of upright character and bold speech as candid officers; whenever clan head has fault, calmly point out to clan rectifiers for persuasion. Whenever clan rectifier has fault, report to clan head for admonition. Whenever clan members have fault, minor directly corrected, major reported to clan head for reprimand, until they reform.
10. Discipline Officer: Select seven of iron-faced impartiality, avoiding neither suspicion nor resentment, as discipline officers. Whenever clan members do evil and ignore persuasion, discipline officers lead them to ancestral hall, where clan head severely punishes. If still不听, then official punishment.
11. Monthly Rotation: Appoint one elder and one junior as monthly rotation; within one month, all good and evil deeds and litigation matters not reported to chief registrar, monthly rotation must inquire and report to each officer, each officer records in books, to report to clan head.

This "Names and Numbers of Teaching Officers" defined clan organization as a quite complete political institution. "Fenglin Xu Clan Genealogy · Eight Clan Norms" even stipulated that "ancestral family law" could be used to execute thieves "whose harm is deep and great, whose nature ultimately refuses reform," "letting them die naturally." Clans could also when necessary organize armed forces like "local braves" (xiangyong) and "righteous soldiers" (yibing) for warfare.

Clan organization was responsible for farmland water conservancy construction and management beyond individual households. "Zhenchuan Zhu Clan Genealogy · Clan Law" stipulated that clan-appointed persons "manage paddy field irrigation, saving labor and water, avoiding disputes — this is the way to unite clans and harmonize kinship," and detailed irrigation order and methods for various plots under various weather conditions.

Clans had public economy, including income from public fields, sacrificial fields, study fields, charity fields. Genealogies strictly stipulated public fields could not be sold.

Clans were also powerful forces cultivating and maintaining social consciousness. Wen Lin's "Clan Norms" stipulated:

Whenever spring and autumn sacrifices, or first and fifteenth day visits, clan head, rectifiers and below sit in order; let three juniors face north and read Emperor Taizu Gao's "Old Regulations." Text: "Be filial to parents, respect elders, harmonize village, teach juniors, each settle in livelihood, do no wrong." All clan members kneel and listen. Then read Mr. Guling Chen's "Admonition": "As my people: father righteous, mother kind, brother friendly, younger brother respectful, son filial; husband and wife have affection, men and women have distinction, juniors have learning, village has rites; poverty and hardship — relatives rescue; marriage and death — neighbors assist; do not be lazy in farming, do not be thieves, do not gamble, do not litigate; do not bully good with evil, do not arrogant to poor with wealth; walkers yield road, farmers yield field borders, gray-haired not burdened on roads — then it is a rite-and-righteousness custom." All clan members stand and listen.

Some genealogies stipulated more ceremoniously: before reciting each text, beat drum three times. During recitation "all must listen with awe; if anyone jokes or chats in ranks, clan rectifier raises before clan, punishes proportionally, to warn future."

Material force plus spiritual force made clan organization very powerful, swallowing government institutions. Such powerful clan force was sufficient to manage village planning and construction concerning entire clan interests. This is the main reason most Nanxi River villages had complete planning and well-managed public life centers. However, except clan head appointed by convention "by age not rank, by age not status," all other positions from clan rectifier down actually could only be held by educated literate people. Result: rural power basically held in hands of gentry and local worthies. One can say their quality determines village's fate and appearance. From villages' genealogies, one sees village's more important construction achievements were all proposed and led by several public-spirited local gentry literati, with clan organizational guarantee. "Tangchuan Zheng Clan Genealogy" contains three important articles: "Long Dike Record," "Pond Record" and "New City Record" — they detail construction and management rules of important projects concerning whole village safety.

sections.name: 士绅的作用
sections.content_zh:
2. 士绅的作用

楠溪江村落的士绅乡贤，主要是辞官还乡的、绝意仕进的和举业不成的读书人，他们组成了乡里社会的领导阶层。他们受过良好的文化教育，在论学吟诗之余，大多关心乡里，乐于"善举"，从而把他们的文化修养带进了村落的建设。

村落的规划一般都在建村之初进行，大多失于记述，早已没有可靠的资料。但各族宗谱里，都记载许多有功于乡里建设的人，也记载了一些有长远影响的建设工程。

例如岩头村，《金氏宗谱》记载了第二世祖日新公（生元中统丙子，卒元至正戊子，即1348年）建设水利的事："时厥土苦于旱潦，频岁不登，府君相地宜，顺水性，浚两渠于渎头之南，达泉下灌，常获丰稔，两都农业，迄今赖之。"其后又有桂林公（生明弘治甲寅，卒隆庆已已，1494-1569年），宗谱说他："由始迁岩头以来，列祖非无建造，而兴利之多，功德之盛，应推府君为第一。"他的作为是"培风水、兴地利、置祭田、建公业。""本族地址颇高，田苦旱涸，升四公(按即桂林公)捐旧废资，开凿长河一带，以备蓄泄，并筑高埠，培闸风水。建亭造塔于其上，垂成，归之大宗祠，为通族公业。"约略与桂林公同时，嘉靖进士金昭（霞峰公）建设了上花园、下花园、大宗祠，还为自己建了个牌楼。先后有几个人从事乡里建设，所以岩头村的水系、街道、公共建筑、园林等等，在楠溪江都是最出色的。

苍坡村和芙蓉村，规划严谨、水系完备、街道整齐，苍坡村还有大片的园林，这些也都靠两村历来有热心建设的人士。筑长堤蓄水成湖，在苍坡大约是南宋时代（1178年）的事，早于岩头几近四百年。芙蓉村陈氏的有绪公（生康熙壬申，卒乾隆癸酉，1692-1753年），"有经济济才，读书知大义。……乐于济施。创神庙，建祖祠，增置祀田，造舟以济往来，筑防以利灌溉。公平生所为，有功于族党者未易枚举"（《两源陈氏宗谱》）。

《棠川郑氏宗谱》里有一篇《长堤记》，记的是清代初年，乾隆丁卯（1747年）春，宗人郑西献捐资并组织人力建造堤堰的事。记中写道：

棠川胜区在双溪会所，衔远山、吞长流，前有雷峰九嶂之异，后有马石天岩之险，至若屏风纳日，和合留云，在在称奇。惟路尚缺一堤，虽乔木荫翳，水声潺湲，而往来行人，往往苦此。今则累石为堤，不惜工程，自东岭至西岭，约数十馀丈，状如江塘，平坦可以车行。

除了水利、宗祠、庙宇、道路之外，书院历来是乡里建设的重点，吸引了士绅们最多的注意。《珍川朱氏合族副谱·慎轩公传》说，公"生平乐善好施，而于读书一事尤其所笃，尝虑族子弟辈无肄业所，不克振长人材，作兴后学，爱捐重赀，襄诸乡之知名者创建文昌阁两庑，以为讲学之所"。也有一些对环境绿化有特殊兴趣的，如花坛村的朱复翁，"好读书，朴而不滞，惟亲贤取友以自励。……洪武初，诏山林隐逸，郡县强荐于京，授朝列大夫，乞归，许之，声名益重。建宗祠，置祭田，以奉祀先人。筑室芳岙，植松树数万株以自蔽，因以云松自号。……啸傲云松间，商榷古今，抚琴作诗"（《明征授朝列大夫云松公墓志铭》）。

这些乡贤士绅，在乡土建设中主要起的作用当然是倡议、擘划、捐资，至于工程的主持，就要依靠宗族的力量。例如，康熙二十一年（1682年）六月，为重建渠口叶氏大宗祠，由宗人叶健等发起，"会同两房商议，仰体先人创建之心，各出己资，重建宗祠。择本年八月初六起工切木，来春二月初一日竖造。当日估算，材木几何，椽木几何，考工几何，约用银陆百两"。两房依人口比例分担，长房出肆百两，二房出二百两。粗工由长房负责。这件事显然是由宗族主持的。（见《渠川叶氏宗谱·叶氏合同议据》）

有些宗族，把修桥补路当作一种义务写进家规，如《岩头金氏宗谱·家规》里写道："桥、路、渡舟倾坏，子孙倘有馀资，当助修治。"在《渠口叶氏宗谱》里有《石马岩石栏杆志》和《前山楼梯岩志》两篇文字。前者记一条"上峻壁、下深潭"的宽仅四尺许的山路，"时有夜行客人至此倾跌而下，其危险莫可言状"。于是，一批村人"醵集钜资，建造石栏数十丈。自斯以往，该处变险为夷"。后者记渠口村前山"有名楼梯岩者，高六丈许，陟降必经之处，峻无阶级。樵夫至此，莫不栗栗危惧"，也有一批善人，集资雇石匠，"将高峻处开凿阶级如楼梯焉"。这个宗谱里还有关于修路的记载二十几则。

把这些善举记录在宗谱里，是对当事人的榆扬，"传之永久"，以为子孙后代表率。宗族用这个崇高的荣誉来激励有馀财的人从事乡里建设。如《岩头金氏宗谱·家规》载，"祠堂、坟屋稍遇倾圮，亟当议修，量以坟租、祠租内暂行抽贮，以给支。如有贤孝子孙捐资乐助者，当登记于谱"。更有在记入宗谱之外再加碑刻。例如《鹤垟谢氏宗谱》记第五世端先公"敦尚德义，轻财好施，凿溪港以疏壅滞，乡里赖之。因勒石于鹤岭溪滨，内镌：'宋绍熙五年（1194年）谢十八居士开港'十二字，以志其绩"。一般修造庙宇和石桥也往往把捐资人的姓名刻在碑上或桥上。最突出的是岩头村的桂林公，在他去世之后，村人为纪念他对村子建设的重大贡献，把他创建的书院改成了奉把他的专祠，称为水亭祠。

在乡文士，或是直接、或是通过宗族组织，从事乡里建设，他们的文化素养和山水情怀就转化在这些建设之中了。楠溪江村落里文化建筑的类型和数量很多，建筑的风格大方素雅，不事奢华的雕琢，而且追求建筑与自然山水的融洽。例如乾隆年间造的花坛村文昌阁，"门临曲水，地耸云端，拱群峰之突屹，面万木之郁葱，珍川之胜，于此称第一焉。登斯阁者，晨夕之赏心各异，四时之兴趣不穷，文思秀发，颖悟宏开"（《珍川朱氏合谱·慎轩公传》），要的是在山川胜景中秀发文思，当是清新俊逸。
sections.content_en:
2. Role of Gentry

Nanxi River village gentry and local worthies were mainly scholars who had resigned and returned home, those who had abandoned official aspirations, and those who had failed examinations — they formed the leadership stratum of village society. They received good cultural education; between discussing learning and composing poetry, most cared about their hometowns, delighted in "good deeds," thereby bringing their cultural cultivation into village construction.

Village planning generally occurred at village founding, mostly unrecorded, long without reliable资料. But each clan's genealogy records many people who contributed to hometown construction, and some construction projects with long-term impact.

For example, Yantou Village: "Jin Clan Genealogy" records second-generation ancestor Rixin Gong (born Yuan Zhongtong Bingzi, died Yuan Zhizheng Wuzi, i.e., 1348) building water conservancy: "At that time the land suffered drought and flood, years of poor harvest; the lord assessed terrain, followed water nature, dredged two canals south of Dutou, reaching springs for irrigation, consistently obtaining abundant harvests; agriculture of both districts relies on it to this day." Later there was Guilin Gong (born Ming Hongzhi Jiayin, died Longqing Jisi, 1494-1569); genealogy says: "Since first moving to Yantou, ancestors did have constructions, but in number of benefits and abundance of merit, this lord ranks first." His achievements: "cultivate fengshui, promote land productivity, establish sacrificial fields, build public property." "Our clan's site is rather high, fields suffer drought; Shengsi Gong (i.e., Guilin Gong) donated old unused funds, dug a long river for storage and drainage, built high embankment, cultivated fengshui gate. Built pavilion and pagoda on it, upon completion donated to main ancestral hall as clan-wide public property." Around same time as Guilin Gong, Jiajing jinshi Jin Zhao (Xiafeng Gong) built Upper Garden, Lower Garden, main ancestral hall, and also built a memorial archway for himself. Several people successively engaged in hometown construction, so Yantou Village's water system, streets, public buildings, gardens etc. are the most outstanding in Nanxi River.

Cangpo and Furong villages have rigorous planning, complete water systems, orderly streets; Cangpo also has large gardens — these also relied on generations of construction-minded people in both villages. Building long dike to store water into lake, in Cangpo roughly Southern Song era (1178), nearly four hundred years earlier than Yantou. Furong Village Chen clan's Youxu Gong (born Kangxi Renshen, died Qianlong Guiyou, 1692-1753), "had economic talent, studied and understood great principles. ... Delighted in charity. Built temples, built ancestral hall, added sacrificial fields, made boats for crossing, built dikes for irrigation. What he did in life, merits to clan and kin cannot be enumerated" ("Liangyuan Chen Clan Genealogy").

"Tangchuan Zheng Clan Genealogy" contains "Long Dike Record," recording early Qing, Qianlong Dingmao (1747) spring, clansman Zheng Xixian donating funds and organizing labor to build dike. Record writes:

Tangchuan scenic district at confluence of two streams, embracing distant mountains, swallowing long flow; before has Leifeng Nine Peaks' wonder, behind has Mashi Tianyan's peril; as for Screen Mountain receiving sun, Hehe retaining clouds — everywhere marvelous. Only road lacked a dike; though tall trees shade, water murmurs, travelers often suffered this. Now stones piled as dike, sparing no effort, from East Ridge to West Ridge, about several tens of zhang, shaped like river embankment, flat enough for carts.

Besides water conservancy, ancestral halls, temples, roads — academies were traditionally the focus of hometown construction, attracting gentry's most attention. "Zhenchuan Zhu Clan Combined Genealogy · Biography of Shenxuan Gong" says the lord "lifelong delighted in good deeds, especially devoted to study; once worried clan juniors lacked place to study, unable to cultivate talent and promote later learning, thus donated heavy funds, with local notable persons built Wenchang Pavilion two wings, as place for lectures." Some had special interest in environmental greening, such as Huatan Village's Zhu Fuweng, "loved reading, simple but not stagnant, only sought worthy friends for self-improvement. ... Early Hongwu, imperial edict sought mountain recluses; county and prefecture forcibly recommended to capital, appointed Court Gentleman; requested return, granted, fame grew. Built ancestral hall, established sacrificial fields to worship ancestors. Built house at Fang'ao, planted tens of thousands of pine trees for shelter, hence called himself Yunsong (Cloud Pine). ... Roamed freely among clouds and pines, discussed past and present, played qin and composed poetry" ("Epitaph of Ming Appointed Court Gentleman Yunsong Gong").

These local worthies and gentry, in vernacular construction, of course mainly played roles of proposing, planning, donating; as for project direction, that relied on clan power. For example, Kangxi twenty-first year (1682) June, to rebuild Qukou Ye clan main ancestral hall, initiated by clansman Ye Jian etc.: "consulted both branches, respecting ancestors' founding intention, each contributed own funds to rebuild ancestral hall. Selected August sixth of this year to start cutting timber, next spring February first to erect. That day estimated: how much timber, how much rafter wood, how much labor, approximately six hundred taels of silver." Both branches shared by population ratio: main branch four hundred taels, second branch two hundred taels. Rough labor by main branch. This matter obviously directed by clan. (See "Quchuan Ye Clan Genealogy · Ye Clan Contract Agreement")

Some clans wrote bridge and road repair as obligation into family rules, e.g., "Yantou Jin Clan Genealogy · Family Rules": "Bridges, roads, ferry boats damaged — if descendants have surplus funds, should assist repair." In "Qukou Ye Clan Genealogy" there are two texts: "Shima Rock Stone Railing Record" and "Qianshan Stair Rock Record." The former records a mountain road "above steep cliff, below deep pool" only four chi wide, "sometimes night travelers fell here, danger beyond description." So a group of villagers "collected large funds, built stone railing several tens of zhang. From then on, this place turned danger to safety." The latter records Qukou Village's Qianshan "has place called Stair Rock, about six zhang high,必经 route for ascent and descent, steep without steps. Woodcutters arriving here all tremble with fear"; also a group of good people raised funds to hire stone masons, "carved steps into steep place like stairs." This genealogy also has over twenty records of road repair.

Recording these good deeds in genealogy was to praise the parties, "transmit forever," as example for descendants. Clan used this lofty honor to激励 those with surplus wealth to engage in hometown construction. E.g., "Yantou Jin Clan Genealogy · Family Rules": "Ancestral halls and grave houses slightly damaged — should promptly discuss repair, allocate from grave rents and hall rents temporarily for expenses. If filial descendants donate and gladly assist, should register in genealogy." Some added stone inscriptions beyond genealogy. E.g., "Heyang Xie Clan Genealogy" records fifth-generation Duanxian Gong "valued morality and righteousness, generous with wealth, dug stream channels to clear blockages, village relied on him. Hence carved stone at Heling stream bank, inscribed: 'Song Shaoxi fifth year (1194) Xie Eighteenth Layman opened channel' twelve characters, to record his merit." Generally building temples and stone bridges also carved donors' names on steles or bridges. Most outstanding: Yantou Village's Guilin Gong — after his death, villagers, to commemorate his major contribution to village construction, converted the academy he founded into a shrine dedicated to him, called Shuiting Shrine (Water Pavilion Shrine).

Local literati, either directly or through clan organization, engaged in hometown construction; their cultural cultivation and landscape sentiment transformed into these constructions. Nanxi River villages have many types and quantities of cultural buildings; architectural style is generous and elegant, without luxurious carving, and pursues harmony between architecture and natural mountains and waters. For example, Huatan Village's Wenchang Pavilion built in Qianlong era: "Gate faces winding water, ground rises to clouds, embraced by sudden peaks, facing lush ten thousand trees; Zhenchuan's beauty ranks first here. Those ascending this pavilion, morning and evening delights differ, four seasons' interests endless; literary thought flourishes, understanding broadens" ("Zhenchuan Zhu Clan Combined Genealogy · Biography of Shenxuan Gong") — what was sought was flourishing literary thought amid mountain-water scenery, fresh and elegant.

sections.name: 堪舆师的作用
sections.content_zh:
3. 堪舆师的作用

堪舆风水之说对楠溪江村落的规划和建设有很大的影响，而阴阳师或者地理师，大都出自乡土文人这个阶层。所以，风水堪舆之说是乡贤士绅影响农村规划和建设的又一个途径，阴阳师或者地理师，实际在一定程度上起着类似规划师的作用，但他们所依据的是迷信。

明代嘉靖年间对岩头村的建设作了重大贡献的桂林公，其实就是一位地理师。《岩头金氏宗谱·桂林公行状》说他"屡试不中，转而习青囊，相宅卜地"。传说他还得到宁王幕下谋士"国师"李自实的帮助。他所兴建的，可能都经过堪舆风水的考究。与桂林公大致同时，还有些士绅好星象之学，如嘉靖年间岩头村还有一位九峰先生，他"凡经史以及诸子百家无不娴，且究心星学，陶情音律，至于制艺歌词，皆其余事耳"（《岩头金氏宗谱·九峰先生五旬寿序》）。清代中叶咸丰年间，蓬溪村有一位谢文波，《宗谱》有一篇《谢公文波六旬初度寿序》说："近百年来，临尚武力，独文波笃内行，嗜书史，学涉赅博，家多藏书，插架林立，于壬奇、星数、音韵反切之学，旁及琴棋八法，无不精通，风雅过人远甚。"这位先生的著作有《东瓯杂俎》、《因音求字》、《四声正误》、《反切法》和《草药谱》等等。

这些记载说明，当时习风水和壬奇、星数的人，都是些饱读经典诗书的儒者。儒学是上层的雅言文化，术数是下层的民俗文化，本来属于不同的两类。不过，早在汉代独尊儒术的时候，就已经把它与阴阳五行之类结合起来了。从那时以后，儒者把堪舆风水和壬奇、星数当做一般文化知识来学，并不以为与儒学的正统精神有根本的矛盾。只在迷信得太似乎"怪、力、乱、神"，有悖于情理的时候，才加以驳斥，例如长期停厝不葬，"以死者为生者祈福"，就受到严厉批评。

堪舆风水是迷信邪说，但阴阳师和主持村落建设的士绅们都是当时当地有知识的人。他们是双重人格的，他们会在一些问题上愚妄可笑，但由于他们富有阅历、经验，也会对一些问题作出合乎实际的判断，如对村落选址、水系规划、村落结构布局、防御工程、街道网、重要建筑物的位置和朝向等等，可能有一些比较好的建议。为了保护他们的职业，或者仅仅为了增强他们对自己的实际判断的自信心和他们的建议对公众的说服力，他们便使他们的经验知识附会风水堪舆的"理论"。塘湾村的筑城和凿池，显然都是为了迫切的实际需要，但都附会了一套风水说法。看来这说法虽然是些无根游谈，但有助于号召村民们同心同德，出钱出力，来办成一些公益事业。

楠溪江中游的村子，例如苍坡、岩头和芙蓉，都流传着"国师"李自实规划村落的故事。例如说，南宋淳熙五年（1178年），苍坡村九世祖李嵩请李自实规划了寨墙、街道和池塘、水渠。他使主街直指西方远处的笔架山，命名主街为笔街，以利于发荣科甲。但笔架山又像火焰，为防笔街引火烧村，就在它东端造了两口池塘，以水克火。池塘之一称砚池，再以村子附会纸张，两块石条附会墨锭，与笔街一起组成"文房四宝"，这就更加有利于科甲了。宗族便以这种无根游谈激励子弟刻苦读书。

又例如说，明代嘉靖年间，桂林公请李自实规划岩头村。他问桂林公，希望"紧发"还是"慢发"。紧发即将寨墙包住全姓聚居范围，数代之内就可以发达，但前途有限；慢发即把杂姓聚居地也围在寨墙里，发达虽比较慢，但前途更加繁荣。桂林公选择了"紧发"，寨墙就是现存的状况。李自实还故弄玄虚说，村东的屿山是一条大蟒幻化的，会对村人不利，所以，在村里规划了四条东西向的窄巷，象征四支"箭"，两条在东端分叉的小巷，和一条东端曲折的小巷象征两把半"镗"，这七件"武器"就把屿山大蟒镇住了，可以保护村人平安。

据传说，元至正元年（1341年）重建芙蓉村的时候，也是李自实看风水，做规划的。

这些故事荒诞无稽，而且一个"国师"李自实，从南宋历元代而直到嘉靖年间还在，显然也是虚构。但这些故事却说明，当时确实有这类人对村子的规划性问题提出建议，不论是合理的，还是虚妄的。

虽然有些士绅从事堪舆风水之术，但是对它的宿命论的消极作用也已经有人注意到了。不语"怪力乱神"的儒家文化，对属于俗文化的风水术是很有批判能力的。例如，伪托朱熹写的《雪心赋》大肆鼓吹风水，说"将相公侯，胥此焉出；荣华富贵，何莫不由"。但是，这种宿命论不但没有丝毫的伦理教化意义，甚至有碍于儒家的伦理教化，破坏了儒家教化的价值观。因此，朱熹在《大学衍义补·家乡之礼》里写道："世有选择之法存焉，不能不用之以代卜筮。但其所谓福禄不可信，其趋吉避凶之说亦不可。"堪舆家也有"灵山灵穴，有德者居之"，"山地好，不如心地好"这
sections.content_en:
3. Role of Fengshui Masters

Fengshui (geomancy) theories had great influence on Nanxi River village planning and construction, while yin-yang masters or geomancers mostly came from the local literati stratum. Therefore, fengshui geomancy was another途径 by which local gentry influenced rural planning and construction; yin-yang masters or geomancers actually played a role similar to planners to some extent, but what they relied on was superstition.

Guilin Gong, who made major contributions to Yantou Village construction in Ming Jiajing era, was actually a geomancer. "Yantou Jin Clan Genealogy · Biography of Guilin Gong" says he "repeatedly failed examinations, then turned to studying Qingnang (geomancy), assessing houses and selecting sites." Legend says he also received help from "National Teacher" Li Zishi, a strategist under Prince of Ning. What he built may all have undergone fengshui scrutiny. Around same time as Guilin Gong, some gentry were fond of astrology; e.g., in Jiajing era Yantou Village there was Mr. Jiufeng, who "was adept in all classics and hundred schools, furthermore delved into astrology, found joy in music, as for examination essays and lyrics, all were secondary matters" ("Yantou Jin Clan Genealogy · Preface to Mr. Jiufeng's Fiftieth Birthday"). Mid-Qing Xianfeng era, Pengxi Village had Xie Wenbo; genealogy has "Preface to Mr. Xie Wenbo's Sixtieth Birthday": "In recent hundred years, Lin favored martial force; only Wenbo was devoted to inner conduct, loved books and history, learning broad and deep, family had many books, shelves lined up; in Renqi (divination), astrology, phonology and fanqie, extending to qin, chess and calligraphy, all mastered — elegance far surpassed others." This gentleman's works include "Dongou Miscellany," "Finding Characters by Sound," "Correction of Four Tones," "Fanqie Method" and "Herbal Manual" etc.

These records show that those who studied fengshui, Renqi and astrology were all Confucian scholars well-read in classics. Confucianism was upper-class literate culture; numerology was lower-class folk culture, originally belonging to different categories. However, as early as Han dynasty when Confucianism was独尊, it had already been combined with yin-yang and five elements. From then on, Confucian scholars studied fengshui, Renqi and astrology as general cultural knowledge, not seeing fundamental contradiction with Confucian orthodoxy. Only when superstition became too much like "strange forces, chaos and spirits," contrary to reason, did they refute it — e.g., long-delayed burial, "using the dead to pray for blessings for the living," was severely criticized.

Fengshui is superstitious heresy, but yin-yang masters and gentry who directed village construction were knowledgeable people of their time and place. They had dual personalities: on some issues they were foolish and ridiculous, but due to rich experience, they also made practical judgments on some issues — such as village site selection, water system planning, village structural layout, defense works, street networks, location and orientation of important buildings etc. — possibly giving some good suggestions. To protect their profession, or merely to增强 their confidence in their practical judgments and the persuasiveness of their suggestions to the public, they attached their experiential knowledge to fengshui "theory." Tangwan Village's wall-building and pool-digging were obviously for urgent practical needs, but both were attached with a set of fengshui explanations. It seems these explanations, though groundless talk, helped mobilize villagers to unite, contribute money and labor, to accomplish some public welfare projects.

Middle Nanxi River villages, such as Cangpo, Yantou and Furong, all circulate stories of "National Teacher" Li Zishi planning villages. For example: in Southern Song Chunxi fifth year (1178), Cangpo Village ninth-generation ancestor Li Song invited Li Zishi to plan village walls, streets, ponds and canals. He made the main street point directly at distant Bijia (Brush-holder) Mountain to the west, named main street Brush Street, to promote examination success. But Bijia Mountain also looked like flame; to prevent Brush Street from drawing fire to village, he built two ponds at its east end, using water to overcome fire. One pond called Inkstone Pool; then village associated with paper, two stone slabs associated with ink sticks, together with Brush Street forming "Four Treasures of the Study" — even more favorable for examination success. The clan used this groundless talk to激励 juniors to study hard.

Another example: in Ming Jiajing era, Guilin Gong invited Li Zishi to plan Yantou Village. He asked Guilin Gong whether he desired "rapid prosperity" or "slow prosperity." Rapid prosperity meant village wall enclosing only same-surname settlement area — within several generations could prosper, but future limited; slow prosperity meant enclosing mixed-surname settlement too — prosperity slower but future more prosperous. Guilin Gong chose "rapid prosperity"; the village wall is as existing. Li Zishi also mystified: Yushan east of village was transformed from a giant python, harmful to villagers; therefore he planned four east-west narrow lanes in village, symbolizing four "arrows"; two lanes branching at east end and one winding lane at east end symbolizing two-and-a-half "tang" (halberds); these seven "weapons" subdued the Yushan python, protecting villagers' peace.

According to legend, when Furong Village was rebuilt in Yuan Zhizheng first year (1341), Li Zishi also assessed fengshui and made the plan.

These stories are absurd and baseless; and one "National Teacher" Li Zishi, from Southern Song through Yuan until Jiajing era still alive — obviously fictional. But these stories说明 that at that time there确实 were such people giving suggestions on village planning issues, whether reasonable or delusional.

Although some gentry practiced fengshui, some had already noticed its fatalistic negative effect. Confucian culture, which does not speak of "strange forces, violence, chaos and spirits," had strong critical ability toward fengshui as folk culture. For example, "Xuexin Fu" falsely attributed to Zhu Xi vigorously advocated fengshui, saying "ministers and generals all emerge from this; glory and wealth all come from it." But this fatalism not only had no ethical-moral significance, even hindered Confucian ethical education, destroying Confucian educational values. Therefore, Zhu Xi wrote in "Daxue Yanyi Bu · Hometown Rituals": "The world has site-selection methods; cannot but use them to replace divination. But its so-called fortune and blessing cannot be trusted; its sayings of seeking good and avoiding evil also cannot be [trusted]." Fengshui practitioners also have sayings: "Spirit mountains and spirit caves, inhabited by the virtuous," "Good mountain land is not as good as good heart" —

key_terms.en: Spirit mountains and caves inhabited by the virtuous

sections.name: 工匠的作用
sections.content_zh:
4. 工匠的作用

楠溪江的建筑工匠体制和他们传统的设计、计算、施工等等方法以及有关的民俗行为，已经无从查考。不过，推断在长期小农自然经济社会中，工匠的专业化程度不高，没有组成经济实体、以父子师徒方式传承、有一些行业习俗，大致合乎实际。

工匠大多不是士人、富人，也无从襄赞善行义举，所以不载于宗谱。偶然有几位因为有功于建设，品行超卓，才得以占几行楮墨。例如《两源陈氏宗谱》载明代的工匠："有福公，字佑如，号兰轩，智巧绝伦，有造风阁龙楼之技。家贫不能读书，然颇知大义。岁戊子建文广公祖祠，公匠心独运，不惮艰辛。"另一位也是明代的，见于《坦下陈氏宗谱》："讳士商，字兆霖。气象温和，与人无忤。少习公输之业，精专其事，相材度木，适中其度。所以遐迩创厦新宇，皆任于君。至今妖蝤有继，家道渐宁，然能颇知尊宗敬祖，凡有义举，靡不竭力。"从"匠心独运"、"相材度木"来看，这两位匠人是兼任了设计者的大匠。

由于父子师徒传承，建筑行业的各作都有了专业村。例如"大木老司出罗坑，石头老司出中堡，烧瓦老司出敬仁，泥水老司出绿嶂"。

虽然有专业村，但工匠的专业化程度还不高。大木老司也做床柜、书桌、琴凳，甚至织布机和风车；泥水老司也垒锅灶；打石老司也做捣臼、磨盘、石柱、牌坊、各种石器，甚至刻碑文。砌墙老司的行当尤其驳杂，要造石拱桥、铺路、筑矶步、垒城墙、挖地道、砌田坎等等。最使这些老司的手艺发挥得淋漓尽致的，是做各种装饰。泥水老司会塑飞禽走兽、人物山水、狮子麒麟。"堆龙就像龙一色，塑凤就像凤飞腾。"打石老司会打这些题材，还要把"狮子捧球打镂空"。砌墙老司则会用卵石在地面镶出各种图案，叫做"插石花"。

关于这些匠作，楠溪江都有歌谣吟咏。雅言文化的宗谱所不取的，在民俗文化中却代代流传。民俗文化，基本上是劳动者的文化。一首《大木老司》的歌谣是：

大木老司手艺精，手控丈杆量得清。
曲尺木斗线弹准，墨划梁柱分寸明。
双退大屋两边轩，能造高楼大厦厅。
梁上叠梁斗叠斗，红油栏杆雕花名。
宫庙寺宇造古董，亭台楼阁八角井。

丈杆或称制尺，在上面划定整幢房子的全部大小尺寸。它相当建筑设计图，工匠依靠它能造出双退住宅、宫庙寺宇和亭台楼阁各种类型和形制的房屋，包括相当复杂的斗拱。不过以造"古董"为能，则是农业社会中的保守心理，反映出生活的停滞和小农眼光的狭隘。

有一首长长的歌谣详细描述了房屋的兴建过程和工匠的劳作：

深山采来沉香木，鲁班祖师造新厅。
择定黄道吉庆日，起木发兴做不停。
大木老司来做工，画好图样定屋形。
石匠老司定磉石，阴阳定向遇吉星。
清吉良辰来拼木，多少功夫利排成。
黄道吉日开柱眼，竹匠柱头箍得紧。
竖柱喜遇黄道日，上梁巧逢紫微星。
梁上重梁斗叠斗，四面花窗映花明。
屋顶盖落滚椽瓦，地砌玉砖斗七星。
四面搭起禽兽头，墙头嵌镜发光明。
九曲游廊团圆走，平池着板大和珍。
玲珑花窗腾落阔，窗下书桌摆现成。
前后镇落对门，开门关门凤凰声。
前有亭栽栖凤竹，后有池养化龙鱼。
兴造房屋关风水，财聚小康振家声。

这首歌谣值得注意的两点是：一、明说木匠老司"画好图样定屋形"；二、明说石匠老司"阴阳定向遇吉星"，这工作是在"定磉石"的时候做的。看来，石匠老师在单幢房屋范围里掌管着风水，可能是遵照《鲁班经》里的一些规矩，因为前面说："鲁班祖师造新厅。"《三十六行歌》开篇唱："鲁班祖师是亲师父，传授老司手艺精。"

这首歌谣也表达了乡人们对建筑的审美理想和对匠人技艺的称赞。
sections.content_en:
4. Role of Craftsmen

Nanxi River's architectural craftsman system and their traditional design, calculation, construction methods and related folk customs can no longer be verified. However, inferring from long-term small-scale peasant natural economy society, craftsmen's specialization degree was not high; they did not form economic entities, transmitted through father-son and master-apprentice, with some trade customs — roughly conforming to reality.

Craftsmen were mostly not scholars or wealthy, nor could they assist in good deeds and charity, so they were not recorded in genealogies. Occasionally a few, due to contributions to construction and outstanding character, earned a few lines of ink. For example, "Liangyuan Chen Clan Genealogy" records a Ming craftsman: "Youfu Gong, courtesy name Youru, hao Lanxuan, ingenious beyond compare, skilled in building pavilions and towers. Poor, unable to study, yet understood great principles. In Wuzi year, when building Wenguang Gong ancestral hall, he used original craftsmanship, not sparing hardship." Another, also Ming, in "Tanxia Chen Clan Genealogy": "Named Shishang, courtesy name Zhaolin. Gentle demeanor, harmonious with all. From youth learned Lu Ban (master carpenter) trade, specialized in it, assessing materials and measuring timber, appropriately proportioned. Therefore near and far building new mansions all entrusted to him. To this day successors continue, family gradually stable, yet he knew to respect clan and ancestors, whenever righteous undertakings, spared no effort." From "original craftsmanship" and "assessing materials and measuring timber," these two craftsmen were master builders who also served as designers.

Due to father-son and master-apprentice transmission, various construction trades had specialized villages. For example: "Great carpenters come from Luokeng, stone masons from Zhongbao, tile kilns from Jingren, plasterers from Lüzhang."

Although there were specialized villages, craftsmen's specialization degree was still not high. Great carpenters also made beds, cabinets, desks, qin stools, even looms and windmills; plasterers also built cooking stoves; stone masons also made mortars, millstones, stone pillars, memorial archways, various stone implements, even carved inscriptions. Wall masons' trade was especially diverse: building stone arch bridges, paving roads, building stepping-stones, piling city walls, digging tunnels, laying field banks etc. What most brought these craftsmen's skills to full play was making various decorations. Plasterers modeled birds and beasts, figures and landscapes, lions and qilin. "Piling dragon looks exactly like dragon, modeling phoenix looks like phoenix soaring." Stone masons carved these subjects, and also "hollowed out lion holding ball." Wall masons used cobblestones to inlay various patterns on ground, called "inserted stone flowers."

About these crafts, Nanxi River has ballads chanting them. What literate genealogies did not record, folk culture passed down generation after generation. Folk culture is basically the culture of laborers. A ballad "Great Carpenter" goes:

Great carpenter's skill exquisite, hand holding measuring rod clear.
Square and ink line accurate, ink marking beams and pillars precise.
Double-retreat great house with side wings, can build tall buildings and halls.
Beams stacked on beams, brackets on brackets, red oil railings carved with flower names.
Palaces, temples, monasteries built antique, pavilions, towers, octagonal wells.

The measuring rod, or ruler, marked all dimensions of the entire house. It相当于 architectural design drawing; craftsmen relied on it to build double-retreat residences, palaces, temples, monasteries, pavilions and towers of various types and forms, including fairly complex bracket sets. However, taking ability to build "antiques" as excellence reflects conservative psychology in agricultural society, showing stagnation of life and narrowness of small-farmer outlook.

A long ballad details house construction process and craftsmen's labor:

From deep mountains gathered aloeswood, Lu Ban ancestor builds new hall.
Selected auspicious day, timber raised and work never stops.
Great carpenter comes to work, draws good design, sets house form.
Stone mason sets foundation stones, yin-yang orientation meets lucky star.
On auspicious morning assemble timber, how much effort arranged.
Auspicious day open mortises, bamboo craftsman tightens column hoops.
Erecting columns meets auspicious day, raising beam encounters Purple Star.
Beams stacked on beams, brackets on brackets, four-sided lattice windows reflect flowers.
Roof covered with rolling rafters and tiles, floor paved jade bricks in Seven Stars pattern.
Four sides set beast and bird heads, wall embedded mirrors shine bright.
Nine-bend winding corridors circular walk, flat pool with boards precious.
Exquisite lattice windows spacious, desk under window ready.
Front and back settle facing doors, opening closing doors sounds phoenix.
Front has pavilion planting phoenix-perching bamboo, back has pool raising dragon-transforming fish.
Building house concerns fengshui, wealth gathers, moderate prosperity elevates family name.

Two points worth noting in this ballad: first, explicitly says carpenter "draws good design, sets house form"; second, explicitly says stone mason "yin-yang orientation meets lucky star," this work done when "setting foundation stones." It seems stone mason, within single house scope, managed fengshui, possibly following rules in "Lu Ban Jing" (Lu Ban Classic), because earlier it says: "Lu Ban ancestor builds new hall." "Thirty-six Trades Song" opens: "Lu Ban ancestor is true master, transmitting craftsmen's exquisite skill."

This ballad also expresses villagers' aesthetic ideals for architecture and praise for craftsmen's skills.

sections.name: 选址
sections.content_zh:
1. 选址

楠溪江中游古村落的建设大都经过完整的规划。建设得比较早，并且把早期的规划基本保存到现在的，有苍坡村、塘湾村、芙蓉村和岩头村等。苍坡于955年建村，从北宋至和二年（1055年）起，重要的建设《苍坡李氏宗谱》都有记载，包括南宋淳熙五年（1178年）的一次全面的规划。这些记载的情况与苍坡村的现状大体符合，水系、主街和公共建筑一一都在。例如淳熙五年九世祖李嵩在村东南筑坝蓄水形成东池、西池。李嵩死后，夫人楼溪刘氏继续完成了寨墙、笔街和寨门，并挖了环泮水渠。塘湾村始建于宋代，《棠川（按即塘湾）郑氏宗谱》里有一则资料，提到绍兴年间的前街、中街，它们至今还是塘湾村的主要街道。芙蓉村也初建于宋代，南宋末因抗元而被完全焚毁，元至正元年（1341年）重建，大体保持了原来的格局。岩头村的规划在明代中叶，清代中叶被大规模破坏，但原状还可以追迹，它的水系和园林绿地在楠溪江村落里是成就最高的。

虽然没有文献资料，从现状看，规划的主要内容包括选址、水系(沟洫渠道、池塘、井)、布局（街巷网、功能分区、公共中心、园林绿地）、防御系统（寨墙、溪门、谯亭）等。这些规划内容的一部分项目，在其他地区的村落里也可能见到，但全面综合地实施它们，而且如此整齐，在其他地区就很少见，因而成为当今楠溪江村落的重要特色。

至于局部地保存下来的规划建设就几乎村村都有了。

楠溪江的村落，在建村之初，都很重视选址。选址的主要考虑，是自给自足的自然经济之下的农业生产和生活。影响生产和生活的基本元素是水、地、山。附会水、地、山对居民凶吉祸福关系的堪舆风水之说相当活跃。

楠溪江人对生存环境的认识是很全面而有综合性的。《渠川叶氏宗谱·重合族谱牒告成附书于后》写道：

渠口，吾祖光宗公发祥之所也。阅世三十有三，历年千百有馀。围绕者数百家，沿缘者七八里。凤山翥其西，雷峰峙其东，南有屿山，而其外有大溪环之。中穿一渠，可以灌田。而其北则层峦叠翠，不一其状。有径可通四处，田高下横逵，布列如画挂然。泉流涓涓，声与耳谋。地僻非僻，山贫不贫。有檀可采，有秫可种，有美可茹，有鲜可食。桑麻蔽野，禾稼连畦。迕笋地而挑衣，趋茶天而焙牛，民赖其利益已久矣！（道光二十年三十一世裔孙举东志）

这一段描写，写到山川形势、交通、水利、农业、林业和渔业。《荀子·强国》里说："其固塞险，形势便，山林川谷美，天材之利多，是形胜也。"渠口正是这样一个形胜之地，它现在是楠溪江中游的大村之一。

（1）村落选址的第一个考虑是要有足够的可耕地，使农产可以自给。正如《管子·度地》所说："圣人之处国者，必于不倾之地而择其形之肥饶者，……乃以其天材，地之所生，利养其人，以育六畜。"

堪舆名著《雪心赋》说到"发福之大居"应是"明堂平旷，万象森罗，众水归朝，诸山聚会，草盛木繁，水深土厚"，也是这个意思。

楠溪江中游的村落，大多分布在河谷冲积平地上。这里土层肥沃，水源丰沛，交通便利，农业生产的条件最好。两侧的山坡，又可以育薪炭林和果木林。条件尤其好的是地形比较开阔的盆地，其中最大的是以岩头村为中心的盆地，这个盆地里村落最多、最密、规模也比较大。除了岩头村之外，重要的有苍坡村、霞美村、周宅村、港头村、渡头村、芙蓉村、溪南村和枫林村等等，都是楠溪江人文最发达的村落。它们的主姓从福建迁来，建村比较早，而且经济、文化一直处于领先地位。其他几个人文发达的大村落，也大多位于小盆地中心，如花坛村、溪口村、桐州村、渠口村、豫章村等等。《珍川朱氏合族副谱》里有一篇《伯清公珍川十咏序》，描写花坛村的环境道：

陵阜夹川，陂陀下弛，衍为原隰。林麓蔽荫，水田环绕，居民耕植其中，熙熙如也。……是盖乾坤清澈之气所锺聚融结，必有玮瑰俊秀杰出乎其间。

由于水土好，有利于农业经济的发展，就能培育出人才来。花坛村确实是个人才辈出的地方，尤其在明代。

宽敞的盆地里，村落大多占用平地，形态集中而且方正。狭窄的河谷平川里，村落大多傍山坡建造，让出宝贵的耕地。而且村落规模不大，顺等高线呈带形。例如蓬溪村、埭头村和水云村。水云村的谷地稍稍宽一点，以致《大岩岩志》说它："村民多集于溪西大岩若北马鞍山麓，土地平旷，山泉下注，涧别渠分，阡陌交通。屋舍比连，安居乐业者二百馀户，大小宗祠檐垣相望也。"

有少数村落，例如周宅村，它北侧的渡头村和南侧的港头村，为了让出耕地，造在河滩上。它们相接呈带形，甚至与南侧的方巷村连接了起来，长度在两公里以上。

有一些沿江村落很少农田，就靠发展手工业，如西岸村，位于一座小山和江流之间，村民以制作粉干，运销温州，辅助收入。还有一些则做木工、烧窑、使船等。

（2）村落选址的第二个考虑是避水害，抗洪排涝。楠溪江流域年年夏季都有台风暴雨。每逢暴雨，江水骤涨，奔腾咆哮，摧毁力极强。康熙年间的一次大水，就把豫章村临江的"外宅"部分一冲而光，至今还是一个积沙的高地。

为了防洪，除了要有足够的高程之外，弯弯曲曲的江流两岸，村落大都造在沉积岸一侧而避开冲刷岸。按照堪舆风水的说法，就是村落前面要有"腰带水"，不可以有"反弓水"。堪舆书《山龙语类》说："反背水，形如反弓，一名反跳水。此水漏泄堂气，无情之水也。"相传为刘基著的《堪舆漫兴》里写道："金城弯曲抱身，如如月弓产凤麟；若是反弓不揖冢，石崇富豪亦须贫。"金城水也叫玉带水或腰带水。《阳宅十书》说："门前若有玉带水，高官必定容易起；出入代代读书声，荣显富贵耀门闾。"鹤湾、鹤垟、鹤盛、东皋、枫林、西岸、桐州、碧莲、豫章、花坛、廊下等等许多大一点的村子都处于"腰带水"的位置。蓬溪村虽然北面对鹤盛溪的反弓，但迎着反弓的是霞港头坚硬高耸的石壁，而一条不大的小溪却在蓬溪村的东面形成腰带，并且潴而成大约2000平方米的一个湖，在风水上正好是"水聚天心"，大吉。芙蓉村在南宋时候曾经出过十八位高级京官，村人至今津津乐道那"十八金带"，归因于芙蓉村的"前横腰带水，后枕纱帽岩，三龙捧珠，四水归心。"芙蓉村陈氏大宗祠里有一副楹联，写的是：

地枕三崖崖吐名花明昭万古；
门临象水水生秀气荣荫千秋。

说的就是这个风水。

关于沉积岸和冲刷岸影响村落安危的认识，就这样被风水迷信吞没了。风水师说"腰带水"有情，仅仅从它的环抱姿态引申而来，幸好没有违背常识的判断。

因为楠溪江流域多火山流纹岩，质地坚硬，有的地段，"反弓水"对江岸的冲刷危险不大，所以仍有一些村落造在"反弓水"的位置。至于风水上的凶煞，可以用一些办法来"破除"，例如，迎着"反弓水"造一座关帝庙就足以"逢凶化吉"了。蓬溪村面对鹤盛溪的"反弓水"，就是这样处理的。关帝是"伏魔大帝"，是"恩主公"，能够镇辟一切灾祸。

村落造在沉积岸，除了可以减弱洪水对地基的冲刷之外，"腰带水"还能够形成一个村落的自然边界，从而造成领域感。领域感会加强村落居民的内聚倾向，这对于血缘村落来说是很重要的。自然边界也有利于减少邻村之间的纠纷。

（3）选址的第三个重要考虑是安全。这是因为，许多村落的始迁祖都是为了避乱才来到楠溪江的，而楠溪江又并非世外桃源。例如，下园村的始祖为避晚唐黄巢之乱而来；苍坡、枫林、溪口、芙蓉等不少村落的始祖为避五代末年闽国王延钧之乱而来；渠口村始祖在北宋末为避方腊之乱而来；豫章村始祖是随宋室南渡辗转经江西而来的。他们饱经离乱，千里颠簸，来到楠溪江，为的是找一块平静的土地，休养生息。所以，他们时常钟情于闭塞的环境，或者易守难攻的环境。

一个例子是蓬溪村。它四面被高山峻岭包围，只在北面有个小小口子却又被鹤盛溪阻隔。要进入这个袋形谷地，唯一的路是架设在溪边悬崖峭壁上的栈道。

坦下村和塘湾村是另一类例子。它们三面环山，山势陡峭，不能通行。另一面不宽，筑起高峻的寨墙，很利于防守。为了选择这个地形，竟不顾村子的朝向，以致坦下村的住宅都朝西南而塘湾村的住宅绝大多数朝东北，虽然两村隔岸相望。

还有一些村子，背山面水，只有踏过长长的石矶步，才能到达寨门。例如廊下村、东皋村、白岩村、鹤垟村等等。西岸村造在山之东、水之西，山水合围，加上一段寨墙，唯一的寨门开在山的南麓，形势十分险固。

选择这种闭塞的，或易守难攻的环境建村，固然是为了安全，但有时也是为了遁世深隐。花坛村的始祖祖操隐公，南宋时在永嘉任县尉，《珍川朱氏宗谱·始祖操隐翁朱公墓志》说他：

见世荒乱，民多聚盗，弃官不仕，家于温。初居城东花柳塘。初欲隐，但目击理乱，关心竟不能释。再迁罗浮，而大乱扣城。对其子曰："此不足以隐吾迹矣！"东观西望，乃定居于清通乡之珍川。其地山明水秀，禽鸟和鸣，林深谷邃，景物幽清。乃置功名于度外，付理乱于不闻。

后来果然"陶然林下"，过着桃花源里的生活。

有些村落位于开阔地上，没有天险可守，就只好全仗筑墙了，例如芙蓉村、岩坦村。

正是由于村落整体的设防，才使村落内部房屋能够开敞外向，一片太平景象。这是血缘村落的特点之一。

（4）选址的第四个重要考虑是要有良好的小气候。楠溪江各地的小气候，因为地形多变，差别很大，因此，村落选址的时候，就要选择比较有利的小气候。相传为金丞相兀钦仄注的《青鸟先生葬经》说，理想的居住环境应该是"草木郁茂，吉气相随。……或本来空缺通风，今有草木郁茂，遮其不足，不觉空缺。故生气自然，草木充塞，又自人为"。说的是好的小气候有利于草木生长，草木生长又能改善小气候，当然有利于农业生产和居民的日常生活。

鹤垟村的始祖谢氏洗五五公，从郡城迁来楠溪江塘下村，有一天，"雪后登山，望见兰台山前积雪先融，遂定居焉，后果蕃昌"（见《鹤垟谢氏宗谱》）。鹤垟村在一个被"腰带水"紧紧从三面抱住的向阳山坡上，前有"鹤溪漾碧"，后有"锦屏叠翠"，土地高燥，光照充足，所以"积雪先融"。

渠口村的发展也是适应了当地的小气候。村子的东、西、北三面有山环抱，挡住冬季的寒风。南面不远处有一座小山，比较低矮，在东南和西南形成两个豁口。一到夏季，季候风沿楠溪江干流北上，一部分到坦下村顺小楠溪河谷折向西北，正好吹进东南豁口。所以渠口村向西发展，迎着季候风，而在东部植林，因为这位置吹不到季候风，却正迎着西晒太阳的炙烤。

隔小楠溪相对的坦下村和塘湾村相距不远，一朝西南而一朝东北，朝西南的坦下村固然有"三阳"高照，朝东北的塘湾村，则因为在漫长而燠热的夏季可以有季候风而补偿了阳光不足的缺憾。

（5）村落选址的第五个重要考虑是风景优美。溪口戴氏大宗祠的门联，有一副：

水秀山明常出仁智；地灵人杰永传声名。

好山水就是好风水，好风水就出好子弟。

楠溪江本来就以风景之美著称，几乎处处都有好景致。从谢灵运、陶弘景以来，楠溪江人的环境意识很强，山水情怀成为地方的文化传统。宋、明两朝，楠溪江中游许多村落文风极盛，受过较高文化教养的乡村士绅们，对自然之美有很敏锐的感受力，科名之余，他们流连于秀水明山之间，吟咏不辍。这种文化氛围，当然影响到他们对村落的选址。

例如一座芙蓉峰，有三块高耸峭拔的悬崖，就有下园村、芙蓉村、岩头村、溪南村都拿它做建村的地标，拿它做乡里风光的借景。《岩头金氏宗谱》记载，岩头村始迁祖安福公（生宋淳祐庚戌，卒元延祐戊午，1250-1318年）"始居西巷，……延祐间来相芙蓉三岩之胜，遂居焉。"又例如塘湾，也是因为风景优美而被郑氏始祖迁祖选中的。《棠川郑氏宗谱·重修棠川郑氏宗谱序》记载，始迁祖"至其地，见夫奇峰突兀，怪石峥嵘，面临雷璧，背枕天岩。九峰围屏，共巽山而拱秀；双溪环带，合曲涧而流芬。福地奚多让乎？"于是在这里建村定居。

各个村落的宗谱里，都有非常夸饰的文字盛赞本村风景的奇特和秀美，字里行间，洋溢着对乡里的浓烈感情。《蓬溪谢氏宗谱·同治甲子（1864年）重修族谱序》描绘山川形胜道：

楠溪形胜，惟蓬川最奇。迎逆流四十馀里，过棠洄荡漾，潴而后泄。守水口者，则有若狮、象、龟、鱼，突怒峭竖，险恶畏人。又有文笔峰撑寿星岩，镇屏山对列赢屿。横墙诸峰如观音坐莲、美女梳妆、鹰捕蛇、狮捉象。仰天湖、瀑布泉、将军、仙人、牛鼻、虎头、燕巢、鸡冠等胜，亦皆秀异可观。余足迹所及，历数之，未有过于此者也。
sections.content_en:
1. Site Selection

Most ancient villages in middle Nanxi River were built with complete planning. Those built relatively early and whose early planning is basically preserved to this day include Cangpo, Tangwan, Furong and Yantou villages. Cangpo was founded in 955; from Northern Song Zhihe second year (1055), important constructions are all recorded in "Cangpo Li Clan Genealogy," including a comprehensive planning in Southern Song Chunxi fifth year (1178). These records大体 match Cangpo Village's current state — water system, main street and public buildings all present. For example, in Chunxi fifth year, ninth-generation ancestor Li Song built a dam southeast of village to store water forming East Pool and West Pool. After Li Song's death, his wife Lady Liu of Louxi continued completing village wall, Brush Street and village gate, and dug the surrounding moat canal. Tangwan Village was founded in Song; "Tangchuan (i.e., Tangwan) Zheng Clan Genealogy" has a record mentioning Front Street and Middle Street from Shaoxing era, which remain Tangwan's main streets to this day. Furong Village was also first built in Song, completely burned in late Southern Song due to anti-Yuan resistance, rebuilt in Yuan Zhizheng first year (1341),大体 maintaining original layout. Yantou Village's planning was mid-Ming, massively damaged in mid-Qing, but original state can be traced; its water system and garden green space are the highest achievement among Nanxi River villages.

Although no documentary资料, from current state, main planning contents include site selection, water system (canals, channels, ponds, wells), layout (street network, functional zoning, public center, garden green space), defense system (village wall, stream gate, watchtower pavilion) etc. Some of these planning items may be seen in villages elsewhere, but comprehensively implementing them all, and so orderly, is rare elsewhere — thus becoming an important feature of today's Nanxi River villages.

As for partially preserved planning and construction, almost every village has it.

Nanxi River villages, at founding, all valued site selection highly. Main consideration for site selection was agricultural production and life under self-sufficient natural economy. Basic elements affecting production and life were water, land, mountains. Fengshui theories attaching auspicious/inauspicious relations to water, land and mountains were quite active.

Nanxi River people's understanding of living environment was comprehensive and integrated. "Quchuan Ye Clan Genealogy · Postscript to Recompiled Genealogy" writes:

Qukou is where our ancestor Guangzong Gong flourished. Thirty-three generations, over a thousand years. Surrounded by several hundred households, stretching seven-eight li. Feng Mountain soars west, Lei Peak stands east, south has Yushan, beyond which great stream encircles. A canal runs through, can irrigate fields. North has layered green peaks, varied forms. Paths connect all directions, fields high and low with horizontal roads, arranged like a painting. Springs flow gently, sound meets ear. Place remote yet not remote, mountains poor yet not poor. Has sandalwood to gather, glutinous millet to plant, delicacies to eat, fresh fish to consume. Mulberry and hemp cover fields, grain stretches continuous. Bamboo shoots in ground touch clothes, tea days roast cattle — people have long benefited from its advantages! (Daoguang twentieth year, thirty-first-generation descendant Judong zhi)

This passage describes mountain-river form, transportation, water conservancy, agriculture, forestry and fishery. "Xunzi · Strong State" says: "Its fortresses strategic, terrain favorable, mountains forests streams valleys beautiful, natural resources abundant — this is strategic terrain." Qukou is exactly such a strategic place; it is now one of the large villages in middle Nanxi River.

(1) First consideration for village site selection: sufficient arable land for self-sufficient agriculture. As "Guanzi · Land Measurement" says: "The sage establishing a state must choose level land and select fertile terrain... thus using natural resources, what the land produces, to benefit and nourish its people, to raise livestock."

Fengshui classic "Xuexin Fu" says "great fortune residence" should be "bright hall flat and open, all phenomena arrayed, all waters converge, all mountains gather, grass lush and trees dense, water deep and soil thick" — same meaning.

Middle Nanxi River villages are mostly distributed on river valley alluvial plains. Here soil fertile, water abundant, transportation convenient, agricultural conditions best. Hillsides on both sides can grow firewood forests and fruit forests. Especially favorable are relatively open basins; the largest is centered on Yantou Village — this basin has most, densest, and relatively large villages. Besides Yantou, important ones include Cangpo, Xiamei, Zhouzhai, Gangtou, Dutou, Furong, Xinan and Fenglin villages etc. — all are Nanxi River's most culturally developed villages. Their main surnames migrated from Fujian, founded relatively early, and economy and culture consistently led. Other culturally developed large villages also mostly located at small basin centers, such as Huatan, Xikou, Tongzhou, Qukou, Yuzhang villages etc. "Zhenchuan Zhu Clan Combined Genealogy" has "Preface to Boqing Gong's Zhenchuan Ten Poems" describing Huatan Village environment:

Hills flank the stream, slopes descend, spreading into marshy plains. Forests shade, paddy fields encircle, residents farm and plant within, prosperous and harmonious. ... This is where heaven and earth's clear qi gathers and congeals, surely there must be outstanding talents emerging among them.

Good water and soil, beneficial to agricultural economy development, can nurture talent. Huatan Village indeed was a place of talent, especially in Ming.

In spacious basins, villages mostly occupy flat land, form concentrated and square. In narrow river valleys, villages mostly built against hillsides, yielding precious farmland. And village scale not large, following contour lines in band form. Examples: Pengxi, Daitou and Shuiyun villages. Shuiyun Village's valley slightly wider, so "Daluo Rock Record" says: "Villagers mostly gather west of stream at north foot of Ma'an Mountain near Daluo Rock; land flat and open, mountain springs flow down, streams divide into canals, fields connected. Houses adjacent, over two hundred households living in peace and contentment, large and small ancestral halls visible to each other."

A few villages, e.g. Zhouzhai, with Dutou north and Gangtou south, to yield farmland, built on river beaches. They connect in band form, even linking with Fangxiang Village south, length over two kilometers.

Some riverside villages have little farmland, rely on developing handicrafts — e.g. Xi'an Village, between a small hill and river, villagers make rice noodles, sell to Wenzhou, supplementing income. Others do carpentry, fire kilns, operate boats etc.

(2) Second consideration for village site selection: avoiding water damage, flood control and drainage. Nanxi River basin has typhoon rains every summer. Whenever heavy rain, river surges, roaring and奔腾, extremely destructive. A great flood in Kangxi era completely washed away Yuzhang Village's riverside "outer estate" — to this day it is a sandbar highland.

For flood control, besides sufficient elevation, along winding river banks, villages mostly built on depositional banks while avoiding erosional banks. In fengshui terms: village front should have "belt water" (yaodai shui), not "reverse-bow water" (fangong shui). Fengshui book "Shanlong Yulei" says: "Reverse-back water, shaped like reverse bow, also called reverse-jump water. This water leaks hall qi, heartless water." Legendary Liu Ji's "Kanyu Manxing" writes: "Gold city curved embracing body, like moon bow produces phoenix and qilin; if reverse bow not bowing to tomb, even Shi Chong's wealth must become poor." Gold city water also called jade belt water or belt water. "Yangzhai Ten Books" says: "If before door there is jade belt water, high office surely easy to attain; generations going out and in hear reading sounds, glory and wealth shine on gate." Hewan, Heyang, Hesheng, Donggao, Fenglin, Xi'an, Tongzhou, Bilian, Yuzhang, Huatan, Langxia etc. — many larger villages are at "belt water" positions. Pengxi Village, though north faces Hesheng Stream's reverse bow, but facing reverse bow is Xiagangtou's hard towering cliff; while a small stream forms belt east of Pengxi Village, pooling into about 2,000 sqm lake — in fengshui exactly "water gathering at heart center," great fortune. Furong Village in Southern Song produced eighteen high-ranking capital officials; villagers to this day relish that "Eighteen Gold Belts," attributing to Furong's "front crossed by belt water, back resting on official-hat rock, three dragons embracing pearl, four waters converging at heart." Furong Chen clan main ancestral hall has a couplet:

Land rests on three cliffs, cliffs emit famous flowers shining through ages;
Gate faces elephant water, water gives birth to elegant qi nourishing generations.

This is exactly that fengshui.

Understanding of depositional and erosional banks affecting village safety was thus swallowed by fengshui superstition. Fengshui masters say "belt water" is affectionate, merely derived from its embracing posture — fortunately not contradicting common-sense judgment.

Because Nanxi River basin has much volcanic rhyolite, hard texture, in some sections "reverse-bow water" poses little bank erosion danger, so some villages still built at "reverse-bow water" positions. As for fengshui inauspiciousness, can use methods to "break" — e.g., building a Guandi Temple facing "reverse-bow water" suffices to "turn misfortune into fortune." Pengxi Village facing Hesheng Stream's "reverse-bow water" was handled this way. Guandi is "Demon-Subduing Great Emperor," "Grace Lord," able to suppress all disasters.

Villages built on depositional banks, besides reducing flood erosion of foundations, "belt water" also forms village's natural boundary, creating sense of territory. Territorial sense strengthens villagers' inward cohesion — very important for kinship villages. Natural boundaries also help reduce disputes between neighboring villages.

(3) Third important consideration for site selection: safety. This is because many villages' founding ancestors came to Nanxi River to escape chaos, and Nanxi River was not a Peach Blossom Spring. For example, Xiayuan Village's founding ancestor came escaping late Tang Huang Chao rebellion; Cangpo, Fenglin, Xikou, Furong and many other villages' founding ancestors came escaping late Five Dynasties Min Kingdom Wang Yanjun's chaos; Qukou Village founding ancestor came escaping Fang La rebellion in late Northern Song; Yuzhang Village founding ancestor came with Song court's southern migration,辗转 through Jiangxi. They experienced turmoil, traveled a thousand li颠簸, came to Nanxi River seeking peaceful land to recuperate. Therefore they often favored enclosed environments, or easily defendable environments.

One example: Pengxi Village. Surrounded on four sides by high mountains, only a small opening north blocked by Hesheng Stream. To enter this pouch-shaped valley, the only road was a plank road built on cliff by the stream.

Tanxia and Tangwan villages are another type. Surrounded by mountains on three sides, steep and impassable. The other side not wide, with high village wall built, very defensible. To choose this terrain, they even disregarded village orientation — so Tanxia residences all face southwest while Tangwan residences mostly face northeast, though the two villages face each other across the stream.

Some villages, back to mountain and facing water, only reachable by crossing long stone stepping-stones to village gate. E.g. Langxia, Donggao, Baiyan, Heyang villages etc. Xi'an Village built east of mountain, west of water, mountains and water encircling, plus a section of village wall, only village gate at south foot of mountain — position very strategic.

Choosing such enclosed or easily defendable environments for village building, of course for safety, but sometimes also for deep reclusion. Huatan Village's founding ancestor Cao Yin Weng, Southern Song county magistrate in Yongjia, "Zhenchuan Zhu Clan Genealogy · Epitaph of Founding Ancestor Cao Yin Weng Zhu Gong" says he:

Seeing world in chaos, people gathering as bandits, resigned office, settled in Wenzhou. Initially lived east of city at Hualiu Tang. Initially wanted reclusion, but witnessing order and chaos, heart could not let go. Moved again to Luofu, then great chaos struck city. Said to his son: "This cannot hide my traces!" Looking east and west, settled at Zhenchuan in Qingtong Township. Its land mountains bright and waters clear, birds sing in harmony, forests deep and valleys remote, scenery secluded and clear. Put fame and rank aside, ignored order and chaos.

Later indeed "contented under trees," living Peach Blossom Spring life.

Some villages on open land, no natural defense, had to rely entirely on walls — e.g. Furong, Yantan villages.

Precisely because villages were overall fortified, houses inside could be open and outward-facing, an atmosphere of peace. This is one feature of kinship villages.

(4) Fourth important consideration for site selection: good microclimate. Nanxi River's various microclimates, due to varied terrain, differ greatly; therefore when selecting village site, choose more favorable microclimate. Legendary "Qingniao Xiansheng Burial Classic" annotated by Jin Chancellor Wu Qinze says ideal living environment should be "plants lush, auspicious qi follows. ... Or originally open and ventilated, now plants lush, covering its deficiency, not feeling open. Thus life qi natural, plants filling, also by human effort." Good microclimate benefits plant growth, plant growth improves microclimate, of course beneficial to agricultural production and residents' daily life.

Heyang Village's founding ancestor Xie Xian Wuwu Gong moved from commandery city to Tangxia Village in Nanxi River; one day, "after snow, climbed mountain, saw snow at front of Lantai Mountain melt first, then settled there, later indeed prospered" (see "Heyang Xie Clan Genealogy"). Heyang Village is on a sunny slope tightly embraced on three sides by "belt water," front has "crane stream rippling green," back has "brocade screen layered green," land high and dry, ample sunlight — hence "snow melts first."

Qukou Village's development also adapted to local microclimate. East, west, north surrounded by mountains, blocking winter cold winds. South not far has a relatively low small hill, forming two gaps southeast and southwest. In summer, monsoon blows north along Nanxi River main stream; part reaches Tanxia Village, turns northwest along Minor Nanxi River valley, exactly blowing into southeast gap. Therefore Qukou Village developed westward, facing monsoon, while planted forests east — because that position gets no monsoon, but faces scorching western sun.

Tanxia and Tangwan villages facing each other across Minor Nanxi River, not far apart — one faces southwest, one northeast. Southwest-facing Tanxia of course has "three suns" shining; northeast-facing Tangwan, in long hot summer, gets monsoon compensating for insufficient sunlight.

(5) Fifth important consideration for village site selection: beautiful scenery. Xikou Dai clan main ancestral hall gate has a couplet:

Waters beautiful and mountains bright, always produce the benevolent and wise;
Land auspicious and people outstanding, forever transmit fame.

Good mountains and waters are good fengshui; good fengshui produces good descendants.

Nanxi River is already renowned for scenic beauty, almost everywhere has fine views. Since Xie Lingyun and Tao Hongjing, Nanxi River people have strong environmental awareness; landscape sentiment became local cultural tradition. In Song and Ming dynasties, many middle Nanxi River villages had flourishing literary culture; rural gentry with higher cultural education had keen sensitivity to natural beauty; between examination successes, they wandered among beautiful waters and mountains, chanting endlessly. This cultural atmosphere certainly influenced their village site selection.

For example, Furong Peak, with three towering sheer cliffs, had Xiayuan, Furong, Yantou, Xinan villages all using it as village landmark, as borrowed scenery for local scenery. "Yantou Jin Clan Genealogy" records Yantou founding ancestor Anfu Gong (born Song Chunyou Gengxu, died Yuan Yanyou Wuwu, 1250-1318) "initially lived West Lane... in Yanyou era came to assess Furong Three Rocks' beauty, then settled there." Another example: Tangwan, also selected by Zheng clan founding ancestor due to beautiful scenery. "Tangchuan Zheng Clan Genealogy · Preface to Rebuilding Tangchuan Zheng Clan Genealogy" records founding ancestor "arrived at that place, saw strange peaks towering, weird rocks jagged, front facing Thunder Cliff, back resting on Heaven Rock. Nine peaks enclose as screen, together with Xun Mountain presenting beauty; twin streams encircle as belt, joining winding ravine flowing fragrance. How could blessed land be inferior?" Thus built village and settled there.

Each village's genealogy has highly exaggerated text praising local scenery's strangeness and beauty, between lines brimming with strong affection for hometown. "Pengxi Xie Clan Genealogy · Tongzhi Jiazi (1864) Preface to Rebuilt Genealogy" describes mountain-river scenery:

Nanxi's scenic beauty, only Pengchuan most wondrous. Going upstream over forty li, passing Tanghui swirling, pooling then releasing. Guarding water mouth are lion, elephant, turtle, fish — suddenly rising sheer, sinister and daunting. Also Writing Brush Peak props Longevity Star Rock, Town Screen Mountain faces Ying Isle. Hengqiang peaks like Guanyin seated on lotus, beauty dressing, eagle catching snake, lion catching elephant. Yangtian Lake, Waterfall Spring, General, Immortal, Ox Nose, Tiger Head, Swallow Nest, Rooster Comb and other sights — all wonderfully beautiful. Wherever my feet have gone, counting them all, none surpass this.

sections.name: 水系
sections.content_zh:
2. 水系

村落的选址决定之后，规划与建设的起点就是兴修水系。

水是农业生产的命脉，在农业社会里，兴水利，除水害，是第一等的大事。所以治水的禹被尊为掌水的"大帝"，与掌天的尧，掌地的舜，合称为"三官大帝"。在楠溪江，田间村头，最多的就是三官庙，几乎到处都有。自古以来，治水也是地方官的首要任务之一，北宋王安石倡导的新政，就有一条"起堤堰，决陂塘，为水陆之利"。水也是村庄赖以生存的命脉。居民饮食要水，洗涤要水，农产品加工和家庭手工业要水，救援火灾也要水。水又是改善小气候、美化环境的必要因素。因此，和其他各地一样，楠溪江各村落的宗族组织和乡贤士绅，都把主持和资助水利建设当作一件经常性的善事来做。

农田水系和村落水系通常是统一规划的。对村落来说，水系的功能，一是供水，把水引进村子里，尽可能方便家家户户日常使用；二是排水，把生活污水、雨水和山洪导出村外。供水和排水都靠自流，所以，沟渠系统就成了村落规划的先决因素，它决定了村落的竖向设计，也就是决定了每幢房屋的相对标高，它也迫使村落必须有一定程度的规划。楠溪江流域夏季多暴雨，雨过之后，村子里没有积水，就是因为建设了合理的沟渠系统的缘故。芙蓉村的北部，内外两道寨墙之间，过去虽然有过几幢大宅，被毁于对岩头村的械斗，但大部分并没有造过房屋，然而却已有整齐的石子路和沟渠。它们证明，村子的建设，是先修筑道路和沟渠，然后才在它们界划出来的地块里造房子的。

楠溪江中游村落的水系，大致有两大类，一类是平川地的，一类是山坡地的。此外还有两类混合的和少数很特殊的。

（1）苍坡、芙蓉、岩头这些平地上的村落，街道和水系与农田相似。方整的街道网把村子大体均匀地界划成若干地块，沟渠沿主要街道流经全村。在农田里为种庄稼的地块，在村子里则建造房屋。《大岩岩志》说水云村的农田"道路修整，沟塍画然"。道路和沟塍的规划建设都依仗农民在农地里引水灌溉的经验。北宋时任永嘉太守的杨蟠则在一首咏永嘉的诗里说：

水如棋局分街陌，山似屏帏绕画楼。

村民们熟悉农田的自流灌溉，把建设农田沟塍系统的方法移植到村落规划中来，是很自然的事。二者在原则上是一样的。

风水师则在水渠的流向上有讲究，如苍坡、岩头和芙蓉三村，水渠都从西北进村，除芙蓉村的从正东出村外，另两村的都从东南出村。堪舆家认为，"凡地西北高东南下水流出辰巳问吉"（见宋·王洙：《地理新书》）。这三村的选址和相应的沟渠规划基本上是合乎这个吉祥的地形的。芙蓉村主渠出东门前，沿"演乐台"南侧曲折，这是避免"去水无情"，而要它多情地滞留一下。村民们把这曲折叫做"锁"，锁住"风"和"气"。

沟渠傍主要街道的一侧，宽度大小不等。最宽的是岩头村浚水街西侧的水渠，有2.7米左右，最窄的是芙蓉村如意街南侧的，只略宽于0.5米。苍坡村的笔街南侧，水渠宽约1米。因为村子里绝大多数的房屋朝同一个方向，所以，水渠通常流经房屋的后门或侧门，门内便是厨房，在有门口的地方，架上石板通行。

水渠边上隔不远便有一两步石级，也有横跨水渠的石板，用来供妇女们洗涤时当搓板用，或者放置桶、盆和衣物。沿着长街短巷，年轻的妇女们蹲踞在清清的沟渠边浣洗。孩子们绕着鹅兜嬉戏，乖巧的小姑娘也会拿一块帕子，学妈妈的样子在石板上揉搓。潺潺水声应和着笑语声，在街上回荡。柔和温暖的生活气息，漫溢在整个村落。也只有在这样的村落里，才会有"秋风催木叶，万户捣衣声"的诗境。

由于水渠同时也流泄各家的生活污水和雨水，所以以前村子都有村规，保护渠水的一定的清洁度。例如岩头村，每天日出之前不许洗衣洗菜，让各家把澄清了一夜的水打回家去作饮食用水；渠内不许放鹅鸭，不许洗沾有粪便的衣物，每年清理一次渠道；等等。虽然有这些规定，有些村子的村民们的饮食用水，仍多汲自水井。苍坡村水井比较多，至少有十三口。岩头村因为渠水量大流急，所以村民挑清晨的渠水饮食，村里没有水井。

许多村子里都有池塘，由水渠的水汇潴而成。除了供洗涤等日常用途之外，还更有防火的作用。由于水池比较开阔，在村子里造成空间的变化，又由于水池特有的美学品质，所以，它们常常成为村子里重要的环境因素。

芙蓉村中央，主要街道如意街的南侧，有芙蓉池，池中设一座芙蓉亭。枫林镇的中心，圣旨门对面，有圣旨门池，也是长方形的，池中造了一座亭子。

渠口村的池塘比较大，在村子前沿，北岸边也有一座长方形的凉亭造在水中。这些水池和亭子，都是村子最重要的休闲场所，尤其是老年人交流几十年友情的场所。有些水池成为公共园林的主要因素，例如溪口村、苍坡村和岩头村的水池，它们的面积都比较大。

以水池为主体的村子里的休闲中心和广阔的公共园林，是楠溪江村落最有特色的景观之一。

（2）塘湾、坦下、埭头、水云这些山坡上的村落，水系的规划与平地村子大不一样，它们的水系最重要的作用是泄山洪。主要的泄洪道大多是天然的冲沟，两岸人工衬砌加固。村子的规划，既要利用泄洪沟排水，又要防山洪的冲击。

山洪来也猛，去也疾，而且洪沟很深，所以不便日用，村子里一般不修沿街引水的水渠，街道上只有二三十厘米宽的排水沟，把雨水和污水送进洪沟。村民的用水，一靠筑池塘汇蓄，如塘湾和埭头；二靠凿井或挖泉源池，如坦下和塘湾；三靠用毛竹当输水管从山上引泉水到家，如水云、埭头、塘湾等村子。

蓬溪村所靠的山比较高、比较深，所以，除了山洪之外，还有常年不断的溪水。蓬溪村的水系，因而也是复合式的，既有山洪冲沟，也有沿主街道的水渠，而且水量丰沛，水流湍急，比较清洁。

除了上面两种水系之外，还有少量特殊的水系。

例如溪南村，它只有一条三五米宽的水渠，弯弯曲曲，反复来回盘绕，村里的房屋就顺势造在这九曲十八弯的水渠两侧。村民日常用水靠这条水渠，街巷里只有大约30厘米宽的排水沟，把雨水和下水排入这条大渠。沿渠有石级、石板、石桥，供妇女洗涤或取水时使用。岸边多种树木，因而这道水渠在村子里形成一条宽阔的绿化带，大大美化了村子的生活环境和改善了小气候。另外在它的卢氏大宗祠前面还有一口池塘，恰好倒映着芙蓉三峰。由于房屋造在弯曲的渠道两岸，所以朝向偏侧，各各不同。楠溪江中游盆地里的村子，房屋大多共朝一个方向，溪南村是个例外。不过它东部建房比较晚近，街巷修直，房舍整齐，与其他村落相似，居民用水靠南边的水渠。

另一个例子是西岸村。它造在一座小山的东坡，面临大楠溪而隔着一片乱石滩。山小没有水源，江滩太阔不便于日常取水，所以村民只好开凿几处大口井。大口井很特别，先挖一个面积很大的深坑，坑壁和坑底都用大块卵石衬砌，坑的平面如同一只瓠瓜，在"瓜"的尽头上宽阔处是储水的井，"瓜"的长柄渐窄处是下去的长台阶。这种水井因此就叫做瓠瓜井。掘井而饮，对整个村子的规划布局就没有多大的影响。
sections.content_en:
2. Water System
