Common practices:

First, random-stone wall. Built with unequal-size random stones. Some are upper section stones smaller, lower section stones larger.

Second, abrupt-change wall. Lower part uses large-uniform cobblestones, built to height about 1.20m, all change to uniform smaller cobblestones, no transition section.

Third, lower part is larger random-stone masonry, wall thick; top is oblong not very regular "人" (herringbone) pattern, thickness smaller; middle is transition of two; from bottom upward, random masonry gradually approaches "人" shape; this transition natural, ingenious, no trace, extremely refined, can be called divine product.

Nanxi River residence stone walls most characteristic, most大量, also most beautiful type is third.

Building cobblestone wall看似 easy, actually difficult. First use large rubble stones lay foundation; then divide inner-outer two skins masonry, each slightly backward-tilt; between two skins naturally mutually squeeze tight and stable. No mortar, plaster or other filler. Wall from bottom upward gradually thins, forming gentle curved batter; bottom projects much;造型 beautiful and appears very stable. Termination or corner, must use large rough stones to strengthen stability; for firmness, large stones' size two faces, i.e. header and stretcher alternately masonry.

Every rainy day, cobblestones' surface soil washed away, revealing stones' original colors: green-blue, persimmon-yellow, gray-white, shimmering with water, extremely gorgeous. Plum-rain season, stone walls also grow a layer fuzzy green moss; over time, wild vines and climbing figs also quietly climb stone walls. Some households also plant scallions and daylilies on wall tops; tender green with golden flowers brilliant as sunlight, making stone wall as if with life, with emotion.

(3) Bamboo-mat plaster wall. This wall uses bamboo strips woven into mat, fixed on beams, columns and keel tie beams; both sides plaster mud. This practice in general residences commonly used for gable walls; used for front-rear eaves also some. It cheap, materials convenient, easy construction, light and thin.

sections.name: 漏窗与漏墙
sections.content_zh:
5. 漏窗与漏墙

在砖石墙上开窗，形式与构造完全不同于木构架上的小木装修，成为漏窗。漏窗扩大，占了很大的墙面，就产生了漏墙。

（1）漏窗。在楠溪江中游村落里，砖石的围护墙上，为通风采光和装饰墙面而开的窗口，窗棂花式，或用整块石板精凿，或用花砖组合。各种各样的空透图案，朴素简洁，墙面显得生动活泼。漏窗花式数不胜数。有代表性且普遍的几种做法是：

回纹窗。以回纹为基本构图形式并常仿木窗的做法，在每个节点上刻出榫卯的插接线，有的还适当配上一些小花饰，是比较普遍的一种。

三角组合窗。用大小相等的砖条，砌成一个个等边三角形，再组成图案。

六边形组合窗。用砖组成一个个六边形格子，很似龟背纹。

十字矩形窗，以十字和矩形图案共同组成。节点上加梅花朵。

锦纹窗。用简单的几何图案构成，图案常有变化。如矩形纹，圆形纹。

玫瑰窗。这种花窗具有西洋装饰的味道，显然仿温州传来的天主教堂中的玫瑰窗。它常用在砖门楼正面顶上，或用在房屋的山墙部位。

有些漏窗用透雕的石板做花格。

漏窗既没有窗扇，也没有窗纱窗纸。正如唐代诗人皮日休的《石窗》诗所说：

苔染浑成绮，云漫便当纱。
棂中空吐月，扉际不扃霞。

晚近有在砖石花格后面加玻璃窗扇的。

（2）漏砖墙。又叫花墙，用专门烧制的异型花砖制成，楠溪江中游地区使用十分普遍，常用在住宅和祠堂的院墙砖门楼两侧八字墙上部。突出并美化建筑入口。质量比较高的大住宅，是十分讲究入口装饰处理的。也可在砖围墙上部形成一个极华丽的装饰带。少数的，面积较大，如花坛某宅、蓬溪村"近云山舍"院内隔墙，埭头某宗祠院墙，苍坡村的水月堂等。漏砖花墙种类很多，常见有回纹式，十字式、菱花式三种。

第一，回纹式，以回纹图案组成漏砖花墙。有单纯回纹式，也有掺入其他小装饰品的，如小小的花卉、树木、人物、动物、灯笼等砖雕，但主体回纹形式不变。

第二，十字式，薄砖组成空十字形、海棠角，有小小的装饰砖雕点缀。如芙蓉村"大宅"书塾墙面，岩头村某宅院墙。

第三，菱花式，这种花墙图案是用瓦片组合成的。使用不多，如水云村某宅。
sections.content_en:
5. Lattice Windows and Lattice Walls (Lou Chuang yu Lou Qiang)

Opening windows on brick-stone walls, form and construction completely different from small-timber joinery on timber frames, become lattice windows (lou chuang). Lattice window enlarged, occupying large wall surface, then produces lattice wall (lou qiang).

(1) Lattice windows. In Nanxi River middle villages, brick-stone enclosure walls, for ventilation-lighting and wall decoration opened windows; window mullion patterns, either use whole stone slab finely chiseled, or use decorative bricks combined. Various openwork patterns, plain-simple, wall surface appears lively. Lattice window patterns countless. Representative and common several practices:

Meander-window (hui wen chuang). Using meander as basic composition form and often imitates wooden window practice; at each node carves mortise-tenon insertion lines; some also appropriately match some small flower decorations; is relatively common type.

Triangle-combination window. Using equal-size brick strips, builds equilateral triangles one by one, then composes patterns.

Hexagon-combination window. Using bricks composes hexagon grids one by one, very like tortoise-shell pattern.

Cross-rectangle window, using cross and rectangle patterns jointly composed. Nodes add plum blossoms.

Brocade-pattern window. Using simple geometric patterns composed; patterns often vary. E.g. rectangle pattern, circle pattern.

Rose window. This decorative window has Western decorative flavor; obviously imitates rose window in Catholic church transmitted from Wenzhou. It commonly used on brick gate tower front top, or used on building gable wall position.

Some lattice windows use openwork-carved stone slabs as lattice.

Lattice window neither has window sash, nor window screen-paper. Just as Tang dynasty poet Pi Rixiu's "Stone Window" poem says:

Moss dyes entirely into brocade, clouds spread conveniently as gauze.
Mullions hollowly emit moon, door edge does not lock rosy clouds.

Recently some add glass window sashes behind brick-stone lattice.

(2) Lattice brick wall. Also called flower wall; made of specially fired special-shaped decorative bricks; Nanxi River middle region use very common; commonly used on residence and ancestral hall courtyard wall brick gate tower both sides splayed-wall upper part. Highlights and beautifies building entrance. Higher-quality large residences, very particular about entrance decoration treatment. Also can form an extremely gorgeous decorative band on brick enclosure wall upper part. Few, area larger, e.g. Huatan某 residence, Pengxi Village "Jinyun Shan She" courtyard partition wall, Daitou某 ancestral hall courtyard wall, Cangpo Village Shuiyue Hall etc. Lattice brick flower wall types many; common have meander style, cross style, rhombus-flower style three.

First, meander style, using meander pattern composes lattice brick flower wall. Has pure meander style, also has mixed other small decorations, e.g. tiny flowers, trees, figures, animals, lanterns etc. brick carvings, but main meander form unchanged.

Second, cross style, thin bricks compose hollow cross shape, begonia corners; has small decorative brick carving embellishments. E.g. Furong Village "Da Zhai" academy wall, Yantou Village某 residence courtyard wall.

Third, rhombus-flower style, this flower wall pattern is composed of tile pieces. Use not much, e.g. Shuiyun Village某 residence.

sections.name: 屋面做法
sections.content_zh:
6. 屋面做法

屋面除了它的实际功能外，还要表现风格，追求一种美。在铺瓦的过程中，可根据各种相关情况对大木构架的举折和生起略作调整，使建筑的屋面更加完整舒展。

（1）屋脊。屋脊是表现建筑精神的重要部分。屋脊做得好，能使建筑大大增色。楠溪江的公共建筑，如祠堂、庙宇、书院，正脊都做得简洁庄重，很少使用花哨的手法。脊端做成与屋脊曲线十分和谐的卷草，翘起，而反曲，完美有力。十分生动有生气。

岩头村进士牌楼是清代嘉靖年间金霞峰考取了进士后建造的，为了装饰和炫耀，做法就接近官式，但装饰题材有地方特色，如正脊正吻虽然做龙头形吻饰，两垂脊上却塑了两只鸡，乡土味十足。

在住宅中，屋脊做法也很简单，但脊的两端装饰性比较强，有的做很轻盈通透卷曲有致的花饰。到了晚期，砖门楼上的脊很华丽，不但有中国传统图案装饰，还融合有西洋风格的图案，如火焰纹，玫瑰纹等。也有在正脊中间做通透图形的。在脊头上，装饰物多为生活中常见的，乡土气息十分浓厚的题材，如花盆葵花、花盆万年青、鱼、鸡、狗等，令人见了耳目一新，很喜兴，但艺术上不很成熟。

（2）瓦面收头及檩椽头的保护。楠溪江地区建筑通常用25厘米×20厘米左右的板瓦，极个别建筑如牌楼才使用筒瓦，直接将瓦叠摞在椽子上面。

瓦垄上部靠近正脊处和下部靠近檐口处的瓦比较密，常压七露三，其他部位的瓦大都压一半露一半，这样就加强了举折的效果。悬山靠边收头处也一样，常叠压两三层瓦，这样，既加强了瓦顶的抗风能力，又使两端结束处逐渐增高，调整和完善屋面弧度，加强生起效果。

为不让椽头直接受日晒雨淋，檐口的滴水和瓦当都很大，一片紧挨一片，完全遮挡住椽头。滴水有长方铲形，25厘米×20厘米，有扁长形，10厘米×20厘米，有如意形，有如意铲形，还有正方形。滴水瓦上常有浅浮雕花纹，如福寿文字、蝙蝠、兽头、水波纹、卷草纹、万年青。雨水盛时，瓦面及滴水瓦上当长出绿色蒙蒙的青苔，十分苍古。

为保护椽头，还用一种很薄的方砖，一块块钉在椽头上，密接成整齐的一排，使椽头不受雨水侵袭。这种做法比起用大滴水瓦来效果好得多。也有用木板做护椽板的，木板易糟朽，效果不如砖的，但更换木板毕竟比更换椽子方便。悬山屋顶，一般都将檩子头露在山面上，很易腐烂，于是把瓦钉在檩头上，加以保护。檩头上有升头木，脊檩上除升头木外还有扶脊木，所以钉在檩头上的瓦比较大，脊檩上往往有上、下两块，将整个暴露的檩头、升头木、扶脊木挡好为止。
sections.content_en:
6. Roof Construction Practices (Wu Mian Zuo Fa)

Roof besides its practical function, also must express style, pursue a kind of beauty. In tile-laying process, can according to various related situations slightly adjust large-timber frame's ju-zhe and sheng-qi, making building roof more complete-elegant.

(1) Roof ridge. Roof ridge is important part expressing building spirit. Roof ridge done well, can greatly enhance building. Nanxi River public buildings, e.g. ancestral halls, temples, academies, main ridge all done simple-dignified, rarely use fancy methods. Ridge end made scrolling grass very harmonious with roof ridge curve, upturned, and reverse-curved, perfect-powerful. Very vivid-lively.

Yantou Village Jinshi Archway was built after Jin Xiafeng passed jinshi exam in Qing Jiajing era; for decoration and炫耀, practice close to official style, but decorative themes have local characteristics, e.g. main ridge zheng wen (ridge ornament) although made dragon-head form ornament, two vertical ridges却 molded two chickens, full of vernacular flavor.

In residences, roof ridge practice also very simple, but ridge both ends decorative relatively strong; some make very light-transparent curled elegant flower decorations. To late period, brick gate tower ridges very gorgeous; not only have Chinese traditional pattern decoration, also integrate Western-style patterns, e.g. flame pattern, rose pattern etc. Also some make transparent图形 in main ridge middle. On ridge ends, decorations mostly common in life, very strong vernacular atmosphere themes, e.g. flowerpot sunflower, flowerpot evergreen, fish, chicken, dog etc., making people see fresh, very festive, but artistically not very mature.

(2) Tile surface termination and purlin-rafter head protection. Nanxi River region buildings usually use about 25cm×20cm flat tiles (ban wa); extremely individual buildings such as archways才 use cylindrical tiles (tong wa), directly stack tiles on rafters.

Tile row upper part near main ridge and lower part near eave tiles relatively dense; often press seven expose three; other parts tiles mostly press half expose half; thus strengthens ju-zhe effect. Overhanging-gable edge termination also same; often stack two-three layers tiles; thus, both strengthens tile roof wind resistance, and makes both ends termination gradually rise, adjusting and perfecting roof arc, strengthening sheng-qi effect.

To not let rafter head directly sun-rain exposed, eave drip tiles (di shui) and tile-ends (wa dang) both very large; one next to one, completely遮挡 rafter heads. Drip tiles have rectangular-shovel shape, 25cm×20cm; have oblong shape, 10cm×20cm; have ruyi shape; have ruyi-shovel shape; also have square. Drip tiles often have low-relief flower patterns, e.g. fu-shou characters, bats, beast heads, water-wave pattern, scrolling-grass pattern, evergreen. When rain abundant, tile surface and drip tiles grow green fuzzy moss, very ancient.

To protect rafter heads, also use a very thin square brick, one by one nailed on rafter heads, closely joined into neat row, making rafter heads not rain attacked. This practice compared to using large drip tiles effect much better. Also some use wood boards as rafter-protection boards; wood boards easy rot, effect not as good as brick, but replacing wood boards after all more convenient than replacing rafters. Overhanging-gable roof, generally expose purlin heads on gable surface, very easy rot; then nail tiles on purlin heads, to protect. Purlin heads have sheng-tou-mu; ridge purlin besides sheng-tou-mu also has ridge-supporting timber; so tiles nailed on purlin heads relatively large; ridge purlin often has upper-lower two pieces, until entire exposed purlin head, sheng-tou-mu, ridge-supporting timber well blocked.

sections.name: 后记
sections.content_zh:
后记

这次楠溪江中游乡土建筑研究是在1990年10月至1991年12月之间进行的。这期间有调查，有测绘，有摄影，陆陆续续好几次。主持这次研究的是陈志华、楼庆西和李秋香，另外有十一位学生参加了测绘，他们是丘健、张旗、葛志红、何培基、莫军、杨哲怡、潘彤、刘晓梅、张葵、周榕和陈彤。陈志华主要负责研究的整体设计，撰写了本书的前言和第一、二、三篇。楼庆西主要负责摄影。李秋香主要负责测绘，并且撰写了本书的第四篇。研究生舒楠也参加了测绘。建筑学院资料室负责照片的管理和制作。

这次研究的全部经费由台湾龙虎文化基金会支付，由《汉声》杂志社编印出版。下决心放下手边熟悉了的工作，从头做乡土建筑研究，原因之一是急于抢救这些资料。大量珍贵的建筑遗产正在迅速毁灭，永远的失去，不给它们留下一份记录是不可原谅的错误。在研究过程之中，短短一年时间里，楠溪江的乡土建筑就继续破坏了不少。有些是因年久失修而倒塌，如构成坦下村美丽的轮廓的一栋住宅。有些是被拆除，以便在它们的基地上造新房子，如芙蓉村的一栋住宅。有些是遭到意外的灾害，如楠溪江唯一幸存下来的一座书院，被一场大火烧光了明伦堂。有些被改造成现代建筑，如岩头村丽水街上的老店面。更教人心焦如焚的，是有些建筑被热心的"保护"者修缮得面目全非，如苍坡村的东池上造了钢筋混泥土的"九曲桥"，仁济庙屋脊上塑起了两条五颜六色的游龙，张牙舞爪，与朴素淡雅的楠溪江村落格格不入。这本书里的有些测绘图和照片，刚刚完成，对象就已经没有了，或者彻底改变了。因此，保存了这些资料值得庆幸，而资料的不够全面，不够细致，又成了永远的遗憾。虽然楠溪江乡土建筑还有许多课题待做，但这一次的研究不得不结束了。这一次工作的收获之一是更深入、更真切地认识到了乡土建筑的研究非做不可，要快做，赶紧做，迫不得已地做，应该以很大的规模去做。这次工作的另一收获是，认识到了工作的一些难点。例如，乡土建筑大多数不能鉴定年代，不容易弄清村落的规划和建筑的变化过程，有时候是追索原状还是着眼于现状，也举棋难定。本书虽然还是着眼于现状，但详细写了第二章"耕读生活与山水情怀"和第三章"村落规划和建设的工作机制"，以探讨聚落和建筑形成的社会根由以及它们所反映的文化心理，但是，由于缺乏足够的文字资料，农村里又早已没有了了解过去生活的人，这两章写得不很充分。

还有一些通常认为很简单的技术，也成了难题，例如，这些用原木和蛮石建造的房屋，应该怎样制图，本书采用尺规制图，失去了它们粗犷的野性，而如实地画出弯弯曲曲的柱子、梁枋和卵石墙，又几乎是不可能的。采用折中的方法，徒手画直线，恐怕既得不到野性的神韵，又显得草率。以后的每一个课题，怎样捕捉它们各自的特色，大概也会是一个难点。希望在乡土建筑的研究中，每次都有所发现，有所发明，有所创造，有所前进，而不是停留在一个模式上。

1992年春
sections.content_en:
Postscript

This Nanxi River middle vernacular architecture research was conducted between October 1990 and December 1991. During this period there were investigations, surveys, photography, several times intermittently. Presiding over this research were Chen Zhihua, Lou Qingxi, and Li Qiuxiang; additionally eleven students participated in surveying: Qiu Jian, Zhang Qi, Ge Zhihong, He Peiji, Mo Jun, Yang Zheyi, Pan Tong, Liu Xiaomei, Zhang Kui, Zhou Rong, and Chen Tong. Chen Zhihua mainly responsible for overall research design, wrote book's preface and Parts One, Two, Three. Lou Qingxi mainly responsible for photography. Li Qiuxiang mainly responsible for surveying, and wrote book's Part Four. Graduate student Shu Nan also participated in surveying. Architecture School reference room responsible for photo management and production.

All funding for this research paid by Taiwan Longhu Cultural Foundation; published by "Echo" (Hansheng) Magazine. Determined to put aside familiar work at hand, to start vernacular architecture research from scratch, one reason was urgency to rescue these materials. Large amounts of precious architectural heritage are rapidly being destroyed, forever lost; not leaving a record for them is an unforgivable mistake. During research process, in just one year, Nanxi River vernacular architecture continued to be damaged considerably. Some collapsed due to long-neglected disrepair, e.g. a residence forming Tanxia Village's beautiful silhouette. Some were demolished to build new houses on their sites, e.g. a residence in Furong Village. Some suffered accidental disasters, e.g. Nanxi River's only surviving academy, its Minglun Hall burned down by a great fire. Some were transformed into modern buildings, e.g. old storefronts on Yantou Village Lishui Street. Even more heart-wrenching, some buildings were restored beyond recognition by enthusiastic "protectors", e.g. Cangpo Village's East Pond built a reinforced concrete "Nine-Bend Bridge"; Renji Temple roof ridge molded two colorful roaming dragons, baring fangs and brandishing claws, incompatible with plain-elegant Nanxi River villages. Some survey drawings and photos in this book, just completed, the objects already gone, or completely changed. Therefore, preserving these materials is fortunate, while materials not comprehensive enough, not detailed enough, became eternal regret. Although Nanxi River vernacular architecture still has many topics to do, this research had to end. One收获 of this work is more deeply, more truly recognizing that vernacular architecture research must be done, must be done quickly, urgently, necessarily, should be done on a large scale. Another收获 of this work is recognizing some difficulties of the work. E.g., vernacular architecture most cannot date; not easy to clarify village planning and building change process; sometimes whether to trace original state or focus on current state, also indecisive. This book although still focuses on current state, but detailed wrote Chapter Two "Farming-Study Life and Landscape Sentiment" and Chapter Three "Village Planning and Construction Work Mechanism", to explore social roots of settlement and architecture formation and cultural psychology they reflect, but, due to lack of sufficient written materials, and villages long ago no people who understand past life, these two chapters not written sufficiently.

Also some usually considered simple technologies, became difficult problems, e.g., these houses built with raw logs and rough stones, how should they be drawn; this book uses ruler-compass drawing, losing their rough wildness, while truthfully drawing crooked columns, beams-fang, and cobblestone walls, almost impossible. Using compromise method, freehand straight lines,恐怕 neither obtains wild charm, nor appears careless. Future each topic, how to capture their respective characteristics, probably also will be a difficulty. Hope in vernacular architecture research, each time have discoveries, inventions, creations, progress, rather than staying in one model.

Spring 1992
